items.title: Muhammad
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim al-Qurashī
items.description: Prophet of Islam and recipient of the Qur’an, whose preaching in Mecca and community-building in Medina established the foundations of Muslim faith, worship, law, and communal life. His sayings and example became the Sunnah, preserved through hadith literature.
items.works: The Qur’an (revelation, not a work authored by him); Prophetic hadith and sīra reports

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀmir al-Taymī, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq
items.description: Abū Bakr was the Prophet’s close companion and first caliph. He consolidated the early Muslim community after the Prophet’s death, suppressed the Ridda rebellions, and initiated campaigns that expanded beyond Arabia.
items.works: No book securely attributed to him; caliphal letters, sermons, and reports preserved in early chronicles

items.title: Uthman Dhu al-Nurayn
items.fullName: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī, Dhū al-Nūrayn
items.description: Third caliph and early convert, ʿUthmān oversaw the standardization and distribution of an authoritative written recension of the Qur’an. His rule also saw major territorial expansion and growing political opposition.
items.works: No independent book securely attributed; associated with the ʿUthmānic codex recension of the Qur’an

items.title: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf al-Zuhrī
items.description: A leading early Muslim merchant and Companion, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was among the earliest converts and one of the ten Companions traditionally promised Paradise. He was known for generosity and a prominent role in the early community.
items.works: No authored works securely known; reports of his hadith, charity, and public service

items.title: Umar al-Faruq
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Nufayl al-ʿAdawī, al-Fārūq
items.description: Second caliph, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb established durable administrative institutions, provincial governance, and the Hijrī calendar while overseeing rapid expansion into Syria, Iraq, Egypt, and Persia. He became a model of just rule in Islamic memory.
items.works: No authored book securely attributed; caliphal directives, judgments, and letters preserved in historical sources

items.title: Ubayy ibn Kab
items.fullName: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ibn Qays al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī
items.description: A Companion renowned for Qur’anic recitation and teaching, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb was counted among the leading early authorities on the Qur’an. Reports associate him with teaching recitation and preserving knowledge of revelation.
items.works: No independent authored work extant; Qur’anic readings and reports preserved in qirāʾāt and hadith sources

items.title: Abdullah ibn Masud
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd ibn Ghāfil al-Hudhalī
items.description: A Companion and major early Qur’an authority, Ibn Masʿūd helped establish the scholarly tradition of Kūfa. His recitation, legal judgments, and teaching influenced later Qur’anic exegesis and Ḥanafī legal thought.
items.works: No independent book securely extant; Qur’anic readings, tafsīr reports, and legal opinions transmitted by students

items.title: Uwais al-Qarani
items.fullName: Uways ibn ʿĀmir al-Qarnī al-Murādī
items.description: Uways al-Qaranī was a Yemen-born Muslim remembered in early ascetic tradition for devotion, sincerity, and filial piety. Though he did not meet the Prophet, later Sufi literature made him an emblem of spiritual intimacy and hidden sainthood.
items.works: No securely authenticated writings; sayings and devotional accounts preserved in early ascetic and Sufi literature

items.title: Ali ibn Abi Talib
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī
items.description: Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet, ʿAlī was the fourth caliph and a central figure in both Sunni and Shiʿi traditions. His sermons, judgments, and political career profoundly shaped Islamic theology, law, ethics, and debates over leadership.
items.works: Sermons and letters later collected in Nahj al-Balāgha (attribution and compilation debated); transmitted sayings and legal judgments

items.title: Abu Hurayra
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr al-Dawsī, known as Abū Hurayra
items.description: A Companion famed for transmitting a large number of Prophetic hadith, Abū Hurayra became a foundational source for Sunni hadith scholarship. His reports are prominent in the major canonical collections.
items.works: No authored book securely attributed; hadith reports in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and other collections

items.title: Alqama ibn Qays
items.fullName: ʿAlqama ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nakhaʿī
items.description: A leading Kūfan Successor and jurist, ʿAlqama studied with Ibn Masʿūd and transmitted his legal and Qur’anic learning. He was an important link in the scholarly tradition that helped shape early Iraqi jurisprudence.
items.works: No independent authored work extant; transmitted Qur’anic, legal, and hadith reports

items.title: Abd Allah ibn Umar
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-ʿAdawī
items.description: Son of the second caliph and a prominent Companion, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar was known for scrupulous adherence to the Prophet’s practice. His hadith and legal opinions became important sources for Sunni law.
items.works: No authored book securely attributed; hadith reports preserved in the canonical collections

items.title: Zayd ibn Thabit
items.fullName: Zayd ibn Thābit ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Anṣārī
items.description: A Companion expert in writing and recitation, Zayd ibn Thābit served as a scribe of revelation and played a central role in compiling the Qur’anic text under Abū Bakr and preparing the standard recension under ʿUthmān.
items.works: No independent authored work extant; associated with the early Qur’an compilation and transmitted legal/hadith reports

items.title: Abd Allah ibn Abbas
items.fullName: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī
items.description: A cousin of the Prophet and leading early exegete, Ibn ʿAbbās became known as the “interpreter of the Qur’an.” His explanations of revelation and legal opinions influenced tafsīr, hadith, and Islamic jurisprudence for centuries.
items.works: No authenticated authored book extant; tafsīr and hadith reports transmitted in later compilations

items.title: al-Hasan al-Basri
items.fullName: al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan Yasār al-Baṣrī
items.description: An influential Basran preacher, theologian, jurist, and ascetic of the Successor generation, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī shaped early discussions of piety, moral responsibility, and the relation between faith and action. His eloquence made him a model preacher.
items.works: Sayings and sermons preserved in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ and other adab/ascetic collections; no securely authored book survives

items.title: Said ibn al-Musayyib
items.fullName: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn al-Makhzūmī
items.description: A leading Medinan jurist among the Successors, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib was renowned for hadith, legal judgment, and knowledge of the Companions’ practice. He became a principal authority for the early Medinan legal tradition.
items.works: No independent book securely extant; legal opinions and hadith reports preserved in early fiqh and hadith collections

items.title: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr
items.fullName: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām al-Asadī
items.description: A Medinan jurist and hadith transmitter from the Quraysh, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr was a nephew of ʿĀʾisha and a key early source for reports about the Prophet’s life. His transmitted material helped shape the developing sīra tradition.
items.works: Early maghāzī/sīra reports preserved by later authors; no complete independent work survives

items.title: Salim ibn Abd Allah
items.fullName: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
items.description: A Medinan jurist of the Successor generation and grandson of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh was highly respected for learning and piety. His legal opinions helped preserve the Medinan school’s early traditions.
items.works: No independent book extant; hadith and legal opinions transmitted in Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ and other collections

items.title: Malik ibn Dinar
items.fullName: Mālik ibn Dīnār al-Baṣrī
items.description: Mālik ibn Dīnār was an early Basran ascetic celebrated for repentance, scrupulous piety, and powerful moral admonition. His sayings became part of the formative literature of Islamic zuhd and Sufism.
items.works: Ascetic sayings and anecdotes preserved in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ and other tazkiya works; no authenticated book

items.title: Zayn al-Abidin
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn
items.description: ʿAlī Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn, great-grandson of the Prophet, was an important figure in the Prophet’s family remembered for worship, learning, and moral refinement. Shiʿi tradition especially preserves his prayers and devotional teachings.
items.works: Al-Ṣaḥīfa al-Sajjādiyya (prayer collection attributed to him); Risālat al-ḥuqūq (attributed ethical treatise)

items.title: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad
items.fullName: al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Taymī
items.description: A Medinan jurist from the generation after the Companions and grandson of Abū Bakr, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad was one of the Seven Jurists of Medina. His learning helped transmit the legal practice later associated with Mālik’s school.
items.works: No independent authored work extant; legal opinions and reports preserved in early Medinan collections

items.title: Ibrahim al-Nakhai
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿī
items.description: A major Kūfan jurist among the Successors, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī transmitted the learning of ʿAlqama and Ibn Masʿūd. His legal reasoning became a principal foundation for the Iraqi tradition inherited by Ḥammād and Abū Ḥanīfa.
items.works: No authored book securely extant; legal opinions preserved in early Kūfan fiqh transmissions

items.title: Muhammad al-Baqir
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī, Muḥammad al-Bāqir
items.description: Muḥammad al-Bāqir, fifth Imam in Twelver Shiʿism and a descendant of the Prophet, was revered for religious knowledge and transmitted teachings in law, Qur’anic interpretation, and theology. His circle contributed to the scholarly legacy of the Prophet’s family.
items.works: No securely extant authored book; teachings and reports transmitted in early Imāmī hadith and biographical sources

items.title: Amr ibn Ubayd
items.fullName: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd ibn Bāb al-Tamīmī
items.description: A Basran theologian and ascetic associated with early Muʿtazilism, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd emphasized moral responsibility and rational theological inquiry. He was an important early figure in the formation of the Muʿtazilī school.
items.works: No complete authenticated work survives; theological positions preserved in heresiography and kalām sources

items.title: Abu Hanifa
items.fullName: al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit ibn Zūṭā al-Taymī, Abū Ḥanīfa
items.description: Abū Ḥanīfa was the eponymous founder of the Ḥanafī school, renowned for legal reasoning and the systematic use of analogy. His Iraqi circle helped develop a juristic method that became one of the world’s largest Sunni legal traditions.
items.works: Al-Fiqh al-akbar (attributed); al-ʿĀlim wa-l-mutaʿallim (attributed); legal doctrines transmitted by his students

items.title: Wasil ibn Ata'
items.fullName: Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-Ghazzāl
items.description: Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ is traditionally regarded as the founder of Muʿtazilism. He stressed divine unity, human moral responsibility, and reasoned theological argument, helping establish a distinct school of kalām in early Basra.
items.works: No complete securely preserved work; theological doctrines and epistles quoted in later kalām and heresiographical sources

items.title: Jafar al-Sadiq
items.fullName: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Hāshimī, al-Ṣādiq
items.description: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq, sixth Imam in Twelver Shiʿism and revered by Ismāʿīlīs, was a celebrated scholar whose transmitted teachings influenced Imāmī law and theology. Later Sunni and Sufi traditions also honored him as a learned authority.
items.works: No securely authenticated complete book; teachings attributed in al-Kāfī and other Imāmī hadith collections

items.title: al-Awzai
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr al-Awzāʿī
items.description: Al-Awzāʿī was a leading Syrian jurist whose legal school once rivaled the later four Sunni schools. His rulings on public law, warfare, and governance were influential, and his reputation for principled independence endured.
items.works: No independent book survives; legal opinions and correspondence preserved in early fiqh sources

items.title: Malik ibn Anas
items.fullName: Mālik ibn Anas ibn Mālik ibn Abī ʿĀmir al-Aṣbaḥī
items.description: Mālik ibn Anas founded the Mālikī school and became a preeminent authority on Medinan legal practice. His Muwaṭṭaʾ combines hadith, Companion reports, and legal judgments, making it one of the earliest major works of Islamic law.
items.works: Al-Muwaṭṭaʾ; legal opinions transmitted in the Mālikī tradition

items.title: Rabia al-Adawiyya
items.fullName: Rābiʿa bint Ismāʿīl al-ʿAdawiyya
items.description: Rābiʿa al-ʿAdawiyya was an early Basran woman ascetic whose devotional ideal of loving God for God’s own sake became central to later Sufi literature. Her life is surrounded by hagiographical accounts, so details require caution.
items.works: Poems, prayers, and sayings attributed in later Sufi biographies; no authenticated authored collection

items.title: Sufyan al-Thawri
items.fullName: Sufyān ibn Saʿīd ibn Masrūq al-Thawrī
items.description: Sufyān al-Thawrī was a major hadith scholar, jurist, and ascetic of Kūfa. His independent legal school later declined, but his hadith transmissions and model of scholarly independence remained influential.
items.works: Tafsīr and legal opinions transmitted under his name; no comprehensive work securely authored

items.title: Reign of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz
Ibrahim ibn Adham
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham al-Balkhī
items.description: Ibrāhīm ibn Adham was an early ascetic remembered for renouncing privilege and adopting a life of worship and austerity. His conversion narrative and teachings became influential exemplars in Sufi hagiography.
items.works: Ascetic sayings preserved in Sufi biographies; no authenticated independent work

items.title: al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi
items.fullName: al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr al-Farāhīdī
items.description: Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad al-Farāhīdī was a pioneering Arab philologist who systematized Arabic prosody and helped establish lexicography. His work on linguistic patterns deeply influenced Arabic grammar and literary scholarship.
items.works: Kitāb al-ʿAyn (attributed, earliest major Arabic dictionary); foundational treatises on Arabic prosody

items.title: Jabir ibn Hayyan
items.fullName: Jābir ibn Ḥayyān al-Azdī
items.description: Jābir ibn Ḥayyān became the legendary namesake of a vast Arabic alchemical corpus. The historical authorship of many works attributed to him is disputed; the Jabirian tradition nevertheless helped shape medieval alchemy and experimental chemical thought.
items.works: Jābirian corpus, including Kitāb al-Kīmiyāʾ and Kitāb al-Sabʿīn (authorship and dating debated)

items.title: Sufyan ibn Uyayna
items.fullName: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Hilālī
items.description: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna was a leading Meccan hadith scholar and jurist whose transmissions were widely used by later compilers. He was also known for Qur’anic interpretation and his role in the scholarly networks of the Ḥijāz.
items.works: Tafsīr and hadith transmissions preserved in later collections; no complete independent book securely survives

items.title: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak ibn Wāḍiḥ al-Ḥanẓalī al-Marwazī
items.description: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak was a renowned hadith scholar, jurist, ascetic, and frontier volunteer. He combined scholarship with ethical discipline, and his writings helped develop early Sunni ideas of piety and religious struggle.
items.works: Kitāb al-Zuhd wa-l-raqāʾiq; Kitāb al-Jihād; al-Musnad (transmitted collection)

items.title: Dirar ibn Amr
items.fullName: Ḍirār ibn ʿAmr al-Ghaṭafānī
items.description: Ḍirār ibn ʿAmr was an early rational theologian associated with formative debates between Muʿtazilīs and other kalām schools. His views on divine attributes, human action, and perception became reference points in later heresiography.
items.works: No complete work survives; theological positions preserved in later kalām and heresiographical reports

items.title: Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl
items.fullName: Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl al-ʿAnbarī
items.description: Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl was a prominent disciple of Abū Ḥanīfa and an influential early Ḥanafī jurist, remembered for his skill in analogical reasoning. His legal views were transmitted through the school rather than a surviving corpus.
items.works: No extant independent work; rulings and legal opinions preserved in Ḥanafī literature

items.title: Abu Yusuf
items.fullName: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm al-Anṣārī, Abū Yūsuf
items.description: Abū Yūsuf was a leading disciple of Abū Ḥanīfa and the first chief judge of the Abbasid caliphate. His legal works helped establish Ḥanafī jurisprudence as an influential tradition of state law and judicial practice.
items.works: Kitāb al-Kharāj; Ikhtilāf Abī Ḥanīfa wa-Ibn Abī Laylā; al-Āthār

items.title: al-Kisa'i
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Ḥamza al-Kisāʾī
items.description: Al-Kisāʾī was a leading grammarian and one of the canonical Qur’an readers. As a key figure in the Kūfan school of Arabic grammar, he helped develop its methods and served at the Abbasid court.
items.works: Qirāʾat al-Kisāʾī (canonical reading); grammatical teachings preserved by students

items.title: Abd al-Razzaq
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn Hammām al-Ṣanʿānī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī was an important Yemeni hadith scholar whose large compilations preserve early legal and exegetical material. His transmissions are especially valuable for reconstructing early Islamic traditions.
items.works: Al-Muṣannaf; Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq

items.title: Musa al-Kazim
items.fullName: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar al-Kāẓim
items.description: Mūsā al-Kāẓim, seventh Imam in Twelver Shiʿism, was revered for patience, devotion, and religious learning. His transmitted teachings became part of the Imāmī tradition and he is honored as an exemplar of spiritual restraint.
items.works: No securely authenticated authored book; sayings and hadith reports transmitted in Imāmī collections

items.title: Muhammad al-Shaybani
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Shaybānī
items.description: Muḥammad al-Shaybānī was a foundational Ḥanafī jurist and student of Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf. His systematic texts preserved and developed the school’s doctrines and influenced later Sunni jurisprudence, including legal theory and international law.
items.works: Al-Aṣl (al-Mabsūṭ); al-Jāmiʿ al-ṣaghīr; al-Jāmiʿ al-kabīr; al-Siyar al-kabīr

items.title: Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Hudhayl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAllāf
items.description: Abū al-Hudhayl al-ʿAllāf was a formative Muʿtazilī theologian of Basra who gave the school a more systematic account of divine unity, attributes, and human agency. His arguments shaped later rational theology.
items.works: No complete work survives; doctrines preserved in later Muʿtazilī and heresiographical sources

items.title: Maruf al-Karkhi
items.fullName: Maʿrūf ibn Fīrūz al-Karkhī
items.description: Maʿrūf al-Karkhī was an early Baghdad ascetic and Sufi revered for sincerity, renunciation, and spiritual influence. Later Sufi lineages frequently connect their chains of initiation to him.
items.works: Sayings and biographical traditions preserved in Sufi sources; no securely authenticated authored book

items.title: Sibawayh
items.fullName: ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Qanbar, known as Sībawayh
items.description: Sībawayh was the Persian-born grammarian whose Kitāb became the foundational systematic treatise of Arabic grammar. Its careful analysis of syntax and morphology shaped the Basran grammatical tradition and later Arabic linguistic scholarship.
items.works: Al-Kitāb (The Book), foundational treatise on Arabic grammar

items.title: al-Farra'
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād al-Farrāʾ
items.description: Al-Farrāʾ was a leading Kūfan grammarian and Qur’anic linguist at the Abbasid court. His analyses of Arabic syntax, dialect, and Qur’anic expressions remain foundational sources for the Kūfan grammatical tradition.
items.works: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān; al-Ḥudūd; linguistic works transmitted under his name

items.title: Abu Thawr
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid al-Kalbī, Abū Thawr
items.description: Abū Thawr was an early jurist who studied with al-Shāfiʿī and developed an independent legal school. His views are known through later biographical and legal literature, especially debates over hadith and legal reasoning.
items.works: No complete authenticated work survives; legal opinions preserved in fiqh sources

items.title: Ali al-Rida
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Mūsā al-Riḍā
items.description: ʿAlī al-Riḍā, eighth Imam in Twelver Shiʿism, was a descendant of the Prophet known for religious learning and theological disputation. His designation as heir by the Abbasid caliph al-Maʾmūn made him an important figure in Abbasid and Imāmī history.
items.works: No securely authenticated independent book; teachings attributed in Imāmī hadith and debate literature

items.title: al-Shafii
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī
items.description: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī founded the Shāfiʿī school and helped systematize legal theory by articulating the authority of Qur’an, Sunnah, consensus, and analogy. His writings profoundly shaped Sunni jurisprudence and uṣūl al-fiqh.
items.works: Al-Risāla; al-Umm; Ikhtilāf al-ḥadīth; Jamāʿ al-ʿilm

items.title: Bishr ibn al-Harith
items.fullName: Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥāfī
items.description: Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith, known as Bishr al-Ḥāfī, was a Baghdad ascetic whose repentance and strict personal ethics made him a celebrated early Sufi figure. His life was widely recounted as a model of sincerity and detachment.
items.works: Sayings preserved in Sufi biographical collections; no authenticated independent book

items.title: Yahya al-Laythi
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Laythī
items.description: Yaḥyā al-Laythī was a major Andalusian transmitter of Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ. His recension helped establish the Mālikī school in al-Andalus and became the principal version used in much of the western Islamic world.
items.works: Recension of Mālik’s al-Muwaṭṭaʾ

items.title: Yahya ibn Main
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn ibn ʿAwn al-Murī
items.description: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn was one of the foremost critics of hadith transmitters. His judgments on narrator reliability became a fundamental resource for the science of al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl and the evaluation of hadith chains.
items.works: Statements on narrators preserved in Tārīkh Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and later rijāl compilations

items.title: al-Nazzam
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Sayyār al-Naẓẓām
items.description: Al-Naẓẓām was an influential Muʿtazilī theologian known for original, sometimes controversial arguments about divine justice, causation, and the created world. His teachings were transmitted chiefly through reports by opponents and later theologians.
items.works: No complete work survives; doctrines preserved in kalām and heresiographical sources

items.title: al-Jahiz
items.fullName: ʿAmr ibn Baḥr al-Jāḥiẓ
items.description: Al-Jāḥiẓ was a celebrated Abbasid prose writer who combined adab, theology, natural observation, and social criticism with wit and stylistic brilliance. He became one of the most important architects of classical Arabic prose.
items.works: Kitāb al-Ḥayawān; al-Bayān wa-l-tabyīn; al-Bukhalāʾ; Risālat al-Tarbīʿ wa-l-Tadwīr

items.title: Sahnun
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Saʿīd al-Tanūkhī, Sahnūn
items.description: Saḥnūn was the leading jurist of early Ifrīqiya and a key architect of Mālikī law in North Africa. His legal transmission of Ibn al-Qāsim’s teachings became authoritative in the Maghrib and helped institutionalize the school.
items.works: Al-Mudawwana al-kubrā (compiled from legal transmissions and associated with his recension)

items.title: Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Abī Duʾād al-Iyādī
items.description: Aḥmad ibn Abī Duʾād was a prominent Muʿtazilī judge and Abbasid court official who played a central role in the miḥna, the inquisition over the createdness of the Qur’an. His career illustrates the political reach of theological disputes.
items.works: No independent authored work securely survives; theological positions and judicial role recorded in chronicles

items.title: Khalifa ibn Khayyat
items.fullName: Khalīfa ibn Khayyāṭ al-ʿUṣfurī
items.description: Khalīfa ibn Khayyāṭ was an early Muslim historian and hadith scholar whose concise chronicles are among the oldest surviving works of Islamic historiography. His biographical and chronological data are valuable sources for the first Islamic centuries.
items.works: Al-Tārīkh; al-Ṭabaqāt

items.title: Ali ibn al-Madini
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Madīnī
items.description: ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī was a leading hadith critic and teacher of al-Bukhārī, renowned for analyzing chains of transmission and identifying hidden defects in reports. His methods strongly influenced classical hadith criticism.
items.works: Al-ʿIlal; works on transmitters and hadith criticism (partly preserved through quotations and later transmission)

items.title: Ahmad ibn Hanbal
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal al-Shaybānī
items.description: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal founded the Ḥanbalī school and became a symbol of traditionalist scholarship after resisting the Abbasid miḥna. His vast hadith learning and insistence on scriptural authority shaped Sunni theology and law.
items.works: Al-Musnad; Kitāb al-Zuhd; al-Radd ʿalā al-Zanādiqa wa-l-Jahmiyya (attributed)

items.title: al-Muhasibi
items.fullName: al-Ḥārith ibn Asad al-Muḥāsibī
items.description: Al-Muḥāsibī was an early theologian and spiritual writer who developed a rigorous psychology of self-examination, intention, and accountability. His synthesis of Sunni doctrine and ascetic discipline influenced later Sufism, especially al-Ghazālī.
items.works: Al-Riʿāya li-ḥuqūq Allāh; Ādāb al-nufūs; al-Waṣāyā

items.title: Ibn Kullab
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd ibn Kullāb al-Qaṭṭān
items.description: Ibn Kullāb was an early Sunni theologian whose arguments about divine speech and attributes influenced the formation of later Ashʿarī kalām. He sought to defend traditional belief through rational disputation.
items.works: No complete works survive; views preserved in later kalām literature

items.title: al-Muzani
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl ibn Yaḥyā al-Muzanī
items.description: Al-Muzanī was a leading disciple of al-Shāfiʿī and an important transmitter of Shāfiʿī jurisprudence. His concise legal epitome became a standard introductory text in the school.
items.works: Mukhtaṣar al-Muzanī; Sharḥ al-Sunna (attributed/fragmentarily transmitted)

items.title: Dhu al-Nun al-Misri
items.fullName: Thawbān ibn Ibrāhīm al-Miṣrī, Dhū al-Nūn
items.description: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī was an early Egyptian Sufi associated with the articulation of maʿrifa, spiritual knowledge of God, and the language of mystical states. Later tradition also links him with allegorical interpretation and alchemical lore, though reports vary in reliability.
items.works: Sayings and prayers preserved in early Sufi sources; writings attributed to him are not securely established

items.title: al-Darimi
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Faḍl al-Dārimī
items.description: Al-Dārimī was a hadith scholar and traditionalist theologian whose collection preserves reports and early doctrinal positions. His work contributed to the development of Sunni hadith-based theology.
items.works: Sunan al-Dārimī (also known as al-Musnad); al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyya (attribution debated)

items.title: al-Kindi
items.fullName: Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Kindī
items.description: Al-Kindī was a pioneering philosopher of the Arabic tradition and a scholar of mathematics, medicine, music, and natural science. He helped introduce and adapt Greek philosophy for Arabic-speaking intellectual life under the Abbasids.
items.works: On First Philosophy; On the Intellect; De radiis (Latin transmission); treatises on optics, music, and medicine

items.title: Abu Yazid al-Bistami
items.fullName: Ṭayfūr ibn ʿĪsā ibn Ādam al-Bisṭāmī, Abū Yazīd
items.description: Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī was an influential Persian mystic remembered for ecstatic utterances and an intense language of divine love and self-annihilation. Though his sayings shaped later Sufi metaphysics, much of his biography comes through hagiographical transmission.
items.works: Ecstatic sayings preserved in Sufi works; no authenticated book by him survives

items.title: Muhammad ibn Karram
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Karrām al-Sijistānī
items.description: Muḥammad ibn Karrām founded the Karrāmiyya, a religious movement prominent in eastern Islamic lands. His ascetic preaching and distinctive theological positions became subjects of debate among later Sunni theologians.
items.works: No complete authentic work survives; doctrines reported in kalām and heresiographical sources

items.title: al-Bukhari
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bukhārī
items.description: Muḥammad al-Bukhārī was a preeminent hadith scholar whose stringent selection principles made his collection one of Sunni Islam’s most authoritative books after the Qur’an. His work shaped hadith criticism and religious education across the Muslim world.
items.works: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī; al-Adab al-mufrad; Khalq afʿāl al-ʿibād; al-Tārīkh al-kabīr

items.title: Ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-Mundhir al-Tamīmī al-Ḥanẓalī al-Rāzī, Ibn Abī Ḥātim
items.description: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī was a leading hadith critic and Qur’anic exegete who preserved detailed evaluations of transmitters and early scholarly disagreements. His works remain important for hadith authentication and tafsīr studies.
items.works: Al-Jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl; Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm; ʿIlal al-ḥadīth

items.title: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
items.fullName: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj ibn Muslim al-Qushayrī al-Naysābūrī
items.description: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj was a major hadith scholar whose Ṣaḥīḥ is one of the two most authoritative Sunni hadith collections. His careful arrangement and critical methods became a foundation of later hadith study.
items.works: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; al-Tamyīz; Kitāb al-Kunā wa-l-Asmāʾ

items.title: Dawud al-Zahiri
items.fullName: Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī al-Iṣbahānī al-Ẓāhirī
items.description: Dāwūd al-Ẓāhirī founded the Ẓāhirī legal school, emphasizing the apparent meaning of scriptural texts and rejecting speculative analogy. Though his school later diminished, its method influenced debates over legal interpretation.
items.works: No complete works securely survive; legal doctrines preserved in later works

items.title: al-Asamm
items.fullName: Abū Bakr ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaysān al-Aṣamm
items.description: Al-Aṣamm, usually identified as Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm, was an early Muʿtazilī theologian and Qur’an commentator known for rationalist interpretation. His views are preserved mainly through quotations and reports in later exegetical and theological literature.
items.works: No complete work survives; tafsīr and theological opinions quoted in later sources

items.title: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani
items.fullName: Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath al-Azdī al-Sijistānī, Abū Dāwūd
items.description: Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī was a leading hadith collector whose Sunan became one of the six canonical Sunni collections. He focused especially on reports relevant to law and provided a lasting resource for jurists.
items.works: Sunan Abī Dāwūd; al-Marāsīl; Kitāb al-Zuhd; Risāla ilā ahl Makka

items.title: Sahl al-Tustari
items.fullName: Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī
items.description: Sahl al-Tustarī was an early Qur’anic exegete and Sufi whose teachings emphasized sincerity, spiritual discipline, and the inner dimensions of revelation. His attributed commentary is among the earliest works associated with mystical tafsīr.
items.works: Tafsīr al-Tustarī (transmitted compilation); al-Masāʾil; sayings and teachings

items.title: al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Bashīr al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī
items.description: Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī was a seminal mystic and religious thinker who explored sainthood, spiritual psychology, and the concept of divine wisdom. His writings helped shape later Sufi understandings of wilāya and the inner life.
items.works: Khatm al-awliyāʾ; ʿIlal al-sharīʿa; Bayān al-farq bayn al-ṣadr wa-l-qalb wa-l-fuʾād wa-l-lubb

items.title: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn Sawra al-Tirmidhī
items.description: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Tirmidhī compiled one of the six canonical Sunni hadith collections, notable for including legal discussion and judgments on hadith grading. His work helped standardize scholarly approaches to Prophetic reports.
items.works: Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī; al-ʿIlal al-kabīr; al-Shamāʾil al-Muḥammadiyya

items.title: Ibn Majah
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Mājah al-Qazwīnī
items.description: Ibn Mājah was a hadith scholar best known for his Sunan, later included among the six canonical Sunni collections. His compilation preserves legal traditions not always found in the other major collections.
items.works: Sunan Ibn Mājah; Tafsīr (lost or incompletely preserved)

items.title: al-Mubarrad
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Akbar al-Thamālī al-Azdī, al-Mubarrad
items.description: Al-Mubarrad was one of the foremost Basran grammarians and a leading Arabic prose stylist. His grammatical writings clarified the legacy of Sībawayh and shaped medieval Arabic linguistics and literary education.
items.works: Al-Kāmil; al-Muqtaḍab; works on grammar and prosody

items.title: al-Nasa'i
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAlī al-Nasāʾī
items.description: Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb al-Nasāʾī was a meticulous hadith critic and compiler whose Sunan became one of the six canonical Sunni collections. He was especially respected for attention to narrator reliability and the legal relevance of reports.
items.works: Al-Sunan al-kubrā; al-Sunan al-ṣughrā (al-Mujtabā); Khaṣāʾiṣ ʿAlī

items.title: al-Junayd al-Baghdadi
items.fullName: al-Junayd ibn Muḥammad al-Baghdādī
items.description: Al-Junayd al-Baghdādī was a foundational Sufi teacher associated with sober, disciplined mysticism grounded in Qur’an and Sunnah. His concise sayings on tawḥīd, spiritual states, and self-effacement became formative for classical Sunni Sufism.
items.works: Letters and sayings preserved in Sufi compilations; no securely authenticated comprehensive authored work

items.title: Ibn Khuzayma
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Khuzayma al-Naysābūrī
items.description: Ibn Khuzayma was a leading hadith scholar and jurist whose collection and theological writings influenced traditionalist Sunni thought. His stringent criteria and extensive learning earned him a reputation as an authority in hadith.
items.works: Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Khuzayma; Kitāb al-Tawḥīd; al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt

items.title: al-Tabari
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī
items.description: Al-Ṭabarī was a monumental historian, Qur’anic exegete, and jurist. His universal history preserves a vast narrative of earlier civilizations and Islamic history, while his comprehensive tafsīr became a foundation of Sunni Qur’anic scholarship.
items.works: Jāmiʿ al-bayān ʿan taʾwīl āy al-Qurʾān; Tārīkh al-rusul wa-l-mulūk; Ikhtilāf al-fuqahāʾ

items.title: Abu al-Husayn al-Nuri
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim al-Nūrī, Abū al-Ḥusayn
items.description: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Nūrī was an early Baghdad Sufi known for asceticism, spiritual insight, and close association with al-Junayd’s circle. His teachings helped define the vocabulary of love, selflessness, and contemplative experience in Sufism.
items.works: Sayings preserved in al-Sarrāj’s al-Lumaʿ and later Sufi biographies; no securely surviving book

items.title: al-Zajjaj
items.fullName: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sarī al-Zajjāj
items.description: Al-Zajjāj was a leading Baghdad grammarian and Qur’anic linguist whose work joined Arabic grammar with lexical and exegetical analysis. He influenced later philologists and commentators through precise explanations of Qur’anic language.
items.works: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān wa-iʿrābuhu; al-Ishtiqāq; works on Arabic grammar

items.title: Abu Ali al-Jubba'i
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Jubbāʾī
items.description: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī was a major Muʿtazilī theologian and teacher of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī before their intellectual break. His systematic arguments on divine justice and attributes shaped later debates in kalām.
items.works: No complete works survive; theological opinions preserved in kalām and heresiographical works

items.title: al-Maturidi
items.fullName: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd al-Māturīdī
items.description: Abū Manṣūr al-Māturīdī founded the Māturīdī school of Sunni theology, defending revelation through disciplined rational argument. His synthesis became especially influential among Ḥanafī communities in Central Asia, Anatolia, and beyond.
items.works: Kitāb al-Tawḥīd; Taʾwīlāt ahl al-Sunna (also called Taʾwīlāt al-Qurʾān)

items.title: al-Tahawi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Salāma al-Ṭaḥāwī
items.description: Al-Ṭaḥāwī was an Egyptian Ḥanafī jurist and hadith scholar whose concise creed became one of the best-known summaries of Sunni belief. His legal and hadith works also helped bridge Egyptian and Iraqi scholarly traditions.
items.works: Al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya; Sharḥ Maʿānī al-āthār; Mushkil al-āthār

items.title: al-Hallaj
items.fullName: al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr al-Ḥallāj
items.description: Al-Ḥallāj was a Persian mystic and preacher whose ecstatic language about divine love and union made him one of Sufism’s most controversial figures. His execution in Baghdad became a lasting symbol in discussions of mystical speech and religious authority.
items.works: Kitāb al-Ṭawāsīn; poems and sayings attributed to him

items.title: al-Shibli
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Dulaf ibn Jaḥdar al-Shiblī
items.description: Al-Shiblī was a Baghdad Sufi and a younger contemporary of al-Junayd, remembered for ecstatic sayings, ascetic practice, and reflections on divine love. Later hagiography made him an emblem of the tension between mystical expression and public norms.
items.works: Sayings and anecdotes preserved in Sufi biographies; no authenticated independent book

items.title: Ibn Surayj
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar ibn Surayj al-Baghdādī
items.description: Ibn Surayj was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist whose legal reasoning helped establish the school’s classical methods. He was renowned for debate and interpretation and influenced later Shāfiʿī jurisprudence in Iraq and the wider Islamic world.
items.works: No complete authenticated work survives; legal opinions and debates transmitted in Shāfiʿī literature

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Razi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Zakariyyā al-Rāzī
items.description: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī, known in Arabic sources as a physician and philosopher distinct from the later theologian Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī, was a major medical innovator and rational thinker. His clinical writings shaped medicine in the Islamic world and Latin Europe.
items.works: Al-Ḥāwī fī al-ṭibb; Kitāb al-Manṣūrī; al-Judarī wa-l-ḥaṣba; philosophical treatises including al-Ṭibb al-rūḥānī

items.title: al-Barbahari
items.fullName: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Khalaf al-Barbahārī
items.description: Al-Barbahārī was a prominent Baghdadi traditionalist associated with strict adherence to early Sunni doctrine and opposition to theological innovation. His teachings became influential in later Ḥanbalī and Atharī thought.
items.works: Sharḥ al-Sunna (attributed); doctrinal views preserved in Ḥanbalī biographical sources

items.title: al-Farabi
items.fullName: Abū Naṣr Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Fārābī
items.description: Al-Fārābī was a major philosopher, logician, political thinker, and music theorist often called the “Second Teacher” after Aristotle. He systematized Aristotelian logic in Arabic and developed influential accounts of intellect, virtue, and the ideal city.
items.works: Ārāʾ ahl al-madīna al-fāḍila; Iḥṣāʾ al-ʿulūm; Kitāb al-Mūsīqā al-kabīr; Risāla fī al-ʿaql

items.title: Ibn Durustawayh
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Durustawayh al-Fārisī
items.description: Ibn Durustawayh was an influential Basran grammarian and philologist who contributed to debates over Arabic syntax, lexicography, and linguistic analogy. His writings reflect the maturation of Arabic grammatical scholarship in the Abbasid period.
items.works: Al-Kitāb (grammar); Sharḥ al-Faṣīḥ; works on grammar and lexicography

items.title: al-Ashari
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ashʿarī
items.description: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī founded the Ashʿarī school of Sunni kalām after leaving Muʿtazilism. He defended core Sunni doctrines through rational argument, and his approach became one of the dominant traditions of Sunni theology.
items.works: Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn; al-Lumaʿ; al-Ibāna ʿan uṣūl al-diyāna (textual history and exact relation among works debated)

items.title: al-Hakim al-Samarqandi
items.fullName: Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ḥakīm al-Samarqandī
items.description: Al-Ḥakīm al-Samarqandī was an early Māturīdī theologian whose concise creed became an important statement of Sunni belief in Transoxiana. His work helped give the emerging school a stable doctrinal formulation.
items.works: Al-Sawād al-aʿẓam

items.title: Ibn Khafif
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Khafīf al-Shīrāzī
items.description: Ibn Khafīf was a Persian Sufi and Shāfiʿī scholar based in Shiraz. Known for combining spiritual discipline with orthodox learning, he helped transmit early Sufi teaching and became an influential teacher in western Iran.
items.works: Al-Iqtiṣād; ʿAqīda (titles and attributions vary); sayings preserved in Sufi biographical sources

items.title: Ibn Masarra
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masarra al-Jabalī
items.description: Ibn Masarra was an early Andalusian philosopher and ascetic whose thought combined Qur’anic interpretation with philosophical and mystical ideas. His influence on later Andalusian intellectual currents is significant, though aspects of his doctrine remain disputed.
items.works: Kitāb al-Tabṣira; Kitāb al-Ḥurūf (attributions and surviving fragments debated)

items.title: Ibn Hibban
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Ḥibbān ibn Aḥmad al-Tamīmī al-Bustī
items.description: Ibn Ḥibbān was a prolific hadith critic, historian, and jurist who developed influential methods for evaluating narrators. His works preserve biographical data and hadith material and were widely used by later Sunni scholars.
items.works: Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Ḥibbān; Kitāb al-Thiqāt; al-Majrūḥīn; Rawḍat al-ʿuqalāʾ

items.title: Abu al-Qasim al-Kabi
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Maḥmūd al-Kaʿbī al-Balkhī
items.description: Abū al-Qāsim al-Kaʿbī was a leading Baghdadi Muʿtazilī theologian and head of a distinct branch of the school. His rationalist positions on divine action and human agency influenced later theological controversies.
items.works: No complete work survives; kalām views quoted by later theologians and heresiographers

items.title: Abu Hashim al-Jubba'i
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Muḥammad al-Jubbāʾī, Abū Hāshim
items.description: Abū Hāshim al-Jubbāʾī was a major Muʿtazilī theologian who developed the theory of “states” (aḥwāl) to explain divine attributes. His doctrine influenced later debates about language, attributes, and the structure of theological explanation.
items.works: No complete works survive; doctrines preserved in later kalām literature

items.title: Abu Ali al-Farisi
items.fullName: al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Ghaffār al-Fārisī
items.description: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī was a leading grammarian whose analytical approach shaped Arabic syntax and philology. He taught important scholars and contributed to the development of grammatical argumentation in the eastern Islamic world.
items.works: Al-Ḥujja li-l-qurrāʾ al-sabʿa; al-Īḍāḥ; al-Takmila

items.title: Abu al-Hasan al-Amiri
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-ʿĀmirī
items.description: Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿĀmirī was a philosopher who sought to demonstrate the compatibility of Islamic revelation and Greek philosophy. His writings compare religious traditions and defend the intellectual and moral value of prophecy.
items.works: Al-Iʿlām bi-manāqib al-Islām; Kitāb al-Amad ʿalā al-abad; al-Saʿāda wa-l-isʿād

items.title: al-Jassas
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Rāzī al-Jaṣṣāṣ
items.description: Al-Jaṣṣāṣ was a leading Ḥanafī jurist and Qur’anic exegete whose work helped systematize legal theory and the interpretation of legal verses. His writings remain central to the classical Ḥanafī school.
items.works: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān; al-Fuṣūl fī al-uṣūl; Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar al-Ṭaḥāwī

items.title: al-Daraqutni
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad al-Dāraquṭnī
items.description: Al-Dāraquṭnī was a major hadith critic whose expertise in subtle defects and variant transmissions made him a leading authority in hadith criticism. His collections also preserve legal traditions and disagreements among early scholars.
items.works: Sunan al-Dāraquṭnī; al-ʿIlal al-wārida fī al-aḥādīth; al-Afrād

items.title: Abu Talib al-Makki
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyya al-Ḥārithī al-Makkī, Abū Ṭālib
items.description: Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī was an influential Sufi author who integrated hadith, worship, asceticism, and spiritual psychology. His work became a source for al-Ghazālī and helped shape the synthesis of Sufism with Sunni religious learning.
items.works: Qūt al-qulūb fī muʿāmalat al-maḥbūb

items.title: Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Abū Muḥammad ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī
items.description: Ibn Abī Zayd al-Qayrawānī was a leading Mālikī jurist of Ifrīqiya whose manual became a foundational statement of Mālikī law and creed in North Africa. His teaching helped establish the school’s authority across the Maghrib.
items.works: Al-Risāla; al-Nawādir wa-l-ziyādāt; Mukhtaṣar al-Mudawwana

items.title: Abu Hayyan al-Tawhidi
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Tawḥīdī
items.description: Abū Ḥayyān al-Tawḥīdī was a celebrated prose writer and intellectual observer of Abbasid society. His works combine philosophical conversation, adab, ethical reflection, and social criticism, making him a major witness to the intellectual life of his era.
items.works: Al-Imtāʿ wa-l-muʾānasa; al-Muqābasāt; al-Baṣāʾir wa-l-dhakhāʾir; Akhlāq al-wazīrayn

items.title: Miskawayh
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb Miskawayh
items.description: Miskawayh was a Persian philosopher, historian, and ethicist who developed an influential account of virtue, character formation, and the cultivation of the soul. His ethical philosophy brought Greek moral philosophy into sustained dialogue with Islamic intellectual life.
items.works: Tahdhīb al-akhlāq wa-taṭhīr al-aʿrāq; Tajārib al-umam; al-Fawz al-aṣghar

items.title: al-Hakim al-Naysaburi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥamdawayh al-Ḥākim al-Naysābūrī
items.description: Al-Ḥākim al-Naysābūrī was a major hadith scholar who sought to identify authentic reports meeting the criteria of al-Bukhārī and Muslim. His biographical and methodological works are important for the history of Sunni hadith scholarship.
items.works: Al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-Ṣaḥīḥayn; Maʿrifat ʿulūm al-ḥadīth; Tārīkh Naysābūr

items.title: Qadi Abd al-Jabbar
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Aḥmad al-Hamadhānī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Jabbār was the most influential later Muʿtazilī theologian, systematizing the school’s doctrines of divine unity, justice, and human responsibility. His extensive works preserve much of what is known about classical Muʿtazilism.
items.works: Al-Mughnī fī abwāb al-tawḥīd wa-l-ʿadl; Sharḥ al-uṣūl al-khamsa; Faḍl al-iʿtizāl; Tanzīh al-Qurʾān ʿan al-maṭāʿin

items.title: Ibn Furak
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Fūrak al-Anṣārī
items.description: Ibn Fūrak was an Ashʿarī theologian and hadith scholar who helped transmit and systematize the thought of al-Ashʿarī. His work strengthened Ashʿarī theology in Khurasan and contributed to its development as a major Sunni intellectual tradition.
items.works: Mujarrad Maqālāt al-Ashʿarī; Mushkil al-ḥadīth wa-bayānuhu; al-Ḥudūd

items.title: Ibn Jinni
items.fullName: ʿUthmān ibn Jinnī al-Mawṣilī
items.description: Ibn Jinnī was a seminal Arabic grammarian and theorist of language whose writings explored morphology, phonetics, analogy, and the philosophical dimensions of linguistic structure. His work remains central to the history of Arabic linguistics.
items.works: Al-Khaṣāʾiṣ; Sirr ṣināʿat al-iʿrāb; al-Munṣif fī sharḥ Kitāb al-Taṣrīf

items.title: Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi
items.fullName: Naṣr ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Samarqandī, Abū al-Layth
items.description: Abū al-Layth al-Samarqandī was a Ḥanafī jurist, Qur’anic exegete, and preacher whose accessible works became widely read in Muslim devotional and educational settings. His writings helped transmit legal and ethical learning across Central Asia.
items.works: Baḥr al-ʿulūm (tafsīr); Tanbīh al-ghāfilīn; Bustān al-ʿārifīn; Khizānat al-fiqh, al-nawazil

items.title: al-Sulami
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī al-Sulamī
items.description: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī was a Sufi scholar and compiler who preserved early mystical sayings and biographies. His collections are indispensable sources for the development of classical Sufism and for the spiritual interpretations of the Qur’an.
items.works: Ṭabaqāt al-ṣūfiyya; Ḥaqāʾiq al-tafsīr; Ādāb al-ṣuḥba; ʿUyūb al-nafs

items.title: Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Mihrān al-Isfarāʾīnī
items.description: Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāʾīnī was an influential Ashʿarī theologian and jurist who helped consolidate Ashʿarī doctrine in the eastern Islamic lands. His teaching contributed to the school’s institutional and intellectual growth.
items.works: No complete securely extant major work; theological positions and legal opinions cited in later Ashʿarī literature

items.title: al-Baqillani
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṭayyib al-Bāqillānī
items.description: Al-Bāqillānī was a central Ashʿarī theologian who refined arguments for divine unity, prophecy, and the createdness of the world. His rigorous use of dialectic helped make Ashʿarī kalām a sophisticated Sunni theological system.
items.works: Kitāb al-Tamhīd; al-Inṣāf; Iʿjāz al-Qurʾān; Manāqib al-aʾimma

items.title: Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Isfarāyīnī, Abū Ḥāmid
items.description: Abū Ḥāmid al-Isfarāyīnī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist and teacher in Baghdad whose legal authority influenced the school’s Iraqi branch. His lessons and opinions were widely transmitted, although much of his written corpus is lost.
items.works: No securely preserved comprehensive book; legal opinions transmitted in Shāfiʿī works

items.title: Abu al-Hasan al-Kharaqani
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Kharaqānī, Abū al-Ḥasan
items.description: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Kharaqānī was a Persian Sufi remembered for spiritual insight, hospitality, and a universal language of devotion. His sayings profoundly influenced later Persian Sufi literature, particularly ʿAṭṭār and other hagiographers.
items.works: Sayings preserved in Nūr al-ʿulūm and later Sufi biographies; attribution details are uncertain

items.title: al-Shurunbulali
items.fullName: Ḥasan ibn ʿAmmār ibn ʿAlī al-Shurunbulālī
items.description: Al-Shurunbulālī was an influential Ottoman-era Ḥanafī jurist whose concise legal manuals became standard references for worship and daily practice. His work helped make Ḥanafī law accessible to students and practitioners.
items.works: Nūr al-īḍāḥ; Marāqī al-falāḥ (commentary on Nūr al-īḍāḥ); al-Durar al-mubāḥa

items.title: Abu Said ibn Abi al-Khayr
items.fullName: Faḍl Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abū Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Khayr
items.description: Abū Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Khayr was a celebrated Persian Sufi who helped develop the communal practices and poetic expression of Khurasanian mysticism. His sayings and spiritual teaching became central to Persian Sufi memory.
items.works: Asrār al-tawḥīd fī maqāmāt al-shaykh Abī Saʿīd (compiled by a descendant); sayings and quatrains attributed to him

items.title: al-Mawardi
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb al-Māwardī
items.description: Al-Māwardī was a Shāfiʿī jurist and political theorist who analyzed the institutions and responsibilities of Islamic governance. His works on public law, administration, and Qur’anic interpretation became lasting references in Sunni political thought.
items.works: Al-Aḥkām al-sulṭāniyya; Adab al-dunyā wa-l-dīn; al-Nukat wa-l-ʿuyūn (tafsīr); Qawānīn al-wizāra

items.title: Ibn Abd al-Barr
items.fullName: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Barr al-Namarī
items.description: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr was a leading Andalusian Mālikī scholar and hadith expert. His biographical dictionaries and syntheses of hadith and law became essential reference works across Sunni scholarship, especially in the western Islamic lands.
items.works: Al-Tamhīd; al-Istidhkār; Jāmiʿ bayān al-ʿilm wa-faḍlihi; al-Istīʿāb fī maʿrifat al-aṣḥāb

items.title: al-Dabusi
items.fullName: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿĪsā al-Dabūsī
items.description: Al-Dabūsī was an early Ḥanafī jurist and theorist who helped shape the technical discipline of uṣūl al-fiqh. His systematic treatment of legal principles influenced later Ḥanafī theorists in Central Asia and beyond.
items.works: Taʾsīs al-naẓar; Taqwīm al-adilla fī uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Amad al-aqṣā

items.title: Ibn Sina
items.fullName: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sīnā
items.description: Ibn Sīnā (Avicenna) was a Persian polymath whose philosophy, medicine, and natural science profoundly influenced the Islamic world and medieval Europe. His metaphysics of essence and existence and his medical synthesis became enduring reference points.
items.works: Al-Shifāʾ; al-Qānūn fī al-ṭibb; al-Najāt; al-Ishārāt wa-l-tanbīhāt; Dāneshnāmeh-ye ʿAlāʾī

items.title: Abu al-Husayn al-Basri
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Baṣrī, Abū al-Ḥusayn
items.description: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Baṣrī was an influential Muʿtazilī theologian and legal theorist who combined rational theology with sophisticated analysis of legal evidence. His work became important to later discussions of epistemology and uṣūl al-fiqh.
items.works: Al-Muʿtamad fī uṣūl al-fiqh; Taṣaffuḥ al-adilla; Ghurar al-adilla (partly lost/fragmentary)

items.title: Abd al-Qahir al-Baghdadi
items.fullName: Abū Manṣūr ʿAbd al-Qāhir ibn Ṭāhir ibn Muḥammad al-Baghdādī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Baghdādī was an Ashʿarī theologian, heresiographer, and mathematician who sought to classify Islamic sects and defend Sunni orthodoxy. His works are significant sources for the history of early Islamic theological movements.
items.works: Al-Farq bayn al-firaq; Uṣūl al-dīn; al-Takmila fī al-ḥisāb

items.title: Abu Ubayd al-Juzjani
items.fullName: Abū ʿUbayd ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Muḥammad al-Jūzjānī
items.description: Al-Jūzjānī was a physician and close disciple of Ibn Sīnā who preserved biographical details about the philosopher and helped transmit his works. His role is especially important for understanding Avicenna’s life and intellectual legacy.
items.works: Biography of Ibn Sīnā appended to Avicennian works; editorial/transmission work on Ibn Sīnā’s writings

items.title: al-Qushayri
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Hawāzin al-Qushayrī
items.description: Al-Qushayrī was a major Shāfiʿī scholar and Sufi who articulated a learned, Sunni account of the mystical path. His epistle became one of the most influential introductions to classical Sufi doctrine, practice, and terminology.
items.works: Al-Risāla al-Qushayriyya; Laṭāʾif al-ishārāt (tafsīr); al-Taysīr fī ʿilm al-tafsīr

items.title: Abu Ya'la
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Farrāʾ al-Baghdādī, Abū Yaʿlā
items.description: Abū Yaʿlā al-Farrāʾ was a leading Ḥanbalī jurist and theologian who codified the school’s doctrines and legal method. His works on governance and creed remain important witnesses to classical Ḥanbalī thought.
items.works: Al-Aḥkām al-sulṭāniyya; al-Muʿtamad fī uṣūl al-dīn; al-ʿUdda fī uṣūl al-fiqh

items.title: Bahmanyar ibn Marzuban
items.fullName: Bahmanyār ibn Marzubān al-Ādharbāyjānī
items.description: Bahmanyār ibn Marzubān was an Iranian philosopher and prominent student of Ibn Sīnā. His systematic exposition of Avicennian philosophy helped transmit and develop the Peripatetic tradition in the generations after Avicenna.
items.works: Al-Taḥṣīl (The Attainment); treatises in Avicennian logic and metaphysics

items.title: al-Bayhaqi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Bayhaqī
items.description: Al-Bayhaqī was a major Shāfiʿī hadith scholar and theologian who assembled extensive evidence for Sunni doctrine, worship, and law. His collections remain important to hadith studies and the history of Ashʿarī traditionalism.
items.works: Al-Sunan al-kubrā; Shuʿab al-īmān; Dalāʾil al-nubuwwa; al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt; Maʿrifat al-sunan wa-l-āthār

items.title: Ibn Hazm
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥazm al-Andalusī
items.description: Ibn Ḥazm was an Andalusian scholar, theologian, historian, and poet, and the foremost intellectual defender of Ẓāhirī legal literalism. His writings range from comparative religion to ethics and love, making him one of medieval Islam’s most distinctive thinkers.
items.works: Al-Muḥallā; al-Iḥkām fī uṣūl al-aḥkām; Ṭawq al-ḥamāma; al-Fiṣal fī al-milal wa-l-ahwāʾ wa-l-niḥal

items.title: Hamid al-Din al-Kirmani
items.fullName: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kirmānī
items.description: Al-Kirmānī was an Ismāʿīlī missionary and philosopher who developed a sophisticated synthesis of Neoplatonic philosophy and Ismāʿīlī theology during the Fatimid era. His work helped formalize the intellectual system of the Ismāʿīlī daʿwa.
items.works: Rāḥat al-ʿaql; al-Riyāḍ; al-Maṣābīḥ fī ithbāt al-imāma

items.title: Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf al-Shīrāzī
items.description: Abū Isḥāq al-Shīrāzī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist and legal theorist whose teaching in Baghdad attracted students from across the Muslim world. His manuals became foundational texts in Shāfiʿī law and uṣūl al-fiqh.
items.works: Al-Muhadhdhab; al-Lumaʿ fī uṣūl al-fiqh; Ṭabaqāt al-fuqahāʾ; al-Tanbīh

items.title: al-Khatib al-Baghdadi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Thābit al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī
items.description: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī was a preeminent hadith scholar and historian of Baghdad. His methodological works on transmission, narrator ethics, and the city’s scholars profoundly influenced Sunni hadith scholarship and biographical writing.
items.works: Tārīkh Baghdād; al-Kifāya fī ʿilm al-riwāya; al-Jāmiʿ li-akhlāq al-rāwī wa-ādāb al-sāmiʿ

items.title: Abd Allah al-Ansari al-Harawi
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī al-Harawī
items.description: ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī al-Harawī was a Persian Hanbalī scholar, preacher, and Sufi whose devotional writing emphasized sincerity, spiritual stations, and reliance on God. His concise manuals influenced later Persian and Arabic Sufi literature.
items.works: Manāzil al-sāʾirīn; Dhamm al-kalām wa-ahlihi; Ṣad maydān; Munājāt

items.title: al-Lakhmi
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qayrawānī al-Rabʿī al-Lakhmī
items.description: Al-Lakhmī was a Mālikī jurist of Qayrawān and a leading commentator on the Mudawwana. His legal analysis influenced the development of Mālikī jurisprudence in the Maghrib and helped clarify points of disagreement within the school.
items.works: Al-Tabṣira; commentaries and legal notes on the Mudawwana (some works survive incompletely)

items.title: al-Sarakhsi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī Sahl al-Sarakhsī
items.description: Al-Sarakhsī was a preeminent Ḥanafī jurist whose vast legal commentary became one of the school’s most influential authorities. His treatment of legal reasoning, transactions, and state relations shaped later Ḥanafī doctrine.
items.works: Al-Mabsūṭ; Uṣūl al-Sarakhsī; Sharḥ al-Siyar al-kabīr

items.title: Ali al-Hujwiri
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān al-Jullābī al-Hujwīrī
items.description: ʿAlī al-Hujwīrī was a Persian Sufi author best known for the earliest surviving comprehensive Persian treatise on Sufism. He explained Sufi doctrine, spiritual practice, and the lives of earlier masters, making the book foundational in Persianate Sufi culture.
items.works: Kashf al-maḥjūb

items.title: Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Qāhir ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jurjānī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī was a seminal theorist of Arabic rhetoric and literary meaning. His theory of naẓm explains eloquence through syntactic relations and meaning, profoundly shaping later balāgha, Qur’anic stylistics, and literary criticism.
items.works: Dalāʾil al-iʿjāz; Asrār al-balāgha; al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa

items.title: Abu al-'Usr al-Bazdawi
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Bazdawī
items.description: Fakhr al-Islām al-Bazdawī was a major Ḥanafī jurist and legal theorist whose synthesis of doctrine influenced the school’s mature legal method. His work became a central reference for Ḥanafī uṣūl al-fiqh.
items.works: Kanz al-wuṣūl ilā maʿrifat al-uṣūl (Uṣūl al-Bazdawī)

items.title: Abu al-Muin al-Nasafi
items.fullName: Maymūn ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muʿtamid al-Makhūlī al-Nasafī, Abū al-Muʿīn
items.description: Abū al-Muʿīn al-Nasafī was a leading Māturīdī theologian who systematized the school’s response to competing theological positions. His comprehensive works became foundational references for Sunni kalām, especially among Ḥanafī scholars.
items.works: Tabṣirat al-adilla; Baḥr al-kalām; al-Tamhīd li-qawāʿid al-tawḥīd

items.title: al-Juwayni
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf al-Juwaynī
items.description: Al-Juwaynī, known as Imām al-Ḥaramayn, was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist and Ashʿarī theologian, and teacher of al-Ghazālī. His sophisticated analyses of theology, legal theory, and political authority helped shape classical Sunni thought.
items.works: Al-Irshād; al-Burhān fī uṣūl al-fiqh; Ghiyāth al-umam; al-ʿAqīda al-Niẓāmiyya

items.title: Abu al-Yusr al-Bazdawi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Bazdawī, Abū al-Yusr
items.description: Abū al-Yusr al-Bazdawī was an important Ḥanafī-Māturīdī theologian who defended Sunni doctrine and helped consolidate Māturīdī kalām in Transoxiana. He is distinct from his brother Fakhr al-Islām al-Bazdawī, the jurist.
items.works: Uṣūl al-dīn; Sharḥ al-Fiqh al-akbar

items.title: Ibn Aqil
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿAqīl ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl al-Baghdādī
items.description: Ibn ʿAqīl was a prominent Ḥanbalī jurist and theologian in Baghdad who wrote on law, theology, ethics, and literary culture. His intellectual range illustrates the engagement of some Ḥanbalī scholars with philosophical and rational disciplines.
items.works: Al-Funūn (encyclopedic work, largely lost); al-Wāḍiḥ fī uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Jadal ʿalā ṭarīqat al-fuqahāʾ

items.title: Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari
items.fullName: Salmān ibn Nāṣir ibn ʿImrān al-Anṣārī al-Nīsābūrī
items.description: Abū al-Qāsim al-Anṣārī was an Ashʿarī theologian and commentator associated with the Naysābūr school. His teaching and explanatory works helped transmit the theological system of al-Juwaynī to later generations.
items.works: Sharḥ al-Irshād (commentary on al-Juwaynī); theological writings mostly preserved through later citations

items.title: al-Baghawi
items.fullName: al-Ḥusayn ibn Masʿūd al-Baghawī
items.description: Al-Baghawī was a Shāfiʿī jurist, hadith scholar, and Qur’anic exegete whose accessible compilations became widely used in Islamic education. He brought together transmitted commentary, hadith, and legal teaching in influential handbooks.
items.works: Maʿālim al-tanzīl; Sharḥ al-Sunna; Maṣābīḥ al-sunna; al-Tahdhīb fī fiqh al-Imām al-Shāfiʿī

items.title: Abu Shuja
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Iṣfahānī, Abū Shujāʿ
items.description: Abū Shujāʿ al-Iṣfahānī was a Shāfiʿī jurist whose concise manual became one of the most widely taught introductions to Shāfiʿī law. Its clarity and compact organization led to many commentaries across centuries.
items.works: Ghāyat al-ikhtiṣār (also al-Taqrīb)

items.title: Badi' al-Zaman al-Hamadhani
items.fullName: Abū al-Faḍl Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Hamadhānī, Badīʿ al-Zamān
items.description: Al-Hamadhānī, likely Badīʿ al-Zamān al-Hamadhānī, was a Persian Arabophone prose innovator credited with establishing the classical maqāma genre. His ornate, witty narratives influenced later Arabic literary prose.
items.works: Maqāmāt al-Hamadhānī; collected epistles

items.title: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali
items.fullName: Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī
items.description: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī was a major theologian, jurist, philosopher, and Sufi whose works reoriented Sunni intellectual life by integrating law, theology, ethics, and spiritual practice. He critically assessed philosophy while appropriating its tools and making inner purification central to religious life.
items.works: Iḥyāʾ ʿulūm al-dīn; Tahāfut al-falāsifa; al-Munqidh min al-ḍalāl; al-Mustaṣfā; Maqāṣid al-falāsifa

items.title: al-Kiya al-Harrasi
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ṭabarī, al-Kiyā al-Harrāsī
items.description: Al-Kiyā al-Harrāsī was a Shāfiʿī jurist and Qur’anic exegete associated with the Nizamiyya scholarly world. His commentary on legal verses contributed to the development of juridical tafsīr and Shāfiʿī legal interpretation.
items.works: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān

items.title: Ibn Rushd al-Jadd
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Rushd al-Qurṭubī, Ibn Rushd al-Jadd
items.description: Ibn Rushd al-Jadd was a leading Andalusian Mālikī jurist and grandfather of the philosopher Averroes. His legal opinions were highly influential in the western Islamic world and helped shape the Mālikī tradition’s treatment of complex cases.
items.works: Al-Bayān wa-l-taḥṣīl; al-Muqaddimāt al-mumahhidāt; legal fatwas

items.title: Ahmad al-Ghazali
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī
items.description: Aḥmad al-Ghazālī was a Persian Sufi preacher and elder brother of Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī. His teachings centered on divine love and the soul’s longing for God, exerting a strong influence on later Persian mystical poetry and Sufi thought.
items.works: Sawāniḥ al-ʿushshāq; sermons and sayings preserved in Sufi literature

items.title: al-Mazari
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Tamīmī al-Māzirī
items.description: Al-Māzarī was a leading Mālikī jurist and Ashʿarī theologian from Sicily and Ifrīqiya. His commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and legal scholarship helped transmit western Islamic learning and became influential beyond North Africa.
items.works: Al-Muʿlim bi-fawāʾid Muslim; Īḍāḥ al-maḥṣūl min burhān al-uṣūl; fatwas

items.title: Najm al-din al-Nasafi
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nasafī
items.description: ʿUmar al-Nasafī was a Ḥanafī-Māturīdī scholar known for a concise creed that became one of the most widely taught summaries of Sunni theology. He also wrote on Qur’anic exegesis, law, and scholarly biography.
items.works: Al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya; al-Taysīr fī al-tafsīr; al-Qand fī dhikr ʿulamāʾ Samarqand

items.title: Abu Ishaq al-Saffar al-Bukhari
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ṣaffār al-Bukhārī
items.description: Abū Isḥāq al-Ṣaffār al-Bukhārī was a Māturīdī theologian who helped articulate Sunni creed and defend it against rival theological approaches. His writings are important witnesses to the diversity and sophistication of Central Asian kalām.
items.works: Talkhīṣ al-adilla li-qawāʿid al-tawḥīd

items.title: Ala' al-Din al-Samarqandi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Samarqandī, ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn
items.description: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Samarqandī was a Ḥanafī jurist and theologian known for works in legal theory and substantive law. His scholarship influenced later Ḥanafī authorities, and his daughter Fāṭima became a respected jurist in her own right.
items.works: Tuḥfat al-fuqahāʾ; Mīzān al-uṣūl fī natāʾij al-ʿuqūl

items.title: al-Zamakhshari
items.fullName: Maḥmūd ibn ʿUmar al-Zamakhsharī
items.description: Al-Zamakhsharī was a major Arabic grammarian, rhetorician, and Qur’anic exegete associated with Muʿtazilī theology. His tafsīr is renowned for linguistic precision and rhetorical analysis and influenced both supportive and critical later commentators.
items.works: Al-Kashshāf ʿan ḥaqāʾiq al-tanzīl; al-Mufaṣṣal fī ṣanʿat al-iʿrāb; Asās al-balāgha; al-Maqāmāt

items.title: Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Qādir ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ Jangī-Dūst al-Jīlānī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī was a celebrated preacher and Hanbalī scholar whose spiritual teaching became foundational to the Qādiriyya Sufi order. Later tradition emphasized his sermons, ethical counsel, and model of repentance and reliance on God.
items.works: Al-Ghunya li-ṭālibī ṭarīq al-ḥaqq; Futūḥ al-ghayb; al-Fatḥ al-rabbānī (sermons attributed/compiled posthumously)

items.title: Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Maʿāfirī al-Ishbīlī, Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī
items.description: Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī was an Andalusian Mālikī jurist, theologian, and Qur’anic exegete who studied in the East and brought its scholarship to the Maghrib. His writings became major sources for legal tafsīr and Mālikī jurisprudence.
items.works: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān; al-ʿAwāṣim min al-qawāṣim; al-Qabas fī sharḥ Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik

items.title: Reign of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rūm
Ibn Tumart
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Tūmart al-Maṣmūdī
items.description: Ibn Tūmart was a North African religious reformer and founder of the Almohad movement, whose teachings on divine unity, moral reform, and leadership reshaped the Maghrib and al-Andalus. His legacy became the ideological basis of the Almohad state.
items.works: Aʿazz mā yuṭlab (attributed); Murshida; teachings preserved in Almohad doctrinal compilations

items.title: Qadi Iyad
items.fullName: ʿIyāḍ ibn Mūsā ibn ʿIyāḍ al-Yaḥṣubī, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ
items.description: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ was a leading Mālikī jurist, hadith scholar, and biographer from Ceuta. His writings on the Prophet’s status and the scholars of Mālikī tradition became authoritative throughout the Muslim world.
items.works: Al-Shifāʾ bi-taʿrīf ḥuqūq al-Muṣṭafā; Tartīb al-madārik; Ikmāl al-Muʿlim bi-fawāʾid Muslim

items.title: Ibn Bajja
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ṣāʾigh al-Tujībī al-Andalusī
items.description: Ibn Bājja (Avempace) was an Andalusian philosopher, physician, and natural scientist who helped introduce Aristotelian philosophy into western Islam. His account of intellectual perfection influenced Ibn Ṭufayl and Ibn Rushd.
items.works: Tadbīr al-mutawaḥḥid; Risālat al-ittiṣāl; treatises on the soul, nature, and astronomy

items.title: al-Shahrastani
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Shahrastānī
items.description: Al-Shahrastānī was a theologian and historian of religions known for his unusually systematic survey of religious and philosophical schools. His work remains an important source for Islamic heresiography and the comparative study of religion.
items.works: Al-Milal wa-l-niḥal; Nihāyat al-aqdām fī ʿilm al-kalām; Mafātīḥ al-asrār

items.title: Ibn al-Arif
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Ṣanhājī al-Maryamī, Ibn al-ʿArīf
items.description: Ibn al-ʿArīf was an Andalusian Sufi and spiritual teacher associated with Almería. His teachings on spiritual stations and divine love influenced early western Islamic mysticism, though later reports about him reflect the contested religious climate of his time.
items.works: Maḥāsin al-majālis; sayings preserved in Sufi biographies

items.title: Ibn Atiyya
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq ibn Ghālib ibn ʿAṭiyya al-Muḥāribī
items.description: Ibn ʿAṭiyya was an Andalusian Mālikī jurist and Qur’anic exegete whose commentary combined transmitted reports with close linguistic analysis. His balanced tafsīr became an important source for later commentators in the Maghrib and beyond.
items.works: Al-Muḥarrar al-wajīz fī tafsīr al-kitāb al-ʿazīz

items.title: Ahmad Yasawi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Yasawī
items.description: Aḥmad Yasawī was a Turkic Sufi poet and teacher whose devotional verse helped spread Islam in Turkic-speaking Central Asia. The Yasawiyya tradition associated with him had a lasting influence on Turkic Sufism and religious culture.
items.works: Dīvān-i Ḥikmet (collection attributed to him and developed through later transmission)

items.title: Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Maqdisī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Ghanī al-Maqdisī was a leading Ḥanbalī hadith scholar whose collections and concise transmitter biographies supported the growth of hadith-centered legal scholarship. He was a significant figure in the scholarly tradition of Damascus.
items.works: Al-Kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl; ʿUmdat al-aḥkām; al-Iqtiṣād fī al-iʿtiqād (attribution varies)

items.title: Ayn al-Qudat al-Hamadhani
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Miyānjī, ʿAyn al-Quḍāt al-Hamadhānī
items.description: ʿAyn al-Quḍāt al-Hamadānī was a Persian mystic, philosopher, and judge whose writings explored divine love, spiritual knowledge, and the limits of rational theology. Executed while young, he became a major figure in Persian mystical literature.
items.works: Tamhīdāt; Zubdat al-ḥaqāʾiq; Shakwā al-gharīb ʿan al-awṭān

items.title: Ibn Tufayl
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṭufayl al-Qaysī
items.description: Ibn Ṭufayl was an Andalusian philosopher, physician, and court official best known for a philosophical tale about a self-taught human who discovers truth through reason and contemplation. His work influenced European Enlightenment debates about knowledge and natural religion.
items.works: Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān

items.title: Ibn Asakir
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Hibat Allāh ibn ʿAsākir al-Dimashqī
items.description: Ibn ʿAsākir was a prominent Damascene Shāfiʿī hadith scholar and historian who documented the city’s scholars and defended Ashʿarī theology. His massive biographical history remains a foundational source for Syria’s Islamic intellectual history.
items.works: Tārīkh Madīnat Dimashq; Tabyīn kadhib al-muftarī fīmā nusiba ilā al-Imām Abī al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī; al-Arbaʿūn al-buldāniyya

items.title: Nur al-Din al-Sabuni
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Maḥmūd ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣābūnī
items.description: Nūr al-Dīn al-Ṣābūnī was a major Māturīdī theologian who helped clarify the school’s doctrinal positions in debate with Ashʿarī and Muʿtazilī thinkers. His concise and extended works became important Central Asian theological texts.
items.works: Al-Bidāya min al-kifāya fī al-hidāya; al-Kifāya fī al-hidāya; al-Muntaqā min ʿiṣmat al-anbiyāʾ

items.title: Ibn al-Jawzi
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Jawzī
items.description: Ibn al-Jawzī was a prolific Ḥanbalī preacher, historian, Qur’anic exegete, and moral writer in Baghdad. His works combined scholarship with accessible preaching and critique of excesses in theology, asceticism, and popular religious practice.
items.works: Ṣayd al-khāṭir; Talbīs Iblīs; Zād al-masīr; al-Muntaẓam; Ṣifat al-ṣafwa; al-Mawḍūʿāt

items.title: Ahmad al-Rifai
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Rifāʿī
items.description: Aḥmad al-Rifāʿī was an Iraqi Sufi master whose devotional teachings became the basis of the Rifāʿiyya order. His legacy emphasizes humility, service, and spiritual discipline, though many sayings attributed to him were transmitted in later sources.
items.works: Al-Burhān al-muʾayyad (sermons attributed/compiled); sayings preserved in Rifāʿī literature

items.title: Ibn Rushd
items.fullName: Abū al-Walīd Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Rushd
items.description: Ibn Rushd (Averroes) was an Andalusian philosopher, jurist, and physician whose commentaries on Aristotle reshaped medieval philosophy in both the Islamic world and Europe. He defended philosophy’s legitimacy and argued for a disciplined relationship between demonstration and revelation.
items.works: Tahāfut al-tahāfut; Faṣl al-maqāl; Bidāyat al-mujtahid; major commentaries on Aristotle; al-Kulliyyāt fī al-ṭibb

items.title: Abu Madyan
items.fullName: Shuʿayb ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Anṣārī al-Andalusī, Abū Madyan
items.description: Abū Madyan was a foundational Maghribi Sufi whose teaching linked spiritual realization with adherence to religious practice. His influence spread across North Africa and helped shape the spiritual environment from which later figures such as Ibn ʿArabī emerged.
items.works: Poems, aphorisms, and teachings preserved in Sufi collections; no single securely authenticated major book

items.title: Ruzbihan Baqli
items.fullName: Rūzbihān ibn Abī Naṣr al-Baqlī al-Shīrāzī
items.description: Rūzbihān Baqlī was a Persian Sufi writer known for rich interpretations of mystical experience, love, and theophany. His writings are important sources for ecstatic Sufism and the esoteric interpretation of Qur’anic language.
items.works: ʿArāʾis al-bayān fī ḥaqāʾiq al-Qurʾān; Sharḥ-i Shaṭḥiyyāt; Mashrab al-arwāḥ

items.title: al-Marghinani
items.fullName: Burhan al-Din ʿAlī ibn Abī Bakr al-Marghīnānī
items.description: Burhān al-Dīn al-Marghīnānī was a leading Ḥanafī jurist whose concise manual became one of the school’s most influential legal texts. Its treatment of worship, commerce, family law, and judicial matters generated a vast commentary tradition.
items.works: Al-Hidāya fī sharḥ Bidāyat al-mubtadī; Bidāyat al-mubtadī;

items.title: Farid al-Din Attar
items.fullName: Farīd al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ʿAṭṭār
items.description: Farīd al-Dīn ʿAṭṭār was a Persian Sufi poet whose allegorical narratives became classics of Persian literature. He used stories of saints, birds, and spiritual travelers to explore the soul’s search for divine truth and the stages of the mystical path.
items.works: Manṭiq al-ṭayr; Ilāhī-nāma; Asrār-nāma; Tadhkirat al-awliyāʾ; Muṣībat-nāma

items.title: Najm al-Din al-Kubra
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Khīwaqī al-Khwārazmī, Najm al-Dīn al-Kubrā
items.description: Najm al-Dīn al-Kubrā was a major Khwarazmian Sufi master and founder of the Kubrawiyya, known for analyses of spiritual experience and visionary perception. His school influenced Persianate mysticism and later theories of subtle spiritual centers.
items.works: Fawāʾiḥ al-jamāl wa-fawātiḥ al-jalāl; al-Uṣūl al-ʿashara; Ādāb al-ṣūfiyya
