items.title: Umar al-Suhrawardi
items.fullName: Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar al-Suhrawardī
items.description: ʿUmar al-Suhrawardī was a Shāfiʿī scholar and Sufi theorist who systematized the etiquette and organization of the Sufi path. His manual became one of the most influential handbooks of institutional Sufism across the Muslim world.
items.works: ʿAwārif al-maʿārif

items.title: Ibn Qudama
items.fullName: Muwaffaq al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Qudāma al-Maqdisī
items.description: Ibn Qudāma was a leading Ḥanbalī jurist and theologian whose works became standard references for the school. His accessible legal manuals, comparative fiqh, and defenses of traditionalist creed influenced generations of Sunni scholars.
items.works: Al-Mughnī; al-Kāfī; ʿUmdat al-fiqh; Lumʿat al-iʿtiqād; Rawḍat al-nāẓir

items.title: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Rāzī, Fakhr al-Dīn
items.description: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī was a major Ashʿarī theologian, Qur’anic exegete, and philosopher who brought rigorous philosophical argument into Sunni kalām. His expansive tafsīr explores language, law, theology, and natural philosophy and shaped later intellectual traditions.
items.works: Mafātīḥ al-ghayb (al-Tafsīr al-kabīr); al-Maḥṣūl fī ʿilm uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Muḥaṣṣal; al-Mabāḥith al-mashriqiyya

items.title: Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabash al-Suhrawardī al-Maqtūl, Shihāb al-Dīn
items.description: Shihāb al-Dīn al-Suhrawardī, the “Master of Illumination,” founded the Illuminationist (Ishrāqī) philosophical tradition, combining rational inquiry with an epistemology of light and spiritual realization. His ideas deeply influenced later Persian philosophy.
items.works: Ḥikmat al-ishrāq; Ḥayākil al-nūr; ʿAql-i surkh; al-Talwīḥāt; al-Muqāwamāt

items.title: al-Amidi
items.fullName: Sayf al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Abī ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Āmidī
items.description: Al-Āmidī was a Shāfiʿī jurist and theologian who became one of the most technically sophisticated scholars of uṣūl al-fiqh and kalām. His comparative method engaged competing schools and influenced later legal theorists.
items.works: Al-Iḥkām fī uṣūl al-aḥkām; Abkār al-afkār; Ghāyat al-marām fī ʿilm al-kalām

items.title: Ibn al-Athir
items.fullName: ʿIzz al-Dīn Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, Ibn al-Athīr
items.description: Ibn al-Athīr was a historian and scholar from Mosul whose universal chronicle is among the most important narrative histories of the medieval Islamic world. He also compiled a major dictionary of hadith vocabulary.
items.works: Al-Kāmil fī al-tārīkh; Usd al-ghāba fī maʿrifat al-ṣaḥāba; al-Nihāya fī gharīb al-ḥadīth wa-l-athar

items.title: al-Rafii
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Rāfiʿī al-Qazwīnī
items.description: Al-Rāfiʿī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist whose comprehensive commentary on al-Ghazālī’s legal summary helped define the school’s authoritative doctrine. His work, together with al-Nawawī’s, became central to later Shāfiʿī legal practice.
items.works: Al-ʿAzīz sharḥ al-Wajīz; al-Muḥarrar; Sharḥ Musnad al-Shāfiʿī

items.title: Abd al-Latif al-Baghdadi
items.fullName: Muwaffaq al-Dīn Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Laṭīf ibn Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Saʿd al-Baghdādī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Laṭīf al-Baghdādī was a polymath physician, philosopher, philologist, and traveler who wrote on medicine, natural history, and intellectual life. His observations on Egypt and the classical sciences offer a distinctive view of medieval scholarship.
items.works: Al-Ifāda wa-l-iʿtibār; Kitāb al-Insān; works on medicine, philosophy, and Aristotle

items.title: Ibn Arabi
items.fullName: Muḥyī al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArabī al-Ḥātimī al-Ṭāʾī
items.description: Ibn ʿArabī was an Andalusian mystic and metaphysician whose writings reshaped Sufi thought through analyses of divine self-disclosure, spiritual knowledge, and the relationship between God and creation. His enormous influence inspired both devoted followers and critics.
items.works: Al-Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya; Fuṣūṣ al-ḥikam; Tarjumān al-ashwāq; Inshāʾ al-dawāʾir

items.title: Ibn al-Salah
items.fullName: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān al-Shahrazūrī, Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ
items.description: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ was a leading Shāfiʿī hadith scholar whose lectures became the standard framework for the technical sciences of hadith. His classification of hadith terminology shaped nearly all later introductory manuals in the field.
items.works: Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ fī ʿulūm al-ḥadīth; Fatāwā Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ; Sharḥ Mushkil al-Wasīṭ

items.title: Ibn al-Farid
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Fāriḍ al-Ḥamawī
items.description: Ibn al-Fāriḍ was an Egyptian Sufi poet whose Arabic verse became among the most celebrated expressions of mystical love. His long poem on the spiritual wine of divine love has been extensively commented upon across Sufi traditions.
items.works: Dīwān Ibn al-Fāriḍ; Naẓm al-sulūk (al-Tāʾiyya al-kubrā); al-Khamriyya

items.title: Shams al-Din al-Tabrizi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Malikdād al-Tabrīzī, Shams al-Dīn
items.description: Shams al-Dīn al-Tabrīzī was a wandering mystic whose encounter with Jalāl al-Dīn Rūmī transformed the latter’s spiritual and poetic life. His remembered teachings emphasize love, direct spiritual insight, and freedom from religious formalism devoid of inner life.
items.works: Maqālāt-i Shams-i Tabrīzī (discourses compiled by disciples)

items.title: Afdal al-Din al-Khunaji
items.fullName: Afḍal al-Dīn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī al-Khūnajī
items.description: Afḍal al-Dīn al-Khūnajī was a philosopher and logician who helped develop post-Avicennian logic and influenced later Islamic philosophical curricula. His writings examined demonstration, definition, and the structure of scientific knowledge.
items.works: Kashf al-asrār ʿan ghawāmiḍ al-afkār; al-Jumal fī al-manṭiq; treatises on logic

items.title: Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Shādhilī
items.description: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī was a North African Sufi master and founder of the Shādhiliyya, a major order emphasizing remembrance of God, inward reliance, and spiritual life within ordinary society. His teaching influenced devotional practice across the Islamic world.
items.works: Ḥizb al-Baḥr and other prayers attributed to him; teachings preserved by disciples, especially in Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh’s works

items.title: Siraj al-Din al-Urmawi
items.fullName: Sirāj al-Dīn Maḥmūd ibn Abī Bakr al-Urmawī
items.description: Sirāj al-Dīn al-Urmawī was a Shāfiʿī jurist, judge, and logician whose works advanced the technical study of logic and legal theory. He held important judicial offices and was influential in the intellectual culture of Anatolia.
items.works: Maṭāliʿ al-anwār fī al-manṭiq; Bayān al-ḥaqq; treatises on logic and uṣūl

items.title: Ahmad al-Badawi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Badawī
items.description: Aḥmad al-Badawī was an Egyptian Sufi saint whose cult and the Aḥmadiyya (Badawiyya) order became prominent in Mamluk and later Egypt. His legacy is chiefly devotional and hagiographical; reliable details of his life remain limited.
items.works: No securely authenticated authored work; prayers and teachings preserved in Badawī devotional traditions

items.title: al-Abhari
items.fullName: Athīr al-Dīn al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar al-Abharī
items.description: Al-Abharī was a logician, philosopher, and astronomer whose concise manuals shaped elementary and intermediate logic in Islamic madrasas. His works were widely commented on across the Ottoman, Persian, and South Asian scholarly worlds.
items.works: Īsāghūjī (logic); Kashf al-ḥaqāʾiq; Hidāyat al-ḥikma

items.title: Ibn Usfur
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Muʾmin ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUṣfūr al-Ishbīlī
items.description: Ibn ʿUṣfūr was a leading Andalusian grammarian whose works on Arabic syntax and morphology contributed to the western Arabic grammatical tradition. He was especially known for his detailed analysis of grammatical structure and disputes.
items.works: Al-Mumtiʿ al-kabīr fī al-taṣrīf; Sharḥ Jumal al-Zajjājī; works on Arabic grammar

items.title: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, Naṣīr al-Dīn
items.description: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī was a Persian polymath in philosophy, theology, mathematics, and astronomy. He made major contributions to astronomical modeling and helped establish the Maragha observatory, while his ethical and theological works remained influential.
items.works: Akhlāq-i Nāṣirī; Tajrīd al-iʿtiqād; al-Tadhkira fī ʿilm al-hayʾa; Zīj-i Īlkhānī; Sharḥ al-Ishārāt

items.title: Ibn Malik
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik al-Ṭāʾī al-Jayyānī
items.description: Ibn Mālik was an Andalusian-born grammarian whose concise verse on Arabic grammar became one of the most influential teaching texts in the Arabic curriculum. His work generated extensive commentary and remains studied in traditional institutions.
items.works: Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik; Tashīl al-fawāʾid wa-takmīl al-maqāṣid; Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl

items.title: Najm al-Din al-Katibi
items.fullName: Najm al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Kātibī al-Qazwīnī
items.description: Najm al-Dīn al-Kātibī was a Persian logician and philosopher whose manuals shaped the teaching of logic and metaphysics. His works were widely studied and commented upon in later Islamic philosophy and madrasa education.
items.works: Al-Risāla al-shamsiyya fī al-qawāʿid al-manṭiqiyya; Ḥikmat al-ʿayn

items.title: Jalal al-Din Rumi
items.fullName: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Balkhī, known as Rūmī
items.description: Jalāl al-Dīn Rūmī was a Persian-language Sufi poet and teacher whose verse expresses divine love, spiritual transformation, and the soul’s return to its source. His poetry and the Mevlevi tradition have had lasting influence across cultures.
items.works: Mathnawī-yi maʿnawī; Dīvān-i Shams; Fīhi mā fīh; Majālis-i sabʿa; Maktūbāt

items.title: al-Qunawi
items.fullName: Ṣadr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Qūnawī
items.description: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī was Ibn ʿArabī’s foremost philosophical disciple and a key systematizer of Akbarian metaphysics. His writings clarified the relation between divine knowledge, existence, and mystical realization and influenced later Ottoman and Persian Sufism.
items.works: Miftāḥ al-ghayb; Iʿjāz al-bayān fī taʾwīl umm al-Qurʾān; al-Nuṣūṣ

items.title: Haji Bektash
items.fullName: Ḥājjī Bektaş Velī
items.description: Ḥājjī Bektaş was a revered Anatolian mystic and spiritual namesake of the Bektashi tradition. His historical biography is difficult to separate from later hagiography, but the tradition associated with him had a major role in Anatolian and Ottoman religious culture.
items.works: Maqālāt (attributed); Vilāyet-nāma is a later hagiography, not his own work

items.title: Saadi al-Shirazi
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad Muṣliḥ al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Shīrāzī, Saʿdī
items.description: Saʿdī al-Shīrāzī was a celebrated Persian poet and prose writer whose ethical tales explore justice, wisdom, humility, and human conduct. His works became central to Persian literary education and circulated widely in translation.
items.works: Būstān; Gulistān; Dīvān; ghazals and qaṣīdas

items.title: al-Busiri
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd al-Būṣīrī
items.description: Al-Būṣīrī was an Egyptian poet famous for his devotional praise of the Prophet. His poem al-Burda became one of the most widely recited and commented-upon works in Muslim devotional literature.
items.works: Qaṣīdat al-Burda; Hamziyya; Dīwān al-Būṣīrī

items.title: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi
items.fullName: Fakhr al-Dīn Ibrāhīm ʿIrāqī
items.description: Fakhr al-Dīn ʿIrāqī was a Persian Sufi poet and prose writer associated with the school of Ibn ʿArabī. His writings unite poetic love imagery with metaphysical reflection and became influential in Persian and Indo-Muslim Sufi traditions.
items.works: Lamaʿāt; ʿUshshāq-nāma; Dīvān

items.title: Afif al-Din al-Tilimsani
items.fullName: ʿAfīf al-Dīn Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī al-Tilimsānī
items.description: ʿAfīf al-Dīn al-Tilimsānī was a Maghribi Sufi poet and commentator associated with Akbarian metaphysics. His writings expressed an uncompromising vision of divine unity and drew both admiration and criticism from later theologians.
items.works: Commentaries on Ibn al-Fāriḍ’s poetry and Ibn ʿArabī’s Fuṣūṣ; Dīwān (attributed)

items.title: al-Qurtubi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abī Bakr al-Anṣārī al-Qurṭubī
items.description: Al-Qurṭubī was an Andalusian-born Mālikī jurist and Qur’anic exegete whose comprehensive commentary is a major reference for legal and linguistic interpretation of the Qur’an. He spent much of his later life in Egypt.
items.works: Al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān; al-Tadhkira bi-aḥwāl al-mawtā wa-umūr al-ākhira; al-Asnā fī sharḥ asmāʾ Allāh al-ḥusnā

items.title: Zahid Gilani
items.fullName: Tāj al-Dīn Ibrāhīm ibn Rūshan Amīr al-Kurdī al-Sanjānī, Zāhid Gīlānī
items.description: Zāhid Gīlānī was a Persian Sufi master traditionally linked to the spiritual lineage of Ṣafī al-Dīn Ardabīlī and the later Safavid order. His significance lies largely in Sufi lineage traditions rather than a clearly preserved authored corpus.
items.works: No reliably authenticated independent work; sayings and lineage accounts preserved in Safavid Sufi sources

items.title: al-Qarafi
items.fullName: Shihāb al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn Idrīs al-Qarāfī
items.description: Al-Qarāfī was a leading Mālikī jurist and legal theorist in Mamluk Egypt. His work on legal maxims, the objectives and subtleties of jurisprudence, and distinctions between legal cases became highly influential in later Mālikī thought.
items.works: Al-Furūq; al-Dhakhīra; Sharḥ Tanqīḥ al-fuṣūl; al-Iḥkām fī tamyīz al-fatāwā ʿan al-aḥkām

items.title: al-Nawawi
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Sharaf al-Nawawī
items.description: Al-Nawawī was a highly influential Shāfiʿī jurist and hadith scholar whose concise manuals and ethical collections are read throughout the Sunni world. His commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and works on hadith and law became standard references.
items.works: Riyāḍ al-ṣāliḥīn; al-Arbaʿūn al-Nawawiyya; al-Majmūʿ; Minhāj al-ṭālibīn; Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; al-Adhkār

items.title: Ibn Sabin
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Naṣr al-Ishbīlī, Ibn Sabʿīn
items.description: Ibn Sabʿīn was an Andalusian philosopher and mystic whose writings pursued metaphysical unity and engaged critically with Aristotelian philosophy. His thought represents an unusual strand of medieval Islamic speculation, often contested by other scholars.
items.works: Bud al-ʿārif; al-Risāla al-nuṣayriyya; responses to the Sicilian Questions

items.title: Qutb al-Din al-Shirazi
items.fullName: Quṭb al-Dīn Maḥmūd ibn Masʿūd al-Shīrāzī
items.description: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī was a Persian polymath in philosophy, medicine, astronomy, and mathematics. He wrote influential commentaries on Avicenna and Suhrawardī and contributed to scientific discussions of optics and celestial models.
items.works: Durrat al-tāj li-ghurrat al-dībāj; Sharḥ Ḥikmat al-ishrāq; Nihāyat al-idrāk fī dirāyat al-aflāk; al-Tuḥfa al-saʿdiyya

items.title: Yunus Emre
items.fullName: Yūnus Emre
items.description: Yūnus Emre was a pioneering Anatolian Turkish Sufi poet whose plain, lyrical language made profound themes of divine love, unity, and humility accessible to ordinary people. His verse remains central to Turkish devotional and literary culture.
items.works: Dīvān; Risālat al-nuṣḥiyya (attributed; manuscript and textual traditions vary)

items.title: al-Baydawi
items.fullName: Nāṣir al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Bayḍāwī
items.description: Al-Bayḍāwī was a Shāfiʿī jurist and Qur’anic exegete whose concise tafsīr became a standard text in madrasas across the Muslim world. Its synthesis of earlier commentary, grammar, and theology inspired numerous supercommentaries.
items.works: Anwār al-tanzīl wa-asrār al-taʾwīl; Minhāj al-wuṣūl ilā ʿilm al-uṣūl; Ṭawāliʿ al-anwār

items.title: Amir Khusraw
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan Yamīn al-Dīn Khusraw Dehlawī, Amīr Khusraw
items.description: Amīr Khusraw was an Indo-Persian poet, musician, and court intellectual whose Persian poetry and Hindavi compositions helped shape South Asian literary and musical cultures. He is also remembered for his association with the Chishti Sufi master Niẓām al-Dīn Awliyāʾ.
items.works: Khamsa; Qirān al-saʿdayn; Nuh sipihr; Tughluq-nāma; historical mas̱navīs and ghazals

items.title: Ibrahim al-Dasuqi
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Dasūqī
items.description: Ibrāhīm al-Dasūqī was an Egyptian Sufi master and the eponym of the Dasūqiyya order. His legacy is primarily devotional and institutional, with later hagiographic sources preserving the teachings attributed to him.
items.works: No securely authenticated authored works; prayers and teachings transmitted in Dasūqī Sufi tradition

items.title: Ibn Ata' Allah
items.fullName: Tāj al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh al-Iskandarī
items.description: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh al-Iskandarī was a Shādhilī Sufi teacher and author who articulated a profound yet practical spirituality centered on reliance on God, sincerity, and inner transformation. His aphorisms remain among the most widely read Sufi texts.
items.works: Al-Ḥikam al-ʿAṭāʾiyya; Laṭāʾif al-minan; Miftāḥ al-falāḥ; al-Tanwīr fī isqāṭ al-tadbīr

items.title: al-Qaysari
items.fullName: Dāwūd ibn Maḥmūd al-Qayṣarī
items.description: Dāwūd al-Qayṣarī was an Ottoman-era philosopher and Sufi commentator who helped systematize Ibn ʿArabī’s metaphysics in Anatolia. His commentaries became influential in the intellectual foundations of early Ottoman Sufism.
items.works: Muqaddima to Sharḥ Fuṣūṣ al-ḥikam; Maṭlaʿ khuṣūṣ al-kilam; Nihāyat al-bayān fī dirāyat al-zamān

items.title: Ibn Taymiyya
items.fullName: Taqī al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥalīm ibn ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Numayrī al-Ḥarrānī, Ibn Taymiyya
items.description: Ibn Taymiyya was a Ḥanbalī jurist and theologian whose scripturalist reformism challenged several established theological and devotional practices. His extensive writings on creed, law, philosophy, and politics have had a major and contested influence on later Islamic movements.
items.works: Majmūʿ al-fatāwā; Darʾ taʿāruḍ al-ʿaql wa-l-naql; Minhāj al-sunna; al-ʿAqīda al-Wāsiṭiyya; Iqtiḍāʾ al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm

items.title: Ibn Ajurrum
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd al-Ṣanhājī
items.description: Ibn Ājurrūm was a Moroccan grammarian whose compact introduction to Arabic syntax became one of the most widely taught grammar texts in the Muslim world. Its clarity made it a foundational step in traditional Arabic education.
items.works: Al-Muqaddima al-Ājurrūmiyya

items.title: al-Dhahabi
items.fullName: Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān al-Dhahabī
items.description: Al-Dhahabī was a leading Mamluk-era hadith critic and historian known for evaluating transmitters, chronicling scholars, and synthesizing Islamic history. His biographical works remain indispensable references for the study of Islamic intellectual life.
items.works: Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ; Tārīkh al-Islām; Mīzān al-iʿtidāl; Tadhkirat al-ḥuffāẓ; al-Kāshif fī maʿrifat man lahu riwāya fī al-kutub al-sitta

items.title: Adud al-Din al-Iji
items.fullName: ʿAḍud al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad al-Ījī
items.description: ʿAḍud al-Dīn al-Ījī was a major Ashʿarī theologian, logician, and jurist whose concise works became central to post-classical Islamic scholarship. His manuals prompted extensive commentary and shaped theological education in Ottoman and other scholarly settings.
items.works: Al-Mawāqif fī ʿilm al-kalām; al-ʿAqāʾid al-ʿAḍudiyya; al-Risāla al-Shāhiyya

items.title: Taqi al-Din al-Subki
items.fullName: Taqī al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Kāfī al-Subkī
items.description: Taqī al-Dīn al-Subkī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist, hadith scholar, and Ashʿarī theologian in Mamluk Syria. He defended Sunni devotional practice and wrote extensively on legal and theological controversy, leaving a major scholarly family legacy.
items.works: Al-Sayf al-ṣaqīl fī al-radd ʿalā Ibn Zafīl; al-Ibhāj fī sharḥ al-Minhāj; Fatāwā al-Subkī

items.title: Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyya
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ayyūb ibn Saʿd al-Zurʿī al-Dimashqī, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya
items.description: Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyya was a Ḥanbalī scholar and close student of Ibn Taymiyya who wrote extensively on theology, law, spirituality, and ethics. His works combine scriptural argument with psychological and devotional insight and remain widely read.
items.works: Zād al-maʿād; Madārij al-sālikīn; Iʿlām al-muwaqqiʿīn; al-Dāʾ wa-l-dawāʾ; Miftāḥ dār al-saʿāda

items.title: Ibn Juzayy
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā ibn Juzayy al-Kalbī
items.description: Ibn Juzayy was a Granadan Mālikī jurist, Qur’anic exegete, and literary scholar. His concise tafsīr combines transmitted reports, language, legal questions, and readings and has been widely used in Qur’anic education.
items.works: Al-Tashīl li-ʿulūm al-tanzīl; al-Qawānīn al-fiqhiyya; al-Mukhtaṣar fī uṣūl al-dīn

items.title: Sadr al-Sharia al-Thani
items.fullName: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Masʿūd al-Maḥbūbī, Ṣadr al-Sharīʿa
items.description: Ṣadr al-Sharīʿa was a Ḥanafī jurist and theologian whose works systematized law, legal theory, and logic in the post-classical period. His manual became especially important in Ottoman and Central Asian scholarly curricula.
items.works: Al-Tawḍīḥ fī ḥall ghawāmiḍ al-Tanqīḥ; Sharḥ Wiqāyat al-riwāya; Taʿdīl al-ʿulūm

items.title: Ibn Kathir
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUmar ibn Kathīr al-Qurashī al-Dimashqī
items.description: Ibn Kathīr was a Syrian Shāfiʿī historian and Qur’anic exegete whose tafsīr became one of the most widely circulated Sunni commentaries. His universal history and biography of the Prophet remain influential sources for traditional Islamic historiography.
items.works: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm; al-Bidāya wa-l-nihāya; al-Sīra al-nabawiyya; Ikhtiṣār ʿulūm al-ḥadīth

items.title: Ibn Battuta
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Lawātī al-Ṭanjī
items.description: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa was a Moroccan traveler whose journeys across Africa, Asia, and parts of Europe provide an extraordinary account of the fourteenth-century Islamic world. His travel narrative records courts, scholars, trade networks, and social customs.
items.works: Tuḥfat al-nuẓẓār fī gharāʾib al-amṣār wa-ʿajāʾib al-asfār (the Riḥla, dictated to Ibn Juzayy)

items.title: Ibn Hisham al-Ansari
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
items.description: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī was a major Egyptian grammarian whose precise analyses of Arabic syntax and morphology became standard in traditional education. His works are known for clarity, systematic organization, and lasting influence on grammatical commentary.
items.works: Mughnī al-labīb ʿan kutub al-aʿārīb; Qaṭr al-nadā wa-ball al-ṣadā; Sharḥ Shudhūr al-dhahab

items.title: al-Babarti
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Maḥmūd al-Bābartī
items.description: Al-Bābartī was a leading Ḥanafī jurist and theologian whose commentaries became influential in Mamluk and early Ottoman scholarly circles. His works engaged legal theory, creed, and philosophy and remained part of advanced madrasa curricula.
items.works: Al-ʿInāya sharḥ al-Hidāya; Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya; al-Radd ʿalā al-Qāʾilīn bi-waḥdat al-wujūd (attributed)

items.title: Ibn Arafa
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa al-Warghammī
items.description: Ibn ʿArafa was a leading Mālikī jurist and teacher in Hafsid Tunis whose opinions influenced North African legal practice. His precise and demanding scholarship helped consolidate the Mālikī tradition in the Maghrib.
items.works: Al-Mukhtaṣar al-fiqhī; tafsīr and legal lessons preserved through students and later commentaries

items.title: Baha al-Din Naqshband
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad Bahāʾ al-Dīn al-Naqshband
items.description: Bahāʾ al-Dīn Naqshband was the eponymous master of the Naqshbandiyya, one of the most influential Sunni Sufi orders. The tradition associated with him emphasized silent remembrance, sober spiritual discipline, and engagement with communal life.
items.works: No authenticated authored book; sayings and principles preserved in Naqshbandi manuals

items.title: Abu Ishaq al-Shatibi
items.fullName: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad al-Lakhmī al-Shāṭibī
items.description: Al-Shāṭibī was an Andalusian Mālikī jurist and Qur’anic scholar whose work on the higher objectives of Islamic law became foundational for maqāṣid al-sharīʿa. His writings also shaped Qur’anic recitation and legal theory.
items.works: Al-Muwāfaqāt fī uṣūl al-sharīʿa; al-Iʿtiṣām;

items.title: al-Taftazani
items.fullName: Saʿd al-Dīn Masʿūd ibn ʿUmar al-Taftāzānī
items.description: Al-Taftāzānī was a Persian theologian, logician, and rhetorician whose commentaries became central to post-classical Islamic education. His works synthesized complex debates in theology, legal theory, grammar, and rhetoric for later scholars.
items.works: Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya; Tahdhīb al-manṭiq wa-l-kalām; al-Muṭawwal; Mukhtaṣar al-maʿānī; al-Talwīḥ

items.title: Hafez
items.fullName: Khwāja Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad Ḥāfiẓ Shīrāzī
items.description: Ḥāfiẓ of Shiraz was one of the greatest Persian lyric poets, celebrated for ghazals that intertwine wine imagery, love, irony, and spiritual ambiguity. His Dīvān became a source of literary imitation, divination practices, and Sufi interpretation.
items.works: Dīvān-i Ḥāfiẓ

items.title: Taj al-Din al-Subki
items.fullName: Tāj al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAlī al-Subkī
items.description: Tāj al-Dīn al-Subkī was a Shāfiʿī jurist, hadith scholar, theologian, and historian who documented the scholars and intellectual institutions of his era. His works are major sources for the development of Sunni legal and theological schools.
items.works: Ṭabaqāt al-Shāfiʿiyya al-kubrā; Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ; Rafʿ al-ḥājib ʿan Mukhtaṣar Ibn al-Ḥājib

items.title: Ibn Abi al-Izz
items.fullName: Ṣadr al-Dīn Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Dimashqī, Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz
items.description: Ibn Abī al-ʿIzz was a Ḥanafī judge and theologian best known for his commentary on al-Ṭaḥāwī’s creed. His interpretation later became especially influential among modern Salafi writers and generated significant scholarly debate.
items.works: Sharḥ al-ʿAqīda al-Ṭaḥāwiyya; al-Tanbīh ʿalā mushkilāt al-Hidāya

items.title: Ibn Khaldun
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Khaldūn al-Ḥaḍramī
items.description: Ibn Khaldūn was a North African historian and social thinker whose Muqaddima analyzed society, political authority, economic life, and the rise and decline of dynasties. His theory of ʿaṣabiyya made him a foundational figure in historiography and social theory.
items.works: Al-Muqaddima; Kitāb al-ʿIbar; al-Taʿrīf bi-Ibn Khaldūn (autobiography)

items.title: Ibn Rajab
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn Rajab al-Salāmī al-Baghdādī
items.description: Ibn Rajab was a Ḥanbalī hadith scholar and spiritual writer known for connecting Prophetic reports with ethical and devotional lessons. His commentaries and studies of early Muslim generations remain widely read in Sunni circles.
items.works: Jāmiʿ al-ʿulūm wa-l-ḥikam; Fatḥ al-Bārī (commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, incomplete); Laṭāʾif al-maʿārif; Dhayl Ṭabaqāt al-Ḥanābila

items.title: al-Sharif al-Jurjani
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
items.description: Al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī was a Persian theologian, logician, and lexicographer whose concise definitions and commentaries became fundamental references in post-classical Islamic scholarship. His works influenced Ottoman and South Asian madrasa curricula.
items.works: Al-Taʿrīfāt; Sharḥ al-Mawāqif; Ḥāshiya on al-Muṭawwal; treatises on logic and theology

items.title: al-Fanari
items.fullName: Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Ḥamza al-Fanārī
items.description: Al-Fanārī was an early Ottoman scholar of theology, logic, and legal theory who helped establish the intellectual curriculum of the Ottoman learned class. His commentaries shaped later study of logic and metaphysics.
items.works: Miṣbāḥ al-uns; Fuṣūl al-badāʾiʿ fī uṣūl al-sharāʾiʿ; commentary on Īsāghūjī

items.title: Abd al-Karim al-Jili
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Ibrāhīm al-Jīlī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jīlī was a Sufi metaphysician associated with the Akbarian tradition. His treatment of the Perfect Human developed and systematized themes from Ibn ʿArabī, influencing later Sufi metaphysics and devotional thought.
items.works: Al-Insān al-kāmil fī maʿrifat al-awākhir wa-l-awāʾil; al-Kahf wa-l-raqīm; al-Manāẓir al-ilāhiyya

items.title: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
items.description: Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī was a preeminent Shāfiʿī jurist and hadith scholar whose commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī became the standard reference for Sunni hadith study. His biographical and critical works remain central to Islamic scholarship.
items.works: Fatḥ al-Bārī; al-Iṣāba fī tamyīz al-ṣaḥāba; Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb; Bulūgh al-marām; Nukhbat al-fikar

items.title: Kamal al-Din Ibn al-Humam
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Siwāsī, Kamāl al-Dīn Ibn al-Humām
items.description: Kamāl al-Dīn Ibn al-Humām was a major Ḥanafī jurist and theologian whose commentaries and treatises addressed law, legal theory, and creed. His work became influential in Ottoman-era Ḥanafī scholarship.
items.works: Fatḥ al-qadīr; al-Taḥrīr fī uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Musāyara fī al-ʿaqāʾid al-munjiya

items.title: Ali Qushji
items.fullName: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qūshjī
items.description: ʿAlī Qūshjī was a Timurid-Ottoman astronomer, mathematician, and theologian whose works advanced astronomy and helped renew mathematical study in Ottoman institutions. His commentaries also shaped the teaching of logic and theology.
items.works: Al-Risāla al-Fatḥiyya; Sharḥ al-Tajrīd; treatises on astronomy and mathematics

items.title: Ala' al-Din al-Tusi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭūsī, ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn
items.description: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī was a theologian and philosopher known for his critique of Ibn Sīnā’s metaphysics and for engaging post-Avicennian debates. His writings formed part of the rich intellectual environment of fifteenth-century Iran and Anatolia.
items.works: Tahāfut al-falāsifa; Ḥāshiya on al-Tajrīd; works on kalām and philosophy

items.title: Mulla Jami
items.fullName: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Jāmī
items.description: Mullā Jāmī was a major Persian poet, Sufi thinker, and scholar of grammar and theology at the Timurid court. His poetry and prose synthesized Persian literary tradition with Akbarian Sufism and influenced Ottoman, Persian, and South Asian culture.
items.works: Haft awrang; Nafahāt al-uns; Lawāʾiḥ; Sharḥ-i Fuṣūṣ al-ḥikam; Bahāristān

items.title: Zakariyya al-Ansari
items.fullName: Zakariyyā ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī
items.description: Zakariyyā al-Anṣārī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī jurist, hadith scholar, and judge whose commentaries became standard references in the school. His long scholarly career helped stabilize late medieval Shāfiʿī teaching and legal practice.
items.works: Asnā al-maṭālib; Fatḥ al-Wahhāb; Tuḥfat al-bārī; Sharḥ al-Bahja al-wardiyya

items.title: al-Dawwani
items.fullName: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Asʿad al-Dawwānī
items.description: Al-Dawwānī was a Persian philosopher, theologian, and ethicist whose works combined Avicennian philosophy, illuminationist themes, and Islamic theology. His treatises were widely studied in the Ottoman, Safavid, and South Asian intellectual traditions.
items.works: Akhlāq-i Jalālī; Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-ʿAḍudiyya; Risāla fī ithbāt al-wājib

items.title: al-Sakhawi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sakhāwī
items.description: Al-Sakhāwī was a leading Shāfiʿī hadith scholar and historian of Mamluk Egypt, renowned for biographical dictionaries and studies of hadith transmitters. His works preserve vital information about scholars, institutions, and intellectual life.
items.works: Al-Ḍawʾ al-lāmiʿ li-ahl al-qarn al-tāsiʿ; Fatḥ al-mughīth; al-Maqāṣid al-ḥasana; al-Jawāhir wa-l-durar

items.title: Muslih al-Din Khwajazade
items.fullName: Muṣliḥ al-Dīn Muṣṭafā ibn Yūsuf Khwājazāda
items.description: Muṣliḥ al-Dīn Khwājazāda was an Ottoman scholar of theology and philosophy remembered for participating in debates over the relative merits of al-Ghazālī and Ibn Rushd. His work reflects Ottoman engagement with the classical philosophical and theological canon.
items.works: Tahāfut al-falāsifa (Ottoman treatise in the tahāfut debate); theological and philosophical writings, some incompletely preserved

items.title: Ahmad Zarruq
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Barnūsī al-Fāsī, Zarrūq
items.description: Aḥmad Zarrūq was a Moroccan Mālikī jurist and Sufi whose writings sought to reconcile spiritual discipline with sound law and theology. His maxims on Sufism became influential in North and West African religious education.
items.works: Qawāʿid al-taṣawwuf; Sharḥ Ḥikam Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh; Naṣīḥat al-murīdīn

items.title: al-Suyuti
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Suyūṭī
items.description: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī was an extraordinarily prolific Egyptian Shāfiʿī scholar whose works span Qur’anic exegesis, hadith, law, history, grammar, and literary studies. His concise compilations became widely used references in traditional Islamic learning.
items.works: Al-Itqān fī ʿulūm al-Qurʾān; Tafsīr al-Jalālayn (completed); al-Durr al-manthūr; Jāmiʿ al-ṣaghīr; Tadrīb al-rāwī; al-Muzhir

items.title: al-Qastallani
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Qasṭallānī
items.description: Al-Qasṭallānī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī scholar best known for his commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and his writings on the Prophet’s life and qualities. His works became important references in hadith and sīra study.
items.works: Irshād al-sārī li-sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī; al-Mawāhib al-laduniyya; Laṭāʾif al-ishārāt

items.title: Ibrahim al-Halabi
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥalabī
items.description: Ibrāhīm al-Ḥalabī was an Ottoman Ḥanafī jurist whose manual of worship and practical law became a standard reference in the Ottoman Empire and beyond. His work was influential in legal teaching and everyday religious practice.
items.works: Multaqā al-abḥur; Ghunyat al-mutamallī (Ḥalabī ṣaghīr); Sharḥ al-Munya

items.title: al-Dashtaki
items.fullName: Ghiyāth al-Dīn Manṣūr ibn Muḥammad al-Dashtakī
items.description: Al-Dashtakī was a Persian philosopher and theologian associated with the Shiraz school, known for engaging Avicennian and illuminationist philosophy. His family’s scholarship contributed to the intellectual culture of late medieval Iran.
items.works: Commentaries and glosses on philosophical texts, including works on al-Tajrīd and Illuminationist philosophy; exact attribution varies by family member

items.title: Ibn Kamal Pasha
items.fullName: Aḥmad Shams al-Dīn ibn Sulaymān ibn Kamāl Pāshā
items.description: Ibn Kamāl Pāshā was an Ottoman polymath, jurist, historian, and Shaykh al-Islām whose works helped shape Ottoman religious scholarship. He wrote on law, theology, Arabic, history, and philosophy and contributed to the institutional authority of the learned class.
items.works: Ṭabaqāt al-fuqahāʾ; Muḥīṭ al-lugha; treatises on theology and legal issues; Ottoman history works

items.title: Ebussuud Efendi
items.fullName: Abū al-Suʿūd Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muṣṭafā al-ʿImādī
items.description: Ebū's-Suʿūd Efendi was the Ottoman Shaykh al-Islām under Süleyman the Magnificent, a jurist and Qur’anic exegete who harmonized Ḥanafī jurisprudence with Ottoman imperial governance. His legal opinions and tafsīr were widely influential.
items.works: Irshād al-ʿaql al-salīm ilā mazāyā al-Kitāb al-karīm; fatwas (Fatāwā Ebüssuʿūd); maʿrūżāt

items.title: al-Sharani
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Aḥmad al-Shaʿrānī
items.description: Al-Shaʿrānī was an Egyptian Sufi, jurist, and prolific religious writer who sought to reconcile the legal schools with spiritual practice. His biographical works on Sufi masters became influential, though some of his historical claims are disputed.
items.works: Al-Ṭabaqāt al-kubrā (Lawāqiḥ al-anwār); al-Mīzān al-kubrā; al-Anwār al-qudsiyya; al-Yawāqīt wa-l-jawāhir

items.title: Fuzuli
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Fużūlī
items.description: Fużūlī was a major Azerbaijani-Turkish, Persian, and Arabic poet whose works explore love, longing, and spiritual pain. His lyrical and narrative poetry helped shape Ottoman and Azerbaijani literary traditions.
items.works: Leylī vü Mecnūn; Dīvān in Azerbaijani Turkish, Persian, and Arabic; Ḥadīqat al-suʿadāʾ; Ṣıḥḥat u maraż

items.title: Taskopruzade
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muṣṭafā Ṭāshköprüzāda
items.description: Ṭāshköprüzāda was an Ottoman scholar and historian of intellectual disciplines whose biographical encyclopedia organized the scholarly sciences and their practitioners. His work remains an important source for Ottoman and Islamic intellectual history.
items.works: Al-Shaqāʾiq al-nuʿmāniyya; Miftāḥ al-saʿāda wa-miṣbāḥ al-siyāda fī mawḍūʿāt al-ʿulūm

items.title: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī
items.description: Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist and legal authority in Mecca. His commentaries and fatwas became major references for later Shāfiʿī jurisprudence, especially in the late classical period.
items.works: Tuḥfat al-muḥtāj bi-sharḥ al-Minhāj; al-Zawājir ʿan iqtirāf al-kabāʾir; al-Fatāwā al-kubrā al-fiqhiyya

items.title: Shams al-Din al-Ramli
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Ramlī
items.description: Shams al-Dīn al-Ramlī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī jurist whose commentaries became among the leading authorities of the school. His works, together with those of Ibn Ḥajar al-Haytamī, helped define later Shāfiʿī legal doctrine.
items.works: Nihāyat al-muḥtāj ilā sharḥ al-Minhāj; Fatāwā al-Ramlī; Ghāyat al-bayān

items.title: al-Akhdari
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Akhḍarī
items.description: Al-Akhḍarī was a North African scholar whose concise didactic texts on logic and Mālikī jurisprudence were widely taught. His works became popular introductory manuals in traditional North and West African education.
items.works: Al-Sullam al-munawraq (logic); Mukhtaṣar al-Akhḍarī fī al-ʿibādāt; al-Qudūriyya al-sharḥ (attributions vary)

items.title: Ali al-Qari
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Sulṭān Muḥammad al-Qārī al-Harawī
items.description: ʿAlī al-Qārī was a Meccan Ḥanafī scholar and hadith commentator whose vast writings covered creed, law, Qur’anic recitation, and devotional practice. His works became influential across the Ottoman and South Asian scholarly worlds.
items.works: Mirqāt al-mafātīḥ sharḥ Mishkāt al-maṣābīḥ; Sharḥ al-Shifāʾ; al-Asrār al-marfūʿa; al-Fiqh al-akbar commentary

items.title: al-Birgivi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Pīr ʿAlī al-Birgīvī
items.description: Al-Birgīvī was an Ottoman Ḥanafī scholar and moral reformer who criticized religious abuses and emphasized sound creed, ethics, and proper practice. His accessible manuals became influential in Ottoman religious education.
items.works: Al-Ṭarīqa al-Muḥammadiyya; al-Ṭarīqa al-Muḥammadiyya wa-l-sīra al-Aḥmadiyya; Iẓhār al-asrār; Waṣiyyat-nāma

items.title: Aziz Mahmud Hudayi
items.fullName: ʿAzīz Maḥmūd Hüdāyî
items.description: ʿAzīz Maḥmūd Hüdāyî was an Ottoman Sufi master, jurist, and poet who founded the Celveti order and served as a respected spiritual adviser in Istanbul. His devotional works and hymns influenced Ottoman religious culture.
items.works: Dīvān; Nefāʾis al-majālis; Vaṣiyyet-nāme; prayers and treatises on spiritual discipline

items.title: al-Munawi
items.fullName: Zayn al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raʾūf ibn Tāj al-ʿĀrifīn al-Munāwī
items.description: Al-Munāwī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī scholar whose writings covered hadith, ethics, and the meanings of Prophetic traditions. His commentary on al-Suyūṭī’s collection became an important reference in hadith interpretation.
items.works: Fayḍ al-Qadīr sharḥ al-Jāmiʿ al-ṣaghīr; al-Taysīr bi-sharḥ al-Jāmiʿ al-ṣaghīr; al-Kawākib al-durriyya

items.title: Mir Damad
items.fullName: Muḥammad Bāqir Astarābādī, known as Mīr Dāmād
items.description: Mīr Dāmād was a Safavid philosopher and theologian who helped establish the School of Isfahan. His metaphysics of time and creation influenced his student Mullā Ṣadrā and shaped later Persian Islamic philosophy.
items.works: Al-Qabasāt; al-Ufuq al-mubīn; al-Ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm; philosophical glosses and treatises

items.title: Ahmad Sirhindi
items.fullName: Aḥmad al-Fārūqī al-Sirhindī
items.description: Aḥmad Sirhindī was an Indian Naqshbandi Sufi and religious reformer known for emphasizing the distinction between Creator and creation and critiquing certain interpretations of mystical unity. His letters became foundational for the Mujaddidiyya branch of the Naqshbandiyya.
items.works: Maktūbāt-i Imām Rabbānī; Ithbāt al-nubuwwa; Radd-i rawāfiḍ

items.title: Mulla Sadra
items.fullName: Ṣadr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Shīrāzī, Mullā Ṣadrā
items.description: Mullā Ṣadrā was a Persian philosopher who developed the transcendent theosophy (al-ḥikma al-mutaʿāliya), combining Avicennian philosophy, illuminationism, and Shiʿi metaphysics. His doctrines of substantial motion and the primacy of existence remain central in later Iranian philosophy.
items.works: Al-Asfār al-arbaʿa; al-Shawāhid al-rubūbiyya; al-Mashāʿir; al-Ḥikma al-ʿarshiyya; Tafsīr al-Qurʾān

items.title: al-Siyalkuti
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm al-Siyālkūtī
items.description: Al-Siyālkūtī was a South Asian theologian and logician whose commentaries became influential in the late post-classical madrasa curriculum. His work engaged complex debates in kalām, logic, and philosophy.
items.works: Ḥāshiya ʿalā Sharḥ al-ʿAqāʾid al-Nasafiyya; glosses on al-Bayḍāwī and logical texts

items.title: Ibn Ashir
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿĀshir al-Anṣārī
items.description: Ibn ʿĀshir was a Moroccan Mālikī scholar and Sufi whose concise didactic poem summarizes creed, law, and spiritual purification. It became a widely taught text in North and West African religious education.
items.works: Al-Murshid al-muʿīn ʿalā al-ḍarūrī min ʿulūm al-dīn (often called Matn Ibn ʿĀshir)

items.title: Muhammad al-Kharashi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Kharashī
items.description: Muḥammad al-Kharashī was an Egyptian Mālikī jurist and the first official Shaykh al-Azhar under that title. His commentaries helped codify and transmit Mālikī jurisprudence in Egypt and across the wider Sunni world.
items.works: Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar Khalīl; Ḥāshiya ʿalā al-Dardīr (attribution/editions vary); legal fatwas

items.title: al-Haddad
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlawī ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaddād
items.description: ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād was a Yemeni Hadrami Sufi scholar and poet whose devotional teachings helped shape the ʿAlawiyya tradition. His concise works on belief, worship, ethics, and remembrance remain widely read.
items.works: Risālat al-muʿāwana; al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-dīniyya; al-Daʿwa al-tāmma; Wird al-Laṭīf; Ratib al-Ḥaddād

items.title: Ahmed Beyazizade
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl Beyāzīzāda
items.description: Aḥmed Beyāzīzāda was an Ottoman Ḥanafī-Māturīdī theologian and jurist who wrote systematic works on creed and legal thought. His scholarship reflects the mature Ottoman synthesis of Māturīdī theology and Ḥanafī law.
items.works: Ishārāt al-marām min ʿibārāt al-Imām; Uṣūl al-munīfa li-l-Imām Abī Ḥanīfa; treatises on theology

items.title: Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulusi
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Ismāʿīl al-Nābulusī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Ghanī al-Nābulusī was a prolific Damascene Sufi, poet, jurist, and traveler associated with the Akbarian tradition. He wrote extensively on metaphysics, devotional practice, dream interpretation, and the permissibility of customary religious practices.
items.works: Al-Ḥaqīqa wa-l-majāz; Idāḥ al-maqṣūd min waḥdat al-wujūd; al-Ḥaḍra al-unsiyya; Dīwān

items.title: Ibrahim al-Kurani
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥasan al-Kūrānī
items.description: Ibrāhīm al-Kūrānī was a Kurdish-born scholar and Sufi based in Medina whose writings reconciled hadith-based theology with Akbarian metaphysics. He influenced major scholars in the Indian Ocean world, including students from Southeast Asia.
items.works: Al-Umam li-īqāẓ al-himam; Itḥāf al-khalaf bi-taḥqīq madhhab al-salaf; treatises on theology and Sufism

items.title: Ismail Haqqi Bursawi
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl Ḥaqqī ibn Muṣṭafā al-Bursawī
items.description: Ismāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursawī was an Ottoman Sufi, Qur’anic exegete, and poet associated with the Jalwati order. His extensive commentary joins linguistic analysis with mystical interpretation and became a major Ottoman tafsīr.
items.works: Rūḥ al-bayān fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān; Rūḥ al-mathnawī; al-Mabdaʾ wa-l-maʿād; Dīvān

items.title: Shah Wali Allah
items.fullName: Quṭb al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Dihlawī, Shāh Walī Allāh
items.description: Shāh Walī Allāh of Delhi was an influential Indian hadith scholar, theologian, and reformer who sought to reconcile legal schools and renew Muslim intellectual life. His writings on hadith, law, social order, and Qur’anic interpretation influenced South Asian reform movements.
items.works: Ḥujjat Allāh al-bāligha; al-Fawz al-kabīr fī uṣūl al-tafsīr; al-Musawwā; al-Muṣaffā; Izālat al-khafāʾ

items.title: Ibrahim Haqqi Erzurumi
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm Ḥaqqī Erzurūmī
items.description: Ibrāhīm Ḥaqqī Erzurūmī was an Ottoman-Turkish Sufi, scholar, and poet whose encyclopedic work joined theology, ethics, astronomy, and practical knowledge. His writings became popular for presenting religious and scientific learning in accessible form.
items.works: Maʿrifetnāme; Dīvān; İrfāniyye

items.title: Ahmad al-Dardir
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Dardīr
items.description: Aḥmad al-Dardīr was an Egyptian Mālikī jurist and Sufi whose legal manual and commentary became standard references in the school. His works were widely taught at al-Azhar and across North Africa.
items.works: Al-Sharḥ al-kabīr ʿalā Mukhtaṣar Khalīl; Aqrab al-masālik; al-Kharīda al-bahiyya fī al-ʿaqīda

items.title: Gelenbevi
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl ibn Muṣṭafā al-Gelenbevī
items.description: Gelenbevī İsmāʿīl was an Ottoman mathematician, logician, and theologian whose works helped sustain advanced mathematical and logical education in the empire. He wrote textbooks and commentaries used in Ottoman scholarly institutions.
items.works: Burhān-i Gelenbevī; treatises on arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and logic

items.title: Murtada al-Zabidi
items.fullName: Muḥammad Murtaḍā ibn Muḥammad al-Zabīdī
items.description: Murtaḍā al-Zabīdī was a celebrated scholar, lexicographer, hadith expert, and Sufi of the eighteenth-century Islamic world. His dictionary commentary and works on hadith and spiritual lineage made him a major encyclopedic scholar in Cairo.
items.works: Tāj al-ʿarūs min jawāhir al-Qāmūs; Itḥāf al-sāda al-muttaqīn; al-Muʿjam al-mukhtaṣṣ; al-Amālī

items.title: Ahmad al-Tijani
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Tijānī
items.description: Aḥmad al-Tijānī was the North African Sufi master who founded the Tijaniyya, a major order that later spread widely across Africa. His teachings centered on devotional litanies and a particular spiritual lineage, preserved mainly through disciples.
items.works: Jawāhir al-maʿānī (compiled by ʿAlī Ḥarāzim); attributed prayers and litanies of the Tijaniyya

items.title: Abdullah al-Sharqawi
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥijāzī al-Sharqāwī
items.description: ʿAbd Allāh al-Sharqāwī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī scholar and Shaykh al-Azhar known for legal and theological teaching during a period of political upheaval. His commentaries were widely used in traditional learning.
items.works: Ḥāshiya ʿalā Sharḥ al-Taḥrīr; Ḥāshiya on al-Bayjūrī’s commentary to Jawharat al-tawḥīd; scholarly treatises

items.title: al-Tahtawi
items.fullName: Rifāʿa Rāfiʿ al-Ṭahṭāwī
items.description: Rifāʿa al-Ṭahṭāwī was an Egyptian scholar, translator, and educational reformer whose work helped introduce European sciences and political thought into modern Arabic discourse. He promoted translation, education, and cultural renewal.
items.works: Takhlīṣ al-ibrīz fī talkhīṣ Bārīz; al-Murshid al-amīn li-l-banāt wa-l-banīn; Manāhij al-albāb al-miṣriyya

items.title: Ibn Ajiba
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAjība al-Ḥasanī
items.description: Ibn ʿAjība was a Moroccan Mālikī scholar and Sufi whose Qur’anic commentary combines exoteric interpretation with spiritual readings. His writings became influential in Shadhili and Darqawi Sufi circles.
items.works: Al-Baḥr al-madīd fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-majīd; Īqāẓ al-himam fī sharḥ al-Ḥikam; Miʿrāj al-tashawwuf

items.title: Khalid al-Baghdadi
items.fullName: Khālid ibn Aḥmad al-Baghdādī
items.description: Khālid al-Baghdādī was a Kurdish Naqshbandi master whose teaching helped spread the Naqshbandiyya-Khalidiyya throughout the Ottoman Empire and the Middle East. His letters and spiritual guidance shaped nineteenth-century Sunni Sufi networks.
items.works: Maktūbāt Khālidiyya; treatises and letters preserved in the Naqshbandi-Khalidi tradition

items.title: al-Bajuri
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Bājūrī
items.description: Ibrāhīm al-Bājūrī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī theologian and rector of al-Azhar whose commentaries became widely used in traditional Islamic education. His works helped preserve and explain post-classical theology and law.
items.works: Tuḥfat al-murīd ʿalā Jawharat al-tawḥīd; Ḥāshiya ʿalā Sharḥ Ibn Qāsim al-Ghazzī; Ḥāshiya on al-Sulamī

items.title: Ibn Abidin
items.fullName: Muḥammad Amīn ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿĀbidīn
items.description: Ibn ʿĀbidīn was one of the most influential late Ottoman Ḥanafī jurists. His encyclopedic commentary on al-Durr al-mukhtār became a central authority for later Ḥanafī legal practice and a key reference for modern fatwa institutions.
items.works: Radd al-muḥtār ʿalā al-Durr al-mukhtār; Majmūʿat rasāʾil Ibn ʿĀbidīn; al-ʿUqūd al-durriyya

items.title: Fadl-i Haqq Khayrabadi
items.fullName: Faḍl-i Ḥaqq Khayrābādī ibn Faḍl Imām Khayrābādī
items.description: Faḍl-i Ḥaqq Khayrābādī was an Indian theologian, logician, poet, and anti-colonial figure who defended classical Islamic philosophy and theology. He was imprisoned by the British after the uprising of 1857 and became an emblem of scholarly resistance.
items.works: Al-Hadiyya al-saʿīdiyya; Tahqīq al-fatwā fī ibṭāl al-ṭāghūt; treatises on logic and kalām; Arabic and Persian poetry

items.title: Hadi Sabzawari
items.fullName: Hādī ibn Mahdī Sabzawārī
items.description: Hādī Sabzawārī was a leading Iranian philosopher who synthesized Mullā Ṣadrā’s transcendent theosophy into a systematic curriculum. His didactic poetry and commentary remained central to later Shiʿi philosophical education.
items.works: Sharḥ al-Manẓūma; Asrār al-ḥikam; al-Risāla fī al-sayr wa-l-sulūk

items.title: al-Alusi
items.fullName: Maḥmūd Shihāb al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusaynī al-Ālūsī
items.description: Maḥmūd al-Ālūsī was an Iraqi Qur’anic exegete and jurist whose expansive commentary combines transmitted interpretation, linguistics, theology, and rational analysis. It is an important reference for the breadth of nineteenth-century Sunni tafsīr.
items.works: Rūḥ al-maʿānī fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm wa-l-sabʿ al-mathānī; Ghāyat al-amānī fī al-radd ʿalā al-Nabhānī

items.title: al-Maydani
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Ṭālib al-Maydānī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Ghanī al-Maydānī was a Syrian Ḥanafī jurist whose concise legal texts became widely taught in the modern period. His manuals clarified practical law and served as a bridge between classical jurisprudence and contemporary instruction.
items.works: Al-Lubāb fī sharḥ al-Kitāb; al-Maydānī’s commentaries on Ḥanafī law

items.title: Emir Abd al-Qadir
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Qādir ibn Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Jazāʾirī
items.description: Emir ʿAbd al-Qādir was an Algerian Sufi, scholar, and resistance leader who fought French conquest and later became known for ethical restraint and protection of civilians. His mystical writings display a mature engagement with Ibn ʿArabī’s metaphysics.
items.works: Kitāb al-Mawāqif; Dhikrā al-ʿāqil wa-tanbīh al-ghāfil; letters and Sufi treatises

items.title: al-Marjani
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan Shihāb al-Dīn Hārūn ibn Bahāʾ al-Dīn ibn Subḥān al-Kazānī al-Marjānī
items.description: Shihāb al-Dīn al-Marjānī was a Volga-Ural Tatar theologian, historian, and reform-minded scholar who helped renew Islamic learning in the Russian Empire. His historical and educational writings challenged inherited assumptions and encouraged critical scholarship.
items.works: Wafiyyat al-aslāf wa-taḥiyyat al-akhlāf; Mustafād al-akhbār fī aḥwāl Qazan wa-Bulghār

items.title: Cevdet Pasha
items.fullName: Aḥmed Cevdet Paşa
items.description: Aḥmed Cevdet Paşa was an Ottoman historian, jurist, statesman, and reformer who helped codify Islamic civil law for the modern state. His historical writing remains among the major sources for Ottoman political and intellectual history.
items.works: Mecelle-i Ahkâm-ı Adliyye (principal editor); Tarih-i Cevdet; Kısas-ı Enbiya ve Tevarih-i Hulefa; Tezakir

items.title: Jamal al-Din al-Afghani
items.fullName: Sayyid Jamāl al-Dīn al-Asadābādī, widely known as al-Afghānī
items.description: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Afghānī was a nineteenth-century Muslim political activist and thinker who advocated resistance to imperial domination and renewal of Muslim intellectual life. His pan-Islamic reformism influenced modernist debates, though aspects of his origins and ideas remain contested.
items.works: Al-ʿUrwa al-wuthqā (co-edited with Muḥammad ʿAbduh); al-Radd ʿalā al-dahriyyīn; political essays and speeches

items.title: Abd al-Hayy al-Lakhnawi
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Ḥayy ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥalīm al-Lakhnawī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Ḥayy al-Lakhnawī was an Indian Ḥanafī hadith scholar and jurist known for critical engagement with legal schools and textual evidence. His works on hadith, legal disagreement, and scholarly biography remain important in South Asian Islamic scholarship.
items.works: Al-Rafʿ wa-l-takmīl fī al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl; al-Taʿlīq al-mumajjad; ʿUmdat al-riʿāya; al-Fawāʾid al-bahiyya fī tarājim al-Ḥanafiyya

items.title: Muhammad Abduh
items.fullName: Muḥammad ʿAbduh ibn Ḥasan Khayr Allāh
items.description: Muḥammad ʿAbduh was an Egyptian reformer, jurist, and Qur’anic thinker who sought educational and religious renewal through reasoned interpretation and institutional reform. His ideas influenced modernist Islam, the reform of al-Azhar, and Arab public thought.
items.works: Risālat al-tawḥīd; Tafsīr al-Manār (lectures continued with Rashīd Riḍā); commentaries on Nahj al-balāgha and Dalāʾil al-iʿjāz

items.title: al-Nabhani
items.fullName: Yūsuf ibn Ismāʿīl al-Nabhānī
items.description: Yūsuf al-Nabhānī was a Palestinian-Ottoman judge, poet, and prolific author devoted to Prophetic praise and Sunni devotional tradition. His works collected hadith, biographies, poems, and defenses of established devotional practices.
items.works: Jāmiʿ karāmāt al-awliyāʾ; Shawāhid al-ḥaqq; Saʿādat al-dārayn; Dīwān al-Nabhānī

items.title: Musa Kazim Efendi
items.fullName: Mūsā Kāẓım Efendi
items.description: Mūsā Kāẓım Efendi was an Ottoman scholar and Shaykh al-Islām who engaged modern political and philosophical questions while working within Islamic scholarly traditions. His writings discuss theology, philosophy, reform, and the role of religion in public life.
items.works: Kulliyyāt-i Mūsā Kāẓım; treatises on philosophy, theology, and constitutionalism

items.title: Ashraf Ali Thanawi
items.fullName: Ashraf ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Thānavī
items.description: Ashraf ʿAlī Thānawī was a major Indian Deobandi scholar, Sufi guide, and prolific author whose work covered law, theology, ethics, and spiritual practice. His accessible advice and legal responses have strongly influenced South Asian Sunni religious life.
items.works: Bayān al-Qurʾān; Imdād al-fatāwā; Bahishti Zewar; al-Takashshuf ʿan muhimmāt al-taṣawwuf; Nashr al-ṭīb

items.title: Filibeli Ahmed Hilmi
items.fullName: Filibeli Aḥmed Ḥilmī
items.description: Aḥmad Hilmī was a late Ottoman thinker and writer whose works addressed Islamic philosophy, spirituality, and responses to materialism. He sought to defend religious metaphysics while engaging modern intellectual currents.
items.works: Üss-i İnkılâb; Huzûr-ı Akl ü Fende Maddiyyûn Meslek-i Dalâleti; Amak-ı Hayal

items.title: Rashid Rida
items.fullName: Muḥammad Rashīd Riḍā ibn ʿAlī Riḍā
items.description: Rashīd Riḍā was a Syrian-Egyptian reformist scholar, publisher, and disciple of Muḥammad ʿAbduh. Through the journal al-Manār and his writings on Qur’anic interpretation, hadith, and governance, he became a major voice in modern Islamic reform.
items.works: Tafsīr al-Manār (continued from ʿAbduh’s lessons); al-Khilāfa aw al-imāma al-ʿuẓmā; Muḥāwarāt al-muṣliḥ wa-l-muqallid; al-Waḥy al-Muḥammadī

items.title: Jamal al-Din al-Qasimi
items.fullName: Muḥammad Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Muḥammad Saʿīd ibn Qāsim al-Ḥallāq al-Qāsimī
items.description: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Qāsimī was a Syrian reformist scholar of hadith, Qur’anic exegesis, and theology who sought renewal through critical study of the early sources. His works influenced Salafi-leaning reform circles in the modern Arab world.
items.works: Maḥāsin al-taʾwīl; Qawāʿid al-taḥdīth; Dalāʾil al-tawḥīd; Iṣlāḥ al-masājid min al-bidaʿ wa-l-ʿawāʾid

items.title: Mustafa Sabri
items.fullName: Muṣṭafā Ṣabrī Efendi
items.description: Muṣṭafā Ṣabrī was the last Ottoman Shaykh al-Islām and a prominent defender of traditional Islamic theology against secularism and materialism. In exile, he wrote major critiques of modern philosophy and argued for the continuing relevance of kalām.
items.works: Mawqif al-ʿaql wa-l-ʿilm wa-l-ʿālam min rabb al-ʿālamīn; al-Nakirāt; Qawl al-maʿrūf fī al-radd ʿalā man ankara al-taṣawwuf

items.title: Muhammad al-Tahir ibn Ashur
items.fullName: Muḥammad al-Ṭāhir ibn ʿĀshūr
items.description: Muḥammad al-Ṭāhir ibn ʿĀshūr was a Tunisian Mālikī jurist and Qur’anic exegete who revitalized the study of maqāṣid al-sharīʿa and modern tafsīr. His commentary balances linguistic depth, legal analysis, and social interpretation.
items.works: Al-Taḥrīr wa-l-tanwīr; Maqāṣid al-sharīʿa al-Islāmiyya; Uṣūl al-niẓām al-ijtimāʿī fī al-Islām

items.title: Bediuzzaman Said Nursi
items.fullName: Saʿīd Nursī, widely known as Bediüzzaman Said Nursî
items.description: Bediüzzaman Said Nursî was a Kurdish-Ottoman/Turkish Muslim scholar and Qur’anic commentator whose Risale-i Nur collection seeks to demonstrate the truths of faith through reason, reflection on nature, and spiritual insight. His movement became influential in modern Turkish religious life.
items.works: Risale-i Nur Külliyatı, including Sözler, Mektubat, Lem'alar, Şualar, İşaratü'l-İ'caz, and Münazarat

items.title: Muhammad Iqbal
items.fullName: Muḥammad Iqbāl
items.description: Muḥammad Iqbāl was a South Asian philosopher and poet writing in Persian and Urdu who explored selfhood, spiritual renewal, and the future of Muslim civilization. His philosophical poetry became a central source for modern Muslim intellectual and political thought.
items.works: Asrār-i Khudī; Rumūz-i Bekhudī; Bāng-i Darā; Jāvīd-nāma; The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam

items.title: Elmalili Hamdi Yazir
items.fullName: Muḥammad Ḥamdī Yazır, known as Elmalılı
items.description: Elmalılı Ḥamdī Yazır was an Ottoman-Turkish scholar of law, theology, philosophy, and Qur’anic interpretation. His Turkish commentary brought classical exegetical scholarship into dialogue with modern questions and remains a major reference in Turkish Islam.
items.works: Hak Dini Kur’an Dili; Metalib ve Mezahib translation/commentary; legal and theological treatises

items.title: Muhammad Zahid al-Kawthari
items.fullName: Muḥammad Zāhid ibn al-Ḥasan al-Kawtharī
items.description: Muḥammad Zāhid al-Kawtharī was a late Ottoman Ḥanafī scholar and theologian who defended classical Sunni legal and theological traditions in exile. His editions, commentaries, and polemical works helped preserve numerous classical texts and shaped twentieth-century Sunni debates.
items.works: Maqālāt al-Kawtharī; Fiqh ahl al-ʿIrāq wa-ḥadīthuhum; editions and commentaries on classical Ḥanafī and kalām works

items.title: Ilyas Kandhlawi
items.fullName: Muḥammad Ilyās ibn Muḥammad Ismāʿīl al-Kāndhlawī
items.description: Muḥammad Ilyās Kāndhlawī founded the Tablighi Jamaat, a transnational Muslim movement emphasizing personal religious renewal, preaching, and everyday practice. His significance lies primarily in the movement and oral guidance developed through his disciples.
items.works: No major authored book securely attributed; malfūẓāt and teachings compiled by disciples

items.title: Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid
items.fullName: Muḥyī al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd
items.description: Muḥyī al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd was a modern Egyptian scholar and editor of classical Arabic texts, especially in grammar, rhetoric, and Islamic studies. His annotated editions made many foundational works accessible to twentieth-century students.
items.works: Scholarly editions and commentaries on works such as Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Balāgha al-wāḍiḥa, and classical Arabic grammar and rhetoric texts

items.title: Muhammad Husayn Tabataba'i
items.fullName: Muḥammad Ḥusayn Ṭabāṭabāʾī
items.description: Muḥammad Ḥusayn Ṭabāṭabāʾī was a major Iranian Twelver Shiʿi philosopher and Qur’anic exegete who integrated philosophy, theology, and spiritual interpretation. His commentary became one of the most influential modern Shiʿi tafsīrs.
items.works: Al-Mīzān fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān; Uṣūl-i falsafa wa-ravish-i riʾālism; Bidāyat al-ḥikma; Nihāyat al-ḥikma; al-Shīʿa dar Islām

items.title: Sayyid Qutb
items.fullName: Sayyid Quṭb Ibrāhīm Ḥusayn al-Shādhilī
items.description: Sayyid Quṭb was an Egyptian writer and Islamist thinker whose Qur’anic commentary and political works became highly influential in twentieth-century Islamic movements. His critique of modern jahiliyya and emphasis on divine sovereignty remain debated across Muslim intellectual traditions.
items.works: Fī ẓilāl al-Qurʾān; Maʿālim fī al-ṭarīq; al-ʿAdāla al-ijtimāʿiyya fī al-Islām; Khaṣāʾiṣ al-taṣawwur al-Islāmī

items.title: Hasan al-Banna
items.fullName: Ḥasan Aḥmad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Bannā
items.description: Ḥasan al-Bannā founded the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt, building a mass movement centered on Islamic reform, social action, and political engagement. His organizational model influenced Islamist movements across the Middle East and beyond.
items.works: Majmūʿat Rasāʾil al-Imām al-Shahīd Ḥasan al-Bannā (collected letters and programmatic essays)

items.title: Muhammad al-Ghazali
items.fullName: Muḥammad al-Ghazālī al-Saqqā
items.description: Muḥammad al-Ghazālī was a modern Egyptian Sunni scholar and public intellectual who wrote widely on ethics, Qur’anic interpretation, social reform, and contemporary Muslim challenges. He advocated renewal rooted in scripture while criticizing both rigid literalism and uncritical Westernization.
items.works: Al-Sunna al-nabawiyya bayna ahl al-fiqh wa-ahl al-ḥadīth; Fiqh al-sīra; Kayfa nataʿāmal maʿ al-Qurʾān; Jaddid ḥayātak

items.title: Wahiduddin Khan
items.fullName: Wāḥid al-Dīn Khān
items.description: Wāḥid al-Dīn Khān was an Indian Islamic thinker and peace advocate who emphasized nonviolence, spiritual renewal, and constructive engagement with modernity. His English and Urdu writings sought to present Islamic teachings to contemporary global audiences.
items.works: Islam and Peace; Tazkirul Quran; The Prophet of Peace; Maʿrifat-i Khudā

items.title: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
items.fullName: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qaraḍāwī
items.description: Yūsuf al-Qaraḍāwī was an Egyptian-born Sunni jurist and influential modern religious broadcaster whose works addressed law, ethics, finance, and Muslim public life. His ideas shaped contemporary debates on fiqh, wasatiyya, and Islamic movements, while remaining contested.
items.works: Al-Ḥalāl wa-l-ḥarām fī al-Islām; Fiqh al-zakāh; al-Ijtihād fī al-sharīʿa al-Islāmiyya; al-Ṣaḥwa al-Islāmiyya bayna al-juhūd wa-l-taṭarruf

items.title: Muhammad Said Ramadan al-Buti
items.fullName: Muḥammad Saʿīd Ramaḍān al-Būṭī
items.description: Muḥammad Saʿīd Ramaḍān al-Būṭī was a Syrian Sunni theologian, Shāfiʿī jurist, and Ashʿarī scholar known for works on creed, legal methodology, spirituality, and the philosophy of religion. His writings reached a broad Arabic-speaking readership and he was a prominent, controversial public voice during Syria’s uprising.
items.works: Kubrā al-yaqīniyyāt al-kawniyya; Fiqh al-sīra al-nabawiyya; Ḍawābiṭ al-maṣlaḥa fī al-sharīʿa al-Islāmiyya; al-Lā madhhabiyya akhṭar bidʿa tuhaddid al-sharīʿa al-Islāmiyya

items.title: Muhammad Ali al-Sabuni
items.fullName: Muḥammad ʿAlī al-Ṣābūnī
items.description: Muḥammad ʿAlī al-Ṣābūnī was a Syrian Qur’anic scholar and author of widely used modern works in tafsīr and Qur’anic sciences. His accessible presentation of classical exegetical material was influential in religious education across the Muslim world.
items.works: Ṣafwat al-tafāsīr; Rawāʾiʿ al-bayān fī tafsīr āyāt al-aḥkām; al-Tibyān fī ʿulūm al-Qurʾān

items.title: Fethullah Gulen
items.fullName: Fethullah Gülen
items.description: Fethullah Gülen was a Turkish Muslim preacher, writer, and educator whose works emphasize faith, ethical service, interfaith dialogue, and education. His ideas inspired a transnational network of educational and civil-society initiatives, while his movement’s political role became deeply controversial in Turkey.
items.works: Pırlanta series, including Kırık Testi; Kalbin Zümrüt Tepeleri; Sonsuz Nur; Yol Mülahazaları; Toward a Global Civilization of Love and Tolerance

items.title: Muqatil ibn Sulayman
items.fullName: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān ibn Bashīr al-Azdī
items.description: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān was an early Qur’anic exegete whose commentary is among the oldest complete tafsīrs to survive. Although later hadith critics questioned his reliability as a transmitter, his work is important for the development of early Qur’anic interpretation and narrative exegesis.
items.works: Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān; al-Wujūh wa-l-naẓāʾir; al-Nāsikh wa-l-mansūkh (attributed)

items.title: al-Tha'labi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Thaʿlabī, Abū Isḥāq
items.description: Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī was a Persian Qur’anic exegete and story collector whose commentary preserves extensive early exegetical reports, narratives of the prophets, and accounts of revelation. His work influenced later Sunni tafsīr, including al-Baghawī.
items.works: Al-Kashf wa-l-bayān ʿan tafsīr al-Qurʾān; ʿArāʾis al-majālis fī qiṣaṣ al-anbiyāʾ

items.title: al-Tha'alibi
items.fullName: Abū Manṣūr ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Thaʿālibī
items.description: Abū Manṣūr al-Thaʿālibī was a Persian Arabophone man of letters and anthologist known for collecting poetry, anecdotes, and linguistic refinements. His compilations are major sources for the literary culture of the eastern Islamic world.
items.works: Yatīmat al-dahr fī maḥāsin ahl al-ʿaṣr; Fiqh al-lugha wa-sirr al-ʿarabiyya; Laṭāʾif al-maʿārif; Thimār al-qulūb

items.title: al-Wahidi
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Wāḥidī al-Naysābūrī
items.description: Al-Wāḥidī was a major Qur’anic exegete known for organizing reports about the circumstances of revelation (asbāb al-nuzūl). His commentaries helped shape classical tafsīr and his work remains a key reference for contextual reports about Qur’anic verses.
items.works: Asbāb al-nuzūl; al-Wasīṭ fī tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-majīd; al-Basīṭ; al-Wajīz

items.title: Abu Hayyan al-Andalusi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf ibn Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī al-Andalusī, Abū Ḥayyān Athīr al-Dīn
items.description: Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī was an Andalusian-born grammarian, Qur’anic exegete, and hadith scholar who spent much of his career in Cairo. His tafsīr is renowned for rigorous grammar, linguistic analysis, and criticism of weak interpretations.
items.works: Al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ; Irtishāf al-ḍarab min lisān al-ʿArab; al-Tadhyīl wa-l-takmīl; Tuḥfat al-arīb

items.title: al-Mahalli
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Maḥallī, Jalāl al-Dīn
items.description: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Maḥallī was an Egyptian Shāfiʿī scholar who began the concise Qur’anic commentary later completed by al-Suyūṭī and known as Tafsīr al-Jalālayn. The work’s brevity and clarity made it a staple of Islamic education.
items.works: Tafsīr al-Jalālayn (first portion); Sharḥ Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ; al-Badr al-ṭāliʿ fī ḥall Jamʿ al-jawāmiʿ

items.title: al-Biqa'i
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥasan al-Biqāʿī
items.description: Burhān al-Dīn al-Biqāʿī was a Shāfiʿī scholar and Qur’anic exegete known for examining coherence between Qur’anic passages and their contexts. His work was innovative in its sustained attention to thematic links across the Qur’an.
items.works: Naẓm al-durar fī tanāsub al-āyāt wa-l-suwar; Maṣāʿid al-naẓar li-l-ishrāf ʿalā maqāṣid al-suwar

items.title: al-Shawkani
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Shawkānī
items.description: Al-Shawkānī was a Yemeni jurist, hadith scholar, and reformist thinker who advocated direct engagement with scriptural evidence beyond strict adherence to a single legal school. His tafsīr and legal works remain widely consulted in modern Sunni scholarship.
items.works: Fatḥ al-qadīr; Nayl al-awṭār; Irshād al-fuḥūl; al-Sayl al-jarrār; al-Badr al-ṭāliʿ

items.title: Abu al-Barakat al-Nasafi
items.fullName: Ḥāfiẓ al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Maḥmūd al-Nasafī
items.description: Abū al-Barakāt al-Nasafī was a Ḥanafī jurist, Māturīdī theologian, and Qur’anic exegete whose concise works became standard texts in Ottoman and South Asian education. His tafsīr synthesizes earlier linguistic and theological scholarship.
items.works: Madārik al-tanzīl wa-ḥaqāʾiq al-taʾwīl; Kanz al-daqāʾiq; al-ʿUmda fī uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Iʿtimād fī al-iʿtiqād

items.title: al-Raghib al-Isfahani
items.fullName: Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal al-Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī
items.description: Al-Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī was an ethical thinker and Qur’anic lexicographer whose analysis of Qur’anic vocabulary and moral psychology influenced later scholars, including al-Ghazālī. He sought to relate language, ethical refinement, and religious understanding.
items.works: Al-Mufradāt fī gharīb al-Qurʾān; al-Dharīʿa ilā makārim al-sharīʿa; Tafṣīl al-nashʾatayn

items.title: al-Zarkashi
items.fullName: Badr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Zarkashī
items.description: Al-Zarkashī was a Mamluk-era Shāfiʿī jurist and scholar of Qur’anic sciences, hadith, and legal theory. His encyclopedic treatment of Qur’anic studies became a foundational reference for later scholars.
items.works: Al-Burhān fī ʿulūm al-Qurʾān; al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ fī uṣūl al-fiqh; al-Manthūr fī al-qawāʿid al-fiqhiyya

items.title: al-Sa'di
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nāṣir al-Saʿdī
items.description: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Saʿdī was a modern Saudi Hanbali scholar and Qur’anic exegete known for clear, accessible interpretation and practical ethical lessons. His tafsīr is widely read for its straightforward synthesis of transmitted commentary and doctrinal teaching.
items.works: Taysīr al-Karīm al-Raḥmān fī tafsīr kalām al-Mannān; al-Qawāʿid al-ḥisān; al-Qawl al-sadīd fī maqāṣid al-tawḥīd

items.title: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali
items.fullName: Ẓālim ibn ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Duʾalī
items.description: Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī was an early Arab grammarian traditionally credited with laying foundations for Arabic grammatical analysis and introducing a system of diacritical marking. Details are partly legendary, but his name is central to accounts of grammar’s origins.
items.works: No securely extant authored book; grammatical rules and verse attributed in later linguistic sources

items.title: Ibn al-Jazari
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf al-Jazarī
items.description: Ibn al-Jazarī was a preeminent scholar of Qur’anic recitation whose works systematized the canonical readings and their transmission. His manuals became central to the study of tajwīd and qirāʾāt throughout the Muslim world.
items.works: Al-Nashr fī al-qirāʾāt al-ʿashr; Ṭayyibat al-nashr; al-Muqaddima al-Jazariyya; Ghāyat al-nihāya fī ṭabaqāt al-qurrāʾ

items.title: Ibn Ishaq
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Yasār al-Muṭṭalibī
items.description: Ibn Isḥāq was an early Muslim historian whose biography of the Prophet became the foundation for later sīra literature. His original work survives mainly through Ibn Hishām’s recension and quotations in later historical writings.
items.works: Kitāb al-Maghāzī / Sīrat Rasūl Allāh (preserved principally through Ibn Hishām and al-Ṭabarī)

items.title: Katip Celebi (Haji Khalifa)
items.fullName: Muṣṭafā ibn ʿAbd Allāh Kâtip Çelebi, known as Ḥājjī Khalīfa
items.description: Ḥājjī Khalīfa (Kâtip Çelebi) was an Ottoman bibliographer, historian, and geographer whose encyclopedic catalogs document Islamic and world scholarship. His works are crucial sources for the history of books, disciplines, and Ottoman intellectual life.
items.works: Kashf al-ẓunūn ʿan asāmī al-kutub wa-l-funūn; Sullam al-wuṣūl; Mīzān al-ḥaqq; Cihannümâ

items.title: Ibn Abi Shayba
items.fullName: Abū Bakr ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAbsī
items.description: Ibn Abī Shayba was a major hadith scholar whose extensive Muṣannaf preserves early legal traditions, Companion opinions, and hadith reports. His work is especially important for reconstructing early Islamic jurisprudence and debates among the first generations.
items.works: Al-Muṣannaf; al-Musnad; Kitāb al-Adab

items.title: al-Tabarani
items.fullName: Sulaymān ibn Aḥmad ibn Ayyūb al-Ṭabarānī
items.description: Al-Ṭabarānī was a major hadith collector whose large compilations preserve a wide range of transmissions from early Muslim authorities. His three Muʿjam collections became important sources for hadith scholars and biographical research.
items.works: Al-Muʿjam al-kabīr; al-Muʿjam al-awsaṭ; al-Muʿjam al-ṣaghīr; Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn

items.title: al-Mizzi
items.fullName: Jamāl al-Dīn Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Mizzī
items.description: Al-Mizzī was a Syrian hadith scholar and biographer whose comprehensive dictionary of transmitters became a fundamental reference for evaluating the narrators in the six canonical Sunni collections. His work influenced Ibn Ḥajar and later hadith criticism.
items.works: Tahdhīb al-Kamāl fī asmāʾ al-rijāl; Tuḥfat al-ashrāf bi-maʿrifat al-aṭrāf

items.title: Zayn al-Din al-'Iraqi
items.fullName: Zayn al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn al-Ḥusayn al-ʿIrāqī
items.description: Zayn al-Dīn al-ʿIrāqī was a leading Shāfiʿī hadith scholar who critically traced the hadith cited in al-Ghazālī’s Iḥyāʾ and wrote influential manuals of hadith terminology. His work advanced source criticism within devotional and legal scholarship.
items.works: Al-Mughnī ʿan ḥaml al-asfār; Alfiyyat al-ḥadīth; al-Taqyīd wa-l-īḍāḥ

items.title: Abu Yala al-Mawsili
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Muthannā al-Tamīmī al-Mawṣilī, Abū Yaʿlā
items.description: Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī was a hadith scholar whose large Musnad preserves Prophetic reports from a wide range of Companions. His collection is a significant source for the transmission history of early Sunni hadith.
items.works: Musnad Abī Yaʿlā; works on hadith and transmitters

items.title: al-Zuhri
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī
items.description: Muḥammad ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī was an early hadith scholar and historian often credited with helping establish the collection and transmission of Prophetic reports. His maghāzī material and reports became central to early sīra and hadith literature.
items.works: Maghāzī and hadith materials preserved by later compilers; no complete independent book survives

items.title: al-Layth ibn Sad
items.fullName: al-Layth ibn Saʿd al-Fahmī
items.description: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd was a leading Egyptian jurist and hadith scholar whose independent legal school later disappeared despite his great reputation. His legal judgments, generosity, and correspondence are frequently cited in early Islamic sources.
items.works: No complete authored work survives; legal opinions and hadith transmissions preserved in early collections

items.title: Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman
items.fullName: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān al-Ashʿarī
items.description: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān was a leading Kūfan jurist and teacher of Abū Ḥanīfa. His transmission of the legal tradition associated with Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī was essential to the formation of early Ḥanafī jurisprudence.
items.works: No independent work extant; legal opinions transmitted through Abū Ḥanīfa and early Ḥanafī sources

items.title: al-Kasani
items.fullName: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn Abū Bakr ibn Masʿūd al-Kāsānī
items.description: Al-Kāsānī was a major Ḥanafī jurist whose systematic treatment of substantive law became a standard reference. His work organizes legal rulings by their underlying principles and remains widely cited in later Ḥanafī scholarship.
items.works: Badāʾiʿ al-ṣanāʾiʿ fī tartīb al-sharāʾiʿ

items.title: Badr al-Din al-Ayni
items.fullName: Maḥmūd ibn Aḥmad ibn Mūsā al-ʿAynī
items.description: Badr al-Dīn al-ʿAynī was a Mamluk Ḥanafī jurist, hadith scholar, and historian whose commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī is one of the most substantial in the tradition. He also wrote on law, history, and Arabic language.
items.works: ʿUmdat al-qārī sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī; al-Bināya sharḥ al-Hidāya; ʿIqd al-jumān fī tārīkh ahl al-zamān

items.title: Izz al-Din ibn Abd al-Salam
items.fullName: ʿIzz al-Dīn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām al-Sulamī
items.description: ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām was a Shāfiʿī jurist and theologian renowned for legal reasoning centered on public welfare, moral purposes, and the hierarchy of benefits and harms. His work profoundly influenced maqāṣid and legal-maxim scholarship.
items.works: Qawāʿid al-aḥkām fī maṣāliḥ al-anām; al-Fatāwā; al-Imām fī bayān adillat al-aḥkām

items.title: al-Asmai
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Qurayb al-Bāhilī al-Aṣmaʿī
items.description: Al-Aṣmaʿī was an Abbasid-era philologist, poet, and collector of Bedouin Arabic, noted for preserving rare vocabulary, poetry, and tribal lore. His linguistic works were important to early lexicography and the interpretation of classical Arabic literature.
items.works: Al-Aṣmaʿiyyāt (poetry anthology associated with him); Kitāb al-Khayl; Kitāb al-Ibil; collections of Arab poetry and vocabulary

items.title: al-Akhfash al-Awsat
items.fullName: Saʿīd ibn Masʿada al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
items.description: Al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ was a prominent Basran grammarian who transmitted and commented on Sībawayh’s Kitāb. His analyses of syntax, prosody, and Qur’anic language contributed to the development of classical Arabic grammar.
items.works: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān; al-Awsaṭ fī al-naḥw; works on prosody and grammar
