items.title: al-Rummani
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī al-Rummānī
items.description: Al-Rummānī was a grammarian, rhetorician, and Muʿtazilī theologian who wrote influential analyses of Qur’anic eloquence. His account of the Qur’an’s inimitability helped shape classical Arabic rhetoric and theological arguments about revelation.
items.works: Al-Nukat fī iʿjāz al-Qurʾān; Maʿānī al-ḥurūf; al-Jāmiʿ fī ʿilm al-Qurʾān; works on grammar

items.title: al-Hariri
items.fullName: al-Qāsim ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Ḥarīrī al-Baṣrī
items.description: Al-Ḥarīrī was an Abbasid-era Arabic prose master whose maqāmāt are celebrated for elaborate linguistic virtuosity, wit, and narrative invention. His work became a classic of Arabic belles lettres and a long-standing text for advanced language study.
items.works: Maqāmāt al-Ḥarīrī; Durra al-ghawwāṣ fī awhām al-khawāṣṣ; Dīwān al-rasāʾil

items.title: Ibn al-Hajib
items.fullName: Jamāl al-Dīn ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar ibn Abī Bakr ibn Yūnus al-Mālikī, Ibn al-Ḥājib
items.description: Ibn al-Ḥājib was a Kurdish-born Mālikī jurist and grammarian whose concise works on Arabic syntax and legal theory became influential across the Islamic world. His manuals generated a vast commentary tradition in Ottoman and other madrasas.
items.works: Al-Kāfiya; al-Shāfiya; Mukhtaṣar al-Muntahā fī uṣūl al-fiqh; Jāmiʿ al-ummahāt

items.title: al-Khatib al-Qazwini
items.fullName: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qazwīnī
items.description: Al-Qazwīnī was a Shāfiʿī jurist, Qur’anic rhetorician, and literary theorist whose manuals helped standardize the later science of Arabic balāgha. His summaries of rhetoric became fundamental texts in advanced Arabic education.
items.works: Al-Talkhīṣ fī ʿulūm al-balāgha; al-Īḍāḥ fī ʿulūm al-balāgha

items.title: Hassan ibn Thabit
items.fullName: Ḥassān ibn Thābit ibn al-Mundhir al-Anṣārī
items.description: Ḥassān ibn Thābit was the Prophet’s celebrated poet, whose verse defended the early Muslim community and praised the Prophet. His poetry is an important source for early Islamic literary culture and the use of panegyric in religious life.
items.works: Dīwān Ḥassān ibn Thābit; panegyrics and poems preserved in sīra and adab works

items.title: Kab ibn Zuhayr
items.fullName: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā
items.description: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr was a pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arab poet who composed the famous qaṣīda Bānat Suʿād in praise of the Prophet. The poem became a classic of Prophetic praise and a major work in Arabic poetic tradition.
items.works: Bānat Suʿād (Qaṣīdat al-Burda); Dīwān Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr

items.title: al-Khansa'
items.fullName: Tumāḍir bint ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith al-Sulamiyya, al-Khansāʾ
items.description: Al-Khansāʾ was a celebrated early Arabic poet renowned for elegies mourning her brothers. Her emotionally forceful poems became canonical examples of Arabic rithāʾ and earned her a lasting place in classical literary history.
items.works: Dīwān al-Khansāʾ; elegies (marāthī) for Ṣakhr and Muʿāwiya

items.title: Jarir ibn Atiyah
items.fullName: Jarīr ibn ʿAṭiyya al-Khaṭafī
items.description: Jarīr ibn ʿAṭiyya was one of the major Umayyad poets, famous for satire, panegyric, and rivalry with al-Farazdaq and al-Akhṭal. His poetry is a key source for tribal politics and literary culture in the Umayyad period.
items.works: Dīwān Jarīr; satires and panegyrics preserved in classical adab anthologies

items.title: al-Farazdaq
items.fullName: Hammām ibn Ghālib al-Tamīmī, al-Farazdaq
items.description: Al-Farazdaq was a major Umayyad poet famed for invective, praise poetry, and a powerful classical style. His long rivalry with Jarīr became a defining episode in Arabic literary history, and his verse preserves valuable tribal and social detail.
items.works: Dīwān al-Farazdaq; qaṣāʾid and naqāʾiḍ poems

items.title: al-Akhtal
items.fullName: Ghiyāth ibn Ghawth al-Taghlibī, al-Akhṭal
items.description: Al-Akhṭal was a Christian Arab poet at the Umayyad court whose panegyrics supported the ruling Marwānids. One of the great poets of the age, he excelled in satire and formal qaṣīda and illustrates the religious diversity of Umayyad literary culture.
items.works: Dīwān al-Akhṭal; panegyrics for Umayyad caliphs and tribal satires

items.title: Umar ibn Abi Rabiah
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī
items.description: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa was an Umayyad-era Meccan poet who transformed the ghazal through vivid scenes of courtship, travel, and social encounter. His urbane love poetry became a major strand of classical Arabic lyric.
items.works: Dīwān ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa; ghazals preserved in adab anthologies

items.title: Abu Nuwas
items.fullName: al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ al-Ḥakamī, Abū Nuwās
items.description: Abū Nuwās was an Abbasid poet celebrated for wine poetry, witty social satire, and experiments with Arabic poetic conventions. His work also includes ascetic and penitential verse, revealing a range broader than the notoriety of his khamriyyāt.
items.works: Dīwān Abī Nuwās, including khamriyyāt, hunting poems, ascetic verse, and panegyric

items.title: Abu al-Atahiya
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl ibn al-Qāsim al-ʿAnazī, Abū al-ʿAtāhiya
items.description: Abū al-ʿAtāhiya was an Abbasid poet known for ascetic, moralizing verse that departed from the conventions of the classical qaṣīda. His poems on mortality and worldly impermanence became widely quoted in religious and literary contexts.
items.works: Dīwān Abī al-ʿAtāhiya; zuhdiyyāt and moral poems

items.title: Abu Tammam
items.fullName: Ḥabīb ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ṭāʾī, Abū Tammām
items.description: Abū Tammām was an Abbasid poet and anthologist whose dense imagery and elaborate metaphors helped define the innovative style of Arabic poetry. His anthology of earlier verse is a major record of pre-Islamic and early Islamic poetic heritage.
items.works: Dīwān Abī Tammām; al-Ḥamāsa (poetry anthology); qaṣīdat al-fatḥ ʿammūriyya

items.title: al-Buhturi
items.fullName: al-Walīd ibn ʿUbayd ibn Yaḥyā al-Tanūkhī al-Buḥturī
items.description: Al-Buḥturī was a leading Abbasid poet celebrated for clarity, musicality, and vivid description. His panegyrics and nature poetry exemplify a more classical style than the elaborate verbal innovations of his contemporary Abū Tammām.
items.works: Dīwān al-Buḥturī; al-Ḥamāsa (anthology sometimes associated with his recension)

items.title: Ibn al-Rumi
items.fullName: ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn Jurayj al-Rūmī
items.description: Ibn al-Rūmī was an Abbasid poet renowned for sharp satire, psychological observation, and descriptive detail. His unusually individual voice explored everyday life and personal vulnerability, making him a distinctive figure in classical Arabic poetry.
items.works: Dīwān Ibn al-Rūmī; satirical and descriptive poems preserved in literary anthologies

items.title: Ibn al-Mu'tazz
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʿtazz ibn al-Mutawakkil
items.description: Ibn al-Muʿtazz was an Abbasid prince, poet, and literary theorist whose analysis of figurative language helped systematize Arabic rhetoric. His brief reign as caliph ended in a coup, but his literary and critical legacy endured.
items.works: Kitāb al-Badīʿ; Ṭabaqāt al-shuʿarāʾ; Dīwān Ibn al-Muʿtazz; Faṣl al-khiṭāb

items.title: Abu Firas al-Hamdani
items.fullName: al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥamdān al-Ḥamdānī, Abū Firās
items.description: Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī was an Arab prince and poet whose captivity poems combine aristocratic pride, courage, and longing. His Rūmiyyāt, written during Byzantine imprisonment, are among the best-known expressions of personal feeling in classical Arabic poetry.
items.works: Rūmiyyāt; Dīwān Abī Firās al-Ḥamdānī

items.title: al-Mutanabbi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī al-Kindī, al-Mutanabbī
items.description: Al-Mutanabbī was one of the greatest Arabic poets, celebrated for rhetorical power, aphoristic wisdom, ambition, and panegyric. His verse became a touchstone of Arabic eloquence and has generated an immense tradition of commentary.
items.works: Dīwān al-Mutanabbī; major panegyrics and poems composed for Sayf al-Dawla and Kafūr

items.title: al-Ma'arri
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān al-Tanūkhī al-Maʿarrī
items.description: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī was a Syrian poet and philosophical prose writer known for skepticism, ethical rigor, and reflections on mortality and religion. His intellectually challenging works made him one of the most original and debated voices in Arabic literature.
items.works: Luzūm mā lā yalzam (Luzūmiyyāt); Risālat al-ghufrān; Saqṭ al-zand; al-Fuṣūl wa-l-ghāyāt

items.title: Ibn Zaydun
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Zaydūn al-Makhzūmī
items.description: Ibn Zaydūn was an Andalusian poet and statesman famous for his refined love poetry, particularly poems addressed to Wallāda bint al-Mustakfī. His verse represents the height of classical Arabic lyric in al-Andalus.
items.works: Dīwān Ibn Zaydūn; Nūniyya; epistles including the satirical risāla al-hazliyya

items.title: Ferdowsi
items.fullName: Abū al-Qāsim Manṣūr ibn Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, Firdawsī
items.description: Ferdowsi was the great Persian epic poet whose Shāhnāmeh narrates the legendary and historical kings of Iran. His work preserved pre-Islamic Iranian cultural memory and became a foundational masterpiece of Persian literature.
items.works: Shāhnāmeh

items.title: Sanai
items.fullName: Abū al-Majd Majdūd ibn Ādam Sanāʾī al-Ghaznawī
items.description: Sanāʾī of Ghazna was an early major Persian Sufi poet who developed didactic and mystical poetry on spiritual transformation, ethics, and the vanity of worldly ambition. His works influenced later masters including ʿAṭṭār and Rūmī.
items.works: Ḥadīqat al-ḥaqīqa wa-sharīʿat al-ṭarīqa; Sayr al-ʿibād ilā al-maʿād; Dīvān

items.title: Nizami Ganjavi
items.fullName: Niẓāmī Ganjavī, Ilyās ibn Yūsuf
items.description: Niẓāmī Ganjavī was a leading Persian narrative poet known for imaginative romances that combine ethics, kingship, love, and spiritual reflection. His Khamsa became one of the most influential models for Persian and later Indo-Persian literature.
items.works: Khamsa: Makhzan al-asrār, Khusraw o Shīrīn, Laylī o Majnūn, Haft paykar, Iskandar-nāma

items.title: Omar Khayyam
items.fullName: Ghiyāth al-Dīn Abū al-Fatḥ ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm al-Khayyāmī
items.description: ʿUmar Khayyām was a Persian mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher as well as a poet traditionally associated with quatrains questioning fate, time, and mortality. The poems attributed to him vary in authenticity, while his scientific contributions are well documented.
items.works: Rubāʿiyyāt (attribution of individual quatrains debated); Treatise on Demonstration of Problems of Algebra; astronomical work associated with the Jalālī calendar

items.title: Nasimi
items.fullName: ʿImād al-Dīn Nasīmī
items.description: ʿImād al-Dīn Nasīmī was a fourteenth-century Turkic and Persian poet associated with Hurufi mystical thought. His bold verse explored divine manifestation, human dignity, and spiritual interpretation and became influential in Azerbaijani and Anatolian literature.
items.works: Dīvān in Azerbaijani Turkish and Persian; mystical ghazals

items.title: Niyazi Misri
items.fullName: Muḥammad Niyāzī al-Miṣrī
items.description: Niyāzī-i Miṣrī was an Ottoman-Turkish Sufi poet and Khalwati master whose devotional verse and commentaries explore divine love and mystical realization. He became an influential figure in Ottoman Sufi culture and was exiled for his religious and political positions.
items.works: Dīvān; İrfān Sofraları; Mevāʾidü’l-ʿİrfān; commentaries on Ibn al-Fāriḍ and Sufi texts

items.title: Nafi Mawla Ibn Umar
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Nāfiʿ ibn Hurmuz (also reported as Sarjis or Kāwus) al-Madanī, mawlā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
items.description: A leading Medinan Successor and jurist, Nafi was the freedman and longtime scholarly companion of Abd Allah ibn Umar. He became one of the most trusted transmitters of hadith; the chain Malik–Nafi–Ibn Umar was especially esteemed by hadith critics.
items.works: No securely extant authored book; hadith and legal reports preserved in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and the canonical hadith collections

items.title: Anas ibn Malik
items.fullName: Anas ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Ḍamḍam ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, Abū Ḥamza
items.description: A Companion of Muhammad from the Khazraj clan of the Ansar, Anas served the Prophet in Medina for about ten years. One of the most prolific hadith transmitters, he preserved reports on the Prophet’s words, worship, and daily conduct and taught a later generation of scholars, including al-Hasan al-Basri.
items.works: No authored book securely attributed; hadith reports preserved in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and other collections

items.title: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
items.fullName: ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAmr ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Taym ibn Murra al-Taymiyya al-Qurashiyya, Umm al-Muʾminīn
items.description: Wife of Muhammad and daughter of Abu Bakr, Aisha became one of the foremost authorities on Prophetic hadith, law, Qur’anic interpretation, and early Muslim history. Companions and later Successors consulted her, and her transmitted reports became central to the preservation and interpretation of the Sunnah.
items.works: Hadith reports in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and other collections; legal opinions and historical reports preserved by later compilers; no authored book securely survives

items.title: Sulayman al-A'mash
items.fullName: Sulaymān ibn Mihrān al-Asadī al-Kāhilī, Abū Muḥammad, al-Aʿmash
items.description: A leading Kufan hadith transmitter and Qur’an reciter of the Successor generation, al-Aʿmash was renowned for his memory and broad transmission of reports. He transmitted from early authorities and taught major later traditionists and jurists.
items.works: No independent book securely attributed; hadith transmissions preserved in the major collections, including Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and in tafsīr and qirāʾāt literature

items.title: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ Aslam al-Qurashī al-Makkī
items.description: A leading Meccan jurist and hadith transmitter of Nubian origin, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ became the foremost legal authority of Mecca in the early Umayyad period. He was especially renowned for his knowledge of pilgrimage rites, and his legal opinions helped shape the early Meccan school of jurisprudence.
items.works: No complete authored work securely survives; legal opinions and Qur’anic commentary transmitted in works by Ibn Jurayj, ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī, and al-Ṭabarī

items.title: Dawud al-Tai
items.fullName: Abū Sulaymān Dāwūd ibn Nuṣayr al-Ṭāʾī
items.description: Dawud al-Tai was a Kufan jurist and ascetic who studied with Abu Hanifa before withdrawing from public life. Later Sufi literature revered him for renunciation and spiritual discipline; Ma'ruf al-Karkhi is counted among those associated with his teaching.
items.works: Ascetic sayings and teachings preserved in early Sufi biographical literature; no securely authenticated independent book is known.

items.title: Hammad ibn Abi Hanifa
items.fullName: Ḥammād ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit al-Taymī
items.description: Hammad was the son of Abu Hanifa and an early transmitter of his father’s legal teachings. He helped preserve the first generation of Hanafi doctrine, though biographical sources provide limited information about his own independent scholarly production.
items.works: Legal opinions and reports transmitted in early Hanafi sources; no independent book is securely extant.

items.title: Yahya ibn Abi Zaida
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾida al-Wāsiṭī
items.description: Yahya ibn Abi Zaida was a Kufan hadith transmitter and jurist associated with the scholarly circle of Abu Hanifa. He was remembered for his extensive hadith knowledge and scrupulous practice; his transmissions appear in early biographical and hadith literature.
items.works: Hadith transmissions preserved in later collections; no independent authored work is securely identified.

items.title: al-Fudayl ibn Iyad
items.fullName: al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ ibn Masʿūd al-Tamīmī al-Yarbūʿī al-Khurāsānī
items.description: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad was a celebrated ascetic and early Sufi who became known for repentance, sincerity, fear of God, and ethical admonition. His sayings were widely transmitted in Sufi and biographical works, and he influenced later ascetics including Bishr al-Hafi.
items.works: Sayings and sermons preserved in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ, Siyar aʿlām al-nubalāʾ, and other biographical collections; no authenticated standalone book survives.

items.title: al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah
items.fullName: al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khurāsānī al-Balkhī, Abū Muṭīʿ
items.description: Known as Abu Muti al-Balkhi, al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah was an early Hanafi jurist and judge of Balkh. He belonged to the formative eastern Hanafi tradition and is cited in transmission chains used by later Hanafi-Maturidi scholars. He is distinct from the later theologian Makhul al-Nasafi, also known as Abu Muti.
items.works: Legal and theological opinions preserved in later sources; no independently authored work can be securely identified.

items.title: Ismail ibn Hammad
items.fullName: Ismāʿīl ibn Ḥammād ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Kūfī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh
items.description: Ismail ibn Hammad, a grandson of Abu Hanifa, was a Hanafi jurist and judge who helped transmit the family’s legal tradition. Later Hanafi biographical sources name him among the links through which early Kufan doctrine reached scholars in Baghdad, including Abu Saʿid al-Bardaʿi.
items.works: Legal opinions and transmitted reports preserved in Hanafi sources; no securely authenticated independent book is known.

items.title: Isa ibn Aban
items.fullName: ʿĪsā ibn Abān ibn Ṣadaqa al-Baghdādī, Abū Mūsā
items.description: Isa ibn Aban was a leading early Hanafi scholar of legal theory. He helped develop arguments about the authority of reports and the methods of juristic reasoning, and his positions were cited by later usul al-fiqh writers even though most of his own writings do not survive independently.
items.works: Works on legal proofs and reports are attributed to him, including discussions known as Kitāb al-Ḥujaj and Akhbār al-wāḥid; his doctrines survive chiefly through later citations.

items.title: Abu Hafs al-Kabir
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Ḥafṣ ibn al-Zibrikān al-ʿIjlī al-Bukhārī, Abū Ḥafṣ al-Kabīr
items.description: Abu Hafs al-Kabir was a prominent Hanafi jurist of Bukhara, born in the mid-eighth century and a major figure in establishing the school in Transoxiana. He transmitted the teachings of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani, and later Bukharan Hanafi scholarship developed around his legacy.
items.works: Legal opinions and reports attributed to him in Hanafi biographical literature, including material known as Masāʾil Abī Ḥafṣ; no major independent work survives securely.

items.title: Abu Sulayman al-Juzjani
items.fullName: Mūsā ibn Sulaymān al-Jūzjānī, Abū Sulaymān
items.description: Abu Sulayman al-Juzjani was an early Hanafi transmitter who studied with Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani. He helped carry the foundational teachings of the Iraqi Hanafi school into Central Asia and stands in the transmission chains cited by later Maturidi theologians.
items.works: Transmissions associated with early Hanafi texts, including reports on al-Fiqh al-akbar and the Risāla ilā ʿUthmān al-Battī; no separate authored book is securely established.

items.title: Muhammad ibn Muqatil
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil al-Rāzī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh
items.description: Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Razi was an early Hanafi jurist and one of Abu Mansur al-Maturidi’s principal teachers. Through his own connection to Muhammad al-Shaybani, he helped transmit early Hanafi doctrine to the theological circles of Transoxiana.
items.works: Legal and theological reports transmitted in later Hanafi-Maturidi sources; no independently extant work is securely known.

items.title: Abu Hafs al-Saghir
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Bukhārī, Abū Ḥafṣ al-Ṣaghīr
items.description: Abu Hafs al-Saghir was a Bukharan Hanafi scholar associated with early efforts to preserve the biography and teachings of Abu Hanifa. He is known particularly through the early Hanafi biographical tradition and is placed in the transmission chain leading to later Transoxianan scholars.
items.works: Manāqib Abī Ḥanīfa, an early biographical work now lost or not securely extant in its original form.

items.title: Makhul ibn al-Fadl
items.fullName: Abū Muṭīʿ Makḥūl ibn al-Faḍl al-Nasafī
items.description: Abu Muti Makhul al-Nasafi was an early eastern Hanafi theologian whose work is a major witness to the development of doctrinal and heresiographical writing in Transoxiana. He should not be confused with the earlier Abu Muti al-Balkhi, al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah.
items.works: Kitāb al-Radd ʿalā al-bidaʿ wa-l-ahwāʾ al-ḍālla; al-Luʾluʾiyyāt. The former is a key early work in the eastern Hanafi heresiographical tradition.

items.title: Abu Nasr
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥusayn al-ʿIyāḍī al-Anṣārī al-Samarqandī, Abū Naṣr
items.description: Abu Nasr al-Iyadi was a Samarqandi Hanafi theologian counted among the teachers of Abu Mansur al-Maturidi. His role in transmitting early Hanafi doctrines is especially visible in later accounts of the intellectual lineage of Maturidi theology.
items.works: No securely authenticated independent work is known; remembered chiefly as a teacher and transmitter in Maturidi-Hanafi chains.

items.title: al-Karkhi
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿUbayd Allāh ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Karkhī
items.description: Abu al-Hasan al-Karkhi was one of the leading Hanafi jurists of Baghdad around the turn of the fourth/tenth century. His teaching and legal methodology shaped a major Iraqi branch of the school; among his students was Abu Bakr al-Jassas.
items.works: Uṣūl al-Karkhī, a foundational statement of Hanafi legal principles; legal opinions and commentarial discussions preserved by later jurists.

items.title: al-Saymari
items.fullName: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣaymarī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh
items.description: Abu Abd Allah al-Saymari was an Iraqi Hanafi jurist and biographer whose work preserves early reports about Abu Hanifa and his students. His compilation is a major source for the formative history of the Hanafi school, especially its Iraqi transmission lines.
items.works: Akhbār Abī Ḥanīfa wa-aṣḥābihī, an important biographical source for Abu Hanifa and his circle.

items.title: al-Halwani
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥalwānī, Abū Muḥammad
items.description: Abd al-Aziz al-Halwani, known as Shams al-Aʾimma, was a leading Transoxianan Hanafi jurist of the fifth/eleventh century. His teaching formed a key link between earlier Central Asian Hanafi doctrine and later authorities such as al-Sarakhsi.
items.works: Legal opinions and teachings transmitted by later Hanafi jurists; no comprehensive independent book is securely attributed to him.

items.title: al-Damighani
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Ḥaswiyya al-Dāmaghānī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh
items.description: Abu Abd Allah al-Damighani was a Hanafi jurist and judge who rose to prominence in Baghdad and served in senior judicial office. His legal writings and teaching belong to the Iraqi Hanafi tradition of the fifth/eleventh century.
items.works: Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar al-Ḥākim is attributed to him in biographical sources; other legal opinions are preserved through later Hanafi literature.

items.title: al-Zaranjari
items.fullName: Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Faḍl al-Zaranjarī, Abū al-Faḍl
items.description: Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Zaranji was a Hanafi jurist active in Bukhara and Merv. His biographical record places him in the eastern Hanafi scholarly network and lists Abd al-Aziz al-Halwani among his teachers; he also transmitted material about Abu Hanifa.
items.works: Manāqib Abī Ḥanīfa, an early Hanafi biographical work associated with him and preserved through the later transmission of reports.

items.title: al-Sadr al-Shahid
items.fullName: Ḥusām al-Dīn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿUmar ibn Māza al-Bukhārī, al-Ṣadr al-Shahīd
items.description: Al-Sadr al-Shahid was one of the leading Hanafi jurists of Bukhara in the sixth/twelfth century and a senior member of the scholarly Āl-i Maza family. He held judicial and teaching authority and was killed during the Qatwan campaign in 536/1141.
items.works: Kitāb al-Wāqiʿāt; writings on judicial practice including Adab al-qāḍī; legal opinions and fatwas preserved in the Hanafi tradition.

items.title: Qadikhan
items.fullName: Ḥasan ibn Manṣūr ibn Maḥmūd al-Uzjandī al-Farghānī, Fakhr al-Dīn, Qāḍīkhān
items.description: Qadi Khan was a highly influential Hanafi jurist of the sixth/twelfth century from Uzjand in the Ferghana region. His legal opinions became an important reference for later jurists and were frequently cited in Hanafi fatwa collections.
items.works: Fatāwā Qāḍīkhān

items.title: al-Kardari
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Sattār al-ʿImādī al-Kardarī, Abū al-Wajd, Shams al-Aʾimma
items.description: Shams al-Aʾimma al-Kardari was a Hanafi scholar from Bukhara whose legal and biographical writings were cited by later jurists. He belongs to the scholarly network of the seventh/thirteenth century and is associated in later transmission accounts with Fakhr al-Din al-Maymarghi.
items.works: Al-Radd wa-l-intiṣār; Manāqib al-Imām al-Aʿẓam; Mukhtaṣar fī bayān taʿrīfāt al-aḥkām, ascribed in biographical sources.

items.title: Taj al-Sharia
items.fullName: Umar ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Maḥbūbī, Tāj al-Sharīʿa
items.description: Taj al-Sharia was a Hanafi jurist of the Mahbubi scholarly family and the grandfather and teacher of Sadr al-Sharia al-Asghar, Ubayd Allah ibn Masud.
items.works: Legal teaching transmitted in the Mahbubi family;

items.title: Ala al-Din al-Bukhari
items.fullName: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Bukhārī
items.description: Ala al-Din Abd al-Aziz al-Bukhari was a prominent Hanafi jurist and legal theorist of the early eighth/fourteenth century. His commentary on the principles of al-Bazdawi became an important work in the school and was studied by later Hanafi scholars.
items.works: Kashf al-asrār fī sharḥ Uṣūl al-Pazdawī; Kitāb al-taḥqīq.

items.title: al-Saghnaqi
items.fullName: Ḥusām al-Dīn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥajjāj al-Saghnaqī
items.description: Husam al-Din al-Saghnaqi was a Hanafi jurist and commentator working in the late seventh/early eighth century AH. His writing engaged with the school’s legal-theoretical literature, and later Hanafi chains identify him as a teacher of Qiwam al-Din al-Kaki.
items.works: Ghāyat al-taḥqīq fī sharḥ al-Muntakhab al-Ḥusāmī, a commentary in Hanafi legal theory.

items.title: Qiwam al-Din al-Kaki
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Kākī al-Khujandī al-Sinjārī, Qiwām al-Dīn
items.description: Qiwam al-Din al-Kaki was a Hanafi jurist of the eighth/fourteenth century known for his commentaries on authoritative legal manuals. His scholarship helped develop the later commentarial tradition of the Hanafi school.
items.works: Miʿrāj al-dirāya fī sharḥ al-Hidāya; ʿUyūn al-madhāhib fī furūʿ al-madhāhib al-arbaʿa; Jāmiʿ al-asrār fī sharḥ al-Manār.

items.title: Jamal al-Din al-Malati
items.fullName: Yūsuf ibn Mūsā ibn Muḥammad al-Malāṭī, Jamāl al-Dīn
items.description: Jamal al-Din al-Malati was a Hanafi jurist and judge active in the eighth/ninth centuries AH. His concise legal work distilled earlier Hanafi doctrine and became part of the tradition of abridgment and commentary on the school’s manuals.
items.works: Al-Muʿtaṣar min al-Mukhtaṣar, a concise Hanafi legal compendium.

items.title: Qari al-Hidaya
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Fāris al-Kinānī, Sirāj al-Dīn, Qārī al-Hidāya
items.description: Siraj al-Din al-Kinani, known as Qari al-Hidaya, was a later Hanafi jurist whose name appears in scholarly transmission chains.Details of his life and literary production are limited in accessible biographical sources.
items.works: No independent work can be securely identified from the biographical evidence consulted.

items.title: Ibn Qutlubugha
items.fullName: Qāsim ibn Quṭlūbughā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Sūdūnī al-Jamālī, Zayn al-Dīn, Abū al-ʿAdl
items.description: Ibn Qutlubugha was a prolific Hanafi jurist and hadith scholar of Cairo who worked to verify legal opinions and assess the hadith evidence cited in Hanafi manuals. His biographical and takhrij works remain valuable references for later Hanafi scholarship.
items.works: Tāj al-tarājim; Munyat al-almaʿī fīmā fāta min takhrīj aḥādīth al-Hidāya; Taṣḥīḥ al-Qudūrī; Khulāṣat al-afkār.

items.title: Al-Quduri
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar al-Qudūrī
items.description: Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Quduri (973–1037) was a leading Hanafi jurist of Baghdad and one of the foremost authorities of the Iraqi Hanafi school in the early 5th/11th century. His concise legal manual, *Mukhtasar al-Quduri*, became one of the most influential foundational texts in Hanafi jurisprudence, while his comparative legal scholarship examined disagreements between the Hanafi and Shafiʿi schools.
items.works: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī, Al-Tajrīd fī Masāʾil al-Khilāf bayna al-Ḥanafiyya wa-al-Shāfiʿiyya, Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar al-Karkhī

items.title: al-Sakuni
items.fullName: Abū Khāzim ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Sakūnī al-Kindī al-Baṣrī
items.description: Abu Khazim al-Sakuni was a prominent Hanafi jurist and judge originally from Basra who served in Damascus, Kufa, and the Karkh district of Baghdad. He was renowned for his mastery of Hanafi jurisprudence, inheritance law, arithmetic, and judicial documentation, particularly legal records and court instruments.He was an important link in the transmission of early Hanafi legal scholarship.
items.works: Adab al-Qadi, Al-Fara'id, Al-Mahadir wa al-Sijillat

items.title: al-Qadi al-Sadr al-Bazdawi
items.fullName: Abū al-Maʿālī al-Qāḍī al-Ṣadr Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mujāhid ibn Abī al-Yusr al-Nasafī al-Bazdawī,
items.description: Abu al-Ma'ali Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bazdawi was a prominent Hanafi jurist, judge, and scholar from Bukhara. Born into the highly influential al-Bazdawi family of Islamic scholars, he was the nephew of the famous jurist Fakhr al-Islam al-Bazdawi and the son of Abu al-Yusr Muhammad al-Bazdawi. Known for his exceptional grasp of legal rulings, dialectics, and pleasant character, he served as a judge in Baghdad and Bukhara. During his pilgrimage to Mecca, he taught in Merv and Baghdad, passing on his transmissions to notable scholars.
items.works: His contributions survive primarily through the extensive transmissions and historical citations found in Hanafi sources.

items.title: Sadr al-Sharia al-Awwal
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn ‘Ubayd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm al-Maḥbūbī Jamāl al-Dīn Shams al-A’immah Sadr al-Sharia al-Awwal
items.description: Jamal al-Dīn Ahmad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Mahbubi, historically venerated as Sadr al-Shari'ah al-Awwal or Sadr al-Shari'ah al-Akbar, was an exceptionally brilliant Hanafi jurist and standard-bearer of Islamic legal science in Bukhara. Tracing his lineage back to the companion Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he hailed from the illustrious al-Mahbubi scholarly dynasty. He attained such mastery in law that he was popularly dubbed Abū Ḥanīfah al-Thānī. A multi-generational master, he anchored the Hanafi intellectual chain in Central Asia: his son was the esteemed Taj al-Shari'ah Mahmud, and his great-grandson was the famous Sadr al-Shari'ah al-Thani.
items.works: Talqih al-Uqul fi Furuq al-Manqul

items.title: Jamal al-Din Ubayd Allah
items.fullName: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmar al-Maḥbūbī Jamāl al-Dīn
items.description: Jamal al-Din Ubayd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Mahbubi was a stellar master of Hanafi law, widely revered in Bukhara as an unrivaled academic authority of his generation. Descending from the noble companion Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he anchored the elite al-Mahbubi lineage of Central Asian jurists.

items.title: Burhan al-Sharia
items.fullName: Maḥmūd ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Maḥbūbī, Burhān al-Sharīʿah
items.description: Mahmud ibn Ubayd Allah, was an eminent Hanafi jurist and author from the venerable al-Mahbubi family of Bukhara. A pivotal master in the classical Central Asian legal tradition, he is remembered for creating one of the most widely read legal texts in Islamic history. He designed this comprehensive legal manual specifically for his grandson and student, Sadr al-Shari'ah al-Thani, who would later write the famous commentary on it. His lineage and work form the definitive backbone of later Hanafi jurisprudence across the Ottoman, Mughal, and Central Asian domains

items.title: Mulla Khusrow
items.fullName: Molla Hüsrev Muḥammad ibn Ferāmurz ibn ʿAlī er-Rūmī
items.description: Mullā Khusraw was a monumental 15th-century Ottoman legal scholar, judge, and Shaykh al-Islam He served as an academic authority under Sultan Murad II and grew into an indispensable legal pillar for Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror His legal and theological texts established the academic equilibrium between empirical governance and textual jurisprudence that guided Ottoman Sharia courts until the modern era.
items.works: Durar al-Hukkam fi Sharh Ghurar al-Ahkam, Mirqat al-Wusul ilā ʿIlm al-Usul, Mir'at al-Usul

items.title: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad
items.fullName: Al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād al-Luʾluʾī al-Kūfī
items.description: Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Lu'lu'i was a major early Hanafi jurist and judge of Kufa. As one of the direct and most prominent students of Abu Hanifa, he played an essential role in dictating, codifying, and shaping the early foundational legal doctrines of the Hanafi school of thought. He briefly served as a judge (qadi) in Kufa and was a contemporary to companion students like Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani. He was highly regarded for his sharp legal acumen.
items.works: Al-Mujarrad, Adab al-Qadi, Al-Amali, Al-Khisal

items.title: al-Hinduwani
items.fullName: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Khaṭīb al-Balkhī al-Hinduwānī
items.description: Abu Ja'far al-Hinduwani was a towering 10th-century Hanafi jurist and standard-bearer of legal science in Balkh. Known across the Islamic world by the honorific title Abu Hanifah al-Saghir due to his exceptional intellectual brilliance and profound legal insight, he served as a primary academic authority in Transoxiana. He passed away in Bukhara and was buried in his hometown of Balkh
items.works: Al-Nawazil, Shuruh Adab al-Qadi, Kitab al-Shurut, Uyun al-Masa’il

items.title: Ibn Nujaym
items.fullName: Zayn al-Dīn ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Barakāt al-Miṣrī al-Ḥanafī
items.description: Zayn al-Din Ibn Nujaym was a phenomenal 16th-century Egyptian jurist, legal theorist, and legal authority who stood as one of the ultimate intellectual pillars of the later Hanafi school. Ibn Nujaym is celebrated for his profound systematic codification of Islamic legal maxims, which centuries later formed the foundational jurisprudence template for the Ottoman civil code.

items.title: Al-Haskafi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaṣkafī al-Dimashqī
items.description: Ala al-Din al-Haskafi was a towering 17th-century Syrian polymath, Mufti of Damascus, and master of the classical, later Hanafi school of legal thought. His family traces its origins to Hasankeyf in southeastern Anatolia, though he spent his life anchoring the intellectual circle of Ottoman Damascus.
items.works: Al-Durr al-Mukhtar, Ad-Durr al-Muntaqa, Ifadat al-Anwar

items.title: Khayr al-Din al-Ramli
items.fullName: Khayr al-Dīn ibn Aḥmad ibn Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī al-Ayyūbī al-Fārūqī al-Ramlī
items.description: Khayr al-Din al-Ramli was an influential 17th-century Hanafi mufti and scholar from Palestine. Educated at Al-Azhar, he became the region's top juristic authority, famed for blending legal theory with local custom regarding agrarian and women's rights.
items.works: Al-Fatawa al-Khayriyah, Al-Haqayiq al-Khafia fi Sharh al-Bahr al-Ra'iq

items.title: al-Tumurtashi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Tamartāshī al-Ghazzī al-Ḥanafī
items.description: Al-Timurtashi was a magnificent 16th-century Palestinian jurist, mufti, and legal theorist born and raised in Gaza. A key late-era authority of the Hanafi school, he traveled to Cairo and Damascus. He wrote dozens of works across jurisprudence, theology, and grammar.
items.works: Tanwir al-Absar, Mu'in al-Mufti,

items.title: Ibn Abi Sharif
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Sharīf al-Murrī al-Maqdisī al-Shāfiʿī
items.description: Kamal al-Din Ibn Abi Sharif was a celebrated 15th-century Shafi'i polymath, academic authority, and Mufti of Jerusalem. Born into a prominent scholarly family in the holy city, he studied under leading minds of the Mamluk era.
items.works: Al-Durr al-Lawami' bi-Tahrir Sharh Jam' al-Jawami, Al-Musamarah Sharh al-Musayarah,

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Khassaf
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn ʿAmr (also read ʿUmar) ibn Muhayr al-Shaybānī al-Khaṣṣāf
items.description: A leading early Hanafi jurist and mujtahid, al-Khassaf contributed to the development of judicial procedure, endowments, legal stratagems, and financial law. He served as a judge in Baghdad under the Abbasid caliphs al-Muʿtazz and al-Muhtadi. His work on the conduct of judges became foundational in Hanafi legal literature.
items.works: Adab al-qadi; Ahkam al-awqaf; Kitab al-Hiyal; Kitab al-Nafaqat; Kitab al-Rida. Some other works, including a book on taxation, are reported lost.

items.title: al-Hakim al-Shahid
items.fullName: Abū al-Faḍl Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Marwazī al-Balkhī, al-Ḥākim al-Shahīd
items.description: A major Hanafi jurist, hadith scholar, and Samanid vizier from Merv, al-Hakim al-Shahid held judicial office in Bukhara and became renowned for his learning and integrity. He was killed during a revolt while serving as vizier. His legal synthesis helped preserve and organize the foundational doctrine of the Hanafi school.
items.works: Al-Kafi, an influential abridgment and synthesis of the core legal works of Muhammad al-Shaybani.

items.title: Siraj al-Din al-Ushi
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad (also reported as Abū al-Ḥasan) Sirāj al-Dīn ʿAlī ibn ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Taymī al-Shahīdī al-Farghānī al-Ūshī
items.description: Al-Ushi was a Hanafi jurist, Maturidi theologian, hadith scholar, and judge from Osh in the Ferghana Valley. He is best known for a concise metrical creed that became widely studied in traditional Muslim education. He also compiled hadith material and wrote on Hanafi legal questions.
items.works: Al-Amali (also called Badʾ al-amali or al-Qasida al-lamiyya); al-Fatawa al-Sirajiyya; Nisab al-akhbar li-tadhkirat al-akhyar; Musnad Anas ibn Malik. His larger collection Ghurar al-akhbar wa-durar al-ashʿar is reported lost.

items.title: Ibn al-Sa'ati
items.fullName: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muẓaffar al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Taghlib al-Baʿlabakkī al-Baghdādī, Ibn al-Sāʿātī
items.description: Ibn al-Saati was a leading Hanafi jurist and legal theorist in Baghdad. The son of a clockmaker, he received advanced training in jurisprudence, legal theory, theology, Arabic, and literature, and taught at major Baghdad madrasas. His most influential writings combined and compared established works of Hanafi law and legal theory.
items.works: Majmaʿ al-bahrayn wa-multaqa al-nayyirayn; al-Badiʿ (also called Nihayat al-wusul ila ʿilm al-usul); Sharh Majmaʿ al-bahrayn.

items.title: Jamal al-Din al-Zayla'i
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad Jamāl al-Dīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Muḥammad al-Zaylaʿī
items.description: Al-Zaylaʿi was a Hanafi jurist and distinguished hadith specialist of Mamluk-era Cairo. He critically traced the hadith evidence cited in major Hanafi legal texts and recorded narrations and evaluations from earlier hadith scholars. His meticulous source criticism made his work an enduring reference for jurists and hadith researchers.
items.works: Nasb al-raya li-ahadith al-Hidaya; takhrij and commentary material concerning the hadith cited in al-Kashshaf.

items.title: Yahya al-Qattan
items.fullName: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd ibn Farrūkh al-Tamīmī al-Baṣrī, Abū Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān al-Aḥwal
items.description: Yahya al-Qattan was a leading Basran hadith scholar and one of the foremost early critics of hadith transmitters. Renowned for his exceptional memory, precision, and rigorous scrutiny of chains of transmission, he helped establish the methods of narrator criticism and the study of hidden defects in hadith. His critical methods profoundly influenced later authorities.
items.works: Al-Duʿafaʾ, Kitab al-Maghazi, A work on ʿIlal al-Hadith

items.title: Ibn Abi al-Dunya
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Sufyān ibn Qays al-Qurashī al-Baghdādī, Abū Bakr
items.description: Ibn Abi al-Dunya was a prominent Baghdad-based hadith scholar, Hanbali jurist, preacher, and prolific author of works on asceticism, ethics, and spiritual discipline. He compiled hadith and reports concerning patience, repentance, gratitude, humility, death, and the afterlife, preserving important early material on Muslim piety and moral education. He also served as tutor to the Abbasid caliph al-Mu'tadid and his son al-Muktafi.
items.works: Al-Samt wa Adab al-Lisan, Al-Zuhd, Al-Faraj baʿd al-Shidda, Makarim al-Akhlaq

items.title: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Marzubān ibn Sābūr ibn Shāhanshāh al-Baghawī, Abū al-Qāsim
items.description: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi was a distinguished Baghdad-based hadith scholar, hadith master, and transmitter renowned for his longevity and exceptional preservation of early Islamic reports. Encouraged by his maternal grandfather, Ahmad ibn Maniʿ, he began studying and recording hadith at a remarkably young age. His works on the Companions and hadith transmission remain valuable sources for early Islamic history and hadith scholarship.
items.works: Muʿjam al-Ṣaḥāba, Al-Jaʿdiyyāt,

items.title: Abdullah ibn Ahmad
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal ibn Hilāl ibn Asad al-Shaybānī al-Marwazī
items.description: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal was a prominent Baghdad-based hadith scholar, transmitter, and critic, and the son and principal transmitter of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. He preserved his father's extensive scholarly legacy, including the Musnad, while also compiling independent works on Sunni creed and hadith. His additions to his father's Musnad and Kitab al-Zuhd preserved important reports not transmitted through his father, making him an essential figure in the transmission of early Hanbali and hadith scholarship.
items.works: Kitāb al-Sunna, Zawāʾid ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ʿalā al-Musnad, Ziyādāt ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad fī Kitāb al-Zuhd, Al-ʿIlal wa-Maʿrifat al-Rijāl, riwāyat ʿAbd Allāh

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Marwadhi
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Marwadhī, Abū Bakr
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Marwadhi was a prominent Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, and ascetic, and one of the closest companions and principal students of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. He transmitted an extensive body of Ahmad's legal opinions, hadith reports, and teachings on asceticism and piety, becoming a major source for the early development of Hanbali jurisprudence. Renowned for his learning, devotion, and humility, he also transmitted reports about early Muslim scholars and their ethical conduct.
items.works: Kitāb al-Waraʿ, Akhbār al-Shuyūkh wa-Akhlāquhum, Masāʾil al-Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, riwāyat Abī Bakr al-Marwadhī

items.title: Harb al-Kirmani
items.fullName: Ḥarb ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Khalaf al-Ḥanẓalī al-Kirmānī, Abū Muḥammad
items.description: Harb al-Kirmani was a prominent hadith scholar, jurist, and early Hanbali authority of Persian origin. A close student and companion of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, he travelled extensively in pursuit of knowledge and became a leading transmitter of their legal opinions and theological teachings. His works preserve important early material on Sunni creed, jurisprudence, and the views of the traditionalist scholars, making him a significant source for the formative Hanbali tradition.
items.works: Masāʾil Ḥarb ibn Ismāʿīl, Kitāb al-Sunna min Masāʾil Ḥarb ibn Ismāʿīl al-Ḥanẓalī al-Kirmānī, Kitāb al-Sunna wa-l-Jamāʿa

items.title: al-Kawsaj
items.fullName: Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr ibn Bahrām al-Tamīmī al-Marwazī, Abū Yaʿqūb al-Kawsaj
items.description: Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Kawsaj was a prominent hadith scholar, jurist, and transmitter originally from Marw who later settled in Nishapur. He studied with leading authorities including Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, recording their answers to legal questions in a major early work of comparative jurisprudence. Widely respected for his memory, reliability, and ascetic devotion, he transmitted hadith preserved in the canonical Sunni collections and helped preserve the legal teachings of two leading scholars of the traditionalist movement.
items.works: Masāʾil al-Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal wa-Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh

items.title: Ibn Batta
items.fullName: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥamdān al-ʿUkbarī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Ibn Batta al-Ukbari was a prominent Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, and theologian who helped shape the development of early traditionalist Sunni theology. A devoted scholar and teacher, he travelled extensively to study hadith and jurisprudence before returning to Ukbara, where he taught for approximately forty years. His writings, particularly al-Ibana al-Kubra and al-Ibana al-Sughra, defended traditionalist Sunni doctrine and criticized theological positions he considered contrary to the teachings of the early Muslim generations.
items.works: Al-Ibana ʿan Shariʿat al-Firqa al-Najiya, Al-Sharh wa-l-Ibana ʿala Usul al-Sunna wa-l-Diyana, Ibtal al-Hiyal

items.title: al-Najjad
items.fullName: Aḥmad ibn Salmān ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus al-Baghdādī al-Ḥanbalī, Abū Bakr
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Najjad was a leading Baghdad-based Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, and transmitter renowned for his extensive knowledge of hadith and legal learning. He maintained two teaching circles at the Jamiʿ al-Mansur on Fridays, one for Hanbali legal opinions and another for dictating hadith. His extensive transmissions and writings contributed to the preservation of early Hanbali jurisprudence and hadith scholarship.
items.works: Al-Sunan, Musnad ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Al-Radd ʿalā man Yaqūl al-Qurʾān Makhluq, Al-Khilāf fī al-Fiqh,

items.title: al-Khiraqi
items.fullName: ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad al-Baghdādī al-Khiraqī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Umar al-Khiraqi was a prominent Baghdad-born Hanbali jurist and one of the formative authorities of the Hanbali school. His Mukhtasar, a concise manual of Ahmad ibn Hanbal's jurisprudence containing approximately 2,300 legal questions, became a foundational text for the school and inspired numerous commentaries, most famously Ibn Qudama's al-Mughni. After leaving Baghdad amid religious conflict, he settled in Damascus, where he died. Most of his other writings were lost when the house in which he had deposited his books burned.
items.works: Mukhtaṣar al-Khiraqī

items.title: al-Khallal
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Hārūn ibn Yazīd al-Baghdādī al-Ḥanbalī al-Khallāl
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Khallal was a leading Hanbali jurist and hadith scholar who systematically collected, organized, and transmitted the legal opinions of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Travelling extensively across Iraq, Persia, Syria, and the Jazira, he gathered reports from Ahmad's sons, disciples, and other transmitters, compiling them into an extensive legal corpus. His monumental *al-Jamiʿ li-ʿUlum al-Imam Ahmad* became foundational to the preservation and systematization of the Hanbali school, helping establish its doctrines as a coherent legal tradition.
items.works: Al-Jāmiʿ li-ʿUlūm al-Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, Al-Sunna, Al-ʿIlal, Ṭabaqāt Aṣḥāb Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal

items.title: al-Ajurri
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Baghdādī al-Ājurrī
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Ajurri was a prominent hadith scholar, jurist, and author whose writings helped preserve early Sunni traditionalist theology and Islamic ethics. Originally from Baghdad, he later settled in Mecca, where he taught and transmitted hadith for approximately thirty years. His Kitab al-Shari'a became an influential work on Sunni creed, while his writings on scholars' conduct, Quranic ethics, and religious discipline shaped later Islamic devotional literature. Biographical sources differ on whether he should be classified primarily as Shafi'i or Hanbali.
items.works: Kitāb al-Sharīʿa, Akhlāq al-ʿUlamāʾ, Akhlāq Ḥamalat al-Qurʾān

items.title: Ibn Mandah
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Mandah al-ʿAbdī al-Iṣbahānī
items.description: Ibn Mandah was a leading hadith master from Isfahan, renowned for his extensive travels in search of hadith, exceptional memorization, and prolific scholarship. He reportedly studied under approximately 1,700 teachers. His writings covered hadith transmission, Islamic faith, divine names and attributes, and the biographies of the Companions. His works, particularly Kitab al-Iman and Kitab al-Tawhid, became important sources for traditional Sunni theology and hadith scholarship.
items.works: Kitab al-Iman, Kitab al-Tawhid wa-Maʿrifat Asmaʾ Allah, Maʿrifat al-Sahaba, Fath al-Bab,

items.title: Ghulam al-Khallal
items.fullName: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn Yazdād al-Baghdādī
items.description: Abu Bakr Ghulam al-Khallal was a leading early Hanbali jurist, hadith transmitter, and Quran commentator in Baghdad. A close student of Abu Bakr al-Khallal, he helped preserve and develop the Hanbali legal tradition through extensive compilations of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal's rulings. His major jurisprudential works, including al-Shafi and al-Muqni, were highly regarded by later Hanbali authorities, who praised his mastery of the school.
items.works: Al-Shafi fi Fiqh al-Imam Ahmad, Al-Muqni, Zad al-Musafir, Al-Khilaf maʿa al-Shafiʿi

items.title: Ibn Shihab al-Ukbari
items.fullName: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Shihāb ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Shihāb al-ʿUkbarī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Ibn Shihab al-Ukbari was a prominent Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, Arabic grammarian, poet, and master calligrapher and copyist from Ukbara, Iraq. He was renowned for his extensive legal opinions and expertise in Hanbali jurisprudence, inheritance law, Arabic, and literature. A close companion and student of Ibn Battah, he helped preserve the early Hanbali tradition and was recognized for both his scholarship and exceptional handwriting. His writings included works on jurisprudence, inheritance, and grammar.
items.works: Risalat al-Ukbari fi Usul al-Fiqh,

items.title: Ibn al-Banna
items.fullName: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Bannāʾ al-Baghdādī al-Ḥanbalī al-Muqriʾ
items.description: Ibn al-Banna al-Hanbali was a prominent Baghdad-based Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, Quran reciter, grammarian, preacher, and prolific author. He studied jurisprudence under Qadi Abu Ya'la al-Farra and became an influential teacher who issued legal opinions and taught hadith in Baghdad's major mosques. His extensive writings included works on Hanbali jurisprudence, legal theory, Quranic recitation, and Arabic grammar. His surviving personal diary provides valuable contemporary evidence for the religious and intellectual life of eleventh-century Baghdad.
items.works: Al-Muqniʿ fi Sharh Mukhtasar al-Khiraqi, Sharh al-Idah li-Abi Ali al-Farisi, Al-Radd ʿala al-Mubtadiʿa

items.title: Majd al-Din Ibn Taymiyya
items.fullName: Majd al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Qāsim al-Khiḍr ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Khiḍr ibn ʿAlī ibn Taymiyya al-Ḥarrānī
items.description: Majd al-Din Ibn Taymiyya was a leading Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, Quran commentator, and authority in legal theory and Quranic recitation from Harran. Renowned for his mastery of Hanbali jurisprudence and comparative legal scholarship, he authored influential works including al-Muharrar fi al-Fiqh and al-Muntaqa fi al-Ahkam. He was the father of Shihab al-Din Abd al-Halim and grandfather of Taqi al-Din Ahmad Ibn Taymiyya, and helped establish the scholarly tradition continued by later generations of his family.
items.works: Al-Muntaqa fi al-Akhbar fi al-Ahkam, Al-Muharrar fi al-Fiqh, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim, Al-Ahkam al-Kubra

items.title: Ibn Hamdan
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Najm al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdān ibn Shabīb ibn Ḥamdān al-Numayrī al-Ḥarrānī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Najm al-Din Ibn Hamdan was a prominent Hanbali jurist, theologian, legal theorist, and man of letters from Harran. He became a leading authority on Hanbali jurisprudence and was also knowledgeable in hadith, legal disagreement, and theology. After travelling to Aleppo and Damascus, he settled in Cairo and served as a deputy judge. His writings on Hanbali law, creed, and the ethics of issuing legal opinions influenced later scholarship.
items.works: Al-Riʿāya al-Kubrā, Al-Riʿāya al-Ṣughrā, Ṣifat al-Muftī wa-l-Mustaftī, Nihāyat al-Mubtadiʾīn fī Uṣūl al-Dīn

items.title: Najm al-Din al-Tufi
items.fullName: Abū al-Rabīʿ Najm al-Dīn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Qawī ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Saʿīd al-Ṣarṣarī al-Ṭūfī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Najm al-Din al-Tufi was a Hanbali jurist, legal theorist, Qur’anic commentator, hadith scholar, theologian, and literary author from the Baghdad region. He became particularly known for his influential and controversial account of maṣlaḥa in Islamic legal theory. His extensive writings cover jurisprudence, legal methodology, Qur’anic exegesis, dialectics, Arabic literature, and Christian-Muslim polemics.
items.works: Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar al-Rawḍa, Al-Bulbul fī Uṣūl al-Fiqh, Al-Taʿyīn fī Sharḥ al-Arbaʿīn, Al-Ishārāt al-Ilāhiyya ilā al-Mabāḥith al-Uṣūliyya

items.title: Ibn Muflih
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Mufliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Mufarrij al-Maqdisī al-Rāmīnī al-Ṣāliḥī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Ibn Muflih al-Maqdisi was a leading Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, and legal author. Based in Damascus, he taught at several religious institutions and served as deputy judge to his father-in-law, the chief judge Jamal al-Din al-Mardawi. Renowned for his mastery of Hanbali jurisprudence and the opinions of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, he produced influential works on substantive law, legal theory, and Islamic ethics. His scholarship was closely connected with Ibn Taymiyya’s intellectual legacy.
items.works: Kitāb al-Furūʿ, Al-Ādāb al-Sharʿiyya wa-l-Minaḥ al-Marʿiyya, Al-Nukat wa-l-Fawāʾid al-Saniyya ʿalā Mushkil al-Muḥarrar

items.title: Ibn al-Mibrad
items.fullName: Abū al-Maḥāsin Jamāl al-Dīn Yūsuf ibn Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd al-Hādī al-Ṣāliḥī al-Dimashqī al-Ḥanbalī
items.description: Jamal al-Din Ibn al-Mibrad was a prolific Hanbali jurist and hadith scholar from Damascus, descended from the scholarly milieu of al-Salihiyya. He taught at Damascene madrasas and briefly served as a deputy judge. He authored hundreds of books and treatises spanning Hanbali jurisprudence, legal theory, hadith criticism, biography, local history, Prophetic biography, and Sufism, becoming an important transmitter of late-medieval Hanbali scholarship.
items.works: Mughnī dhawī al-afhām, Al-Durr al-naqī fī sharḥ alfāẓ al-Khiraqī, Ghāyat al-sūl ilā ʿilm al-uṣūl

items.title: Ibn Balban
items.fullName: Shams al-Dīn Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Badr al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Qādir ibn Muḥammad ibn Balbān al-Baʿlī
items.description: Ibn Balban al-Hanbali was a leading Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, teacher, and author in Ottoman-era Damascus. Although affiliated with the Hanbali school, he taught and issued legal opinions across all four Sunni legal schools. He became a major scholarly authority in the Ṣāliḥiyya quarter and authored concise, influential manuals on Hanbali jurisprudence, religious etiquette, creed, and Qur'anic recitation.
items.works: Akhaṣar al-Mukhtaṣarāt, Kāfī al-Mubtadī min al-Ṭullāb, Mukhtaṣar al-Ifādāt, Qalāʾid al-ʿIqyān

items.title: Abu al-Mawahib
items.fullName: Abū al-Mawāhib Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn ʿAbd al-Bāqī ibn ʿAbd al-Qādir
items.description: Abu al-Mawahib al-Hanbali was a prominent Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, Qur'anic reciter, teacher, and mufti of Damascus during the Ottoman period. Born into a scholarly family originally from Baalbek, he studied with leading scholars in Damascus, the Hijaz, and Egypt. He succeeded his father as a major authority among Damascus's Hanbalis, taught numerous students, and produced works on hadith transmission, Qur'anic recitation, exegesis, and religious practice. He was also known for his engagement with Sufi scholarship.
items.works: Fayḍ al-Wudūd, Al-Kawākib al-Zāhira, Fayḍ al-Makārim, Tuḥfat al-Anām

items.title: al-Saffarini
items.fullName: Shams al-Dīn Abū al-ʿAwn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Sālim ibn Sulaymān al-Saffārīnī
items.description: Muhammad al-Saffarini was a prominent Hanbali jurist, hadith scholar, theologian, historian, and poet from Nablus, Palestine. After studying with leading scholars in Damascus and Medina, he returned to Nablus, where he taught, issued fatwas, and became an influential authority in Hanbali jurisprudence and Athari theology. His extensive writings covered Islamic creed, legal rulings, hadith commentary, ethics, and the Hereafter.
items.works: Lawāmiʿ al-Anwār al-Bahiyya, Ghidhāʾ al-Albāb, Al-Durra al-Muḍiyya, Kashf al-Lithām,

items.title: Al-Buwayti
items.fullName: Abū Yaʿqūb Yūsuf ibn Yaḥyā al-Qurashī al-Miṣrī al-Buwayṭī
items.description: Abu Yaqub al-Buwayti was a leading Egyptian jurist and one of Imam al-Shafiʿi’s closest disciples. After al-Shafiʿi’s death, he succeeded him in leading the Shafiʿi teaching circle in Egypt and helped preserve the school’s early legal doctrines. During the Abbasid inquisition over the createdness of the Qur’an, he refused to affirm the doctrine and was transported in chains from Egypt to Baghdad, where he died in prison. He is remembered for both his jurisprudence and steadfastness under persecution.
items.works: Mukhtaṣar al-Buwayṭī

items.title: Ibn al-Mundhir
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jārūd al-Naysābūrī
items.description: Ibn al-Mundhir was a leading hadith scholar and jurist renowned for his comparative study of Islamic law. Based in Mecca, he became an authoritative teacher and mufti of the Sacred Mosque. Although associated with the Shafiʿi tradition, he was recognized for independent legal reasoning and refused to confine himself rigidly to any single school's opinions. His systematic comparisons of juristic disagreements, evidence, and scholarly consensus made him a major early authority in comparative jurisprudence.
items.works: Al-Awsaṭ min al-Sunan wa-l-Ijmāʿ wa-l-Ikhtilāf, Al-Ishrāf ʿalā Madhāhib Ahl al-ʿIlm, Kitāb al-Ijmāʿ

items.title: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Sulayman al-Muradi
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn Kāmil al-Murādī
items.description: Al-Rabi ibn Sulayman al-Muradi was an Egyptian hadith scholar, jurist, and the foremost transmitter of Imam al-Shafiʿi’s later teachings and writings. A close disciple of al-Shafiʿi in Egypt, he preserved and transmitted foundational works including al-Umm and al-Risala, making him central to the formation and transmission of the Shafiʿi school. He also transmitted hadith from numerous Egyptian and other scholars and taught leading traditionists.
items.works: Al-Rabiʿ is chiefly known as a transmitter rather than as an independent author.

items.title: al-Anmati
items.fullName: Abū al-Qāsim ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd ibn Bashshār al-Baghdādī al-Anmāṭī al-Aḥwal
items.description: Abu al-Qasim al-Anmati was a leading early Shafiʿi jurist and hadith transmitter in Baghdad. He helped establish the Shafiʿi school in Iraq by encouraging the copying, memorization, and teaching of al-Shafiʿi's legal works. His students included Abu al-Abbas ibn Surayj, one of the most important early authorities in the development of Iraqi Shafiʿi jurisprudence.
items.works: No independently authored book is securely attributed to Abu al-Qasim al-Anmati in the principal biographical sources.

items.title: Abu Ishaq al-Marwazi
items.fullName: Ibrāhīm ibn Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq al-Marwazī
items.description: Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist who succeeded Ibn Surayj as the foremost authority of the school in Baghdad. He later moved to Egypt, where he continued teaching and became a major figure in transmitting and consolidating Shāfiʿī jurisprudence.
items.works: Sharḥ Mukhtaṣar al-Muzanī, Al-Fuṣūl fī Maʿrifat al-Uṣūl, Al-Shurūṭ wa-l-Wathāʾiq

items.title: Al-Khattabi
items.fullName: Abu Sulayman Hamd ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Khattab al-Busti
items.description: Al-Khattabi was a Shafiʿi jurist, hadith scholar, philologist, and commentator from Bust. He travelled to major centers of learning, including Nishapur, Baghdad, Basra, and Mecca. He became renowned for his explanations of hadith and his work on difficult vocabulary in prophetic traditions.
items.works: Maʿalim al-Sunan, Aʿlam al-Hadith, Gharib al-Hadith, Kitab al-ʿUzla, Islah Ghalat al-Muhaddithin

items.title: Al-Qadi Husayn al-Marwarudhi
items.fullName: Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Marwarudhi
items.description: Al-Qadi Husayn was a leading Shafi'i jurist of Khurasan and a major authority in the school's legal tradition. A prominent student of Abu Bakr al-Qaffal al-Marwazi, he was known for his precise legal analysis and distinctive positions within the madhhab. His Ta'liqa became an important reference for later Shafi'i scholars.
items.works: Al-Ta'liqa al-Kubra, Al-Fatawa, Ta'liqa fi al-Fiqh

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Qaffal al-Marwazi
items.fullName: Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Marwazi
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Qaffal al-Marwazi was a leading Shafi'i jurist of Khurasan and a major authority in the regional tradition of Shafi'i jurisprudence. Originally trained as a locksmith, he turned to the study of law at around thirty and became renowned for his legal scholarship and teaching. He is known as the Qaffal al-Saghir.
items.works: Al-Marwaziyyat

items.title: Abu Muhammad al-Juwayni
items.fullName: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Hayyuya al-Juwayni
items.description: Abu Muhammad al-Juwayni was a leading Shafi'i jurist, legal theorist, Qur'anic exegete, grammarian, and scholar of hadith in Nishapur. He studied in Nishapur and Merv, became a prominent teacher and legal authority, and was the father and first teacher of Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni. He was known for his careful legal reasoning and extensive scholarly output.
items.works: Al-Tafsir al-Kabir, Al-Tabsira wa-l-Tadhkira, Al-Jamʿ wa-l-Farq, Al-Wasaʾil fi Furuq al-Masaʾil

items.title: Abu al-Tayyib al-Tabari
items.fullName: Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir ibn Umar al-Tabari
items.description: Abu al-Tayyib al-Tabari was a leading Shafi'i jurist, legal scholar, hadith transmitter, and judge in 11th-century Baghdad. Appointed judge in the Karkh district in 436 AH, he became one of the foremost authorities of the Iraqi Shafi'i school.
items.works: Sharh Mukhtasar al-Muzani, Rawdat al-Muntaha, Al-Ta'liqa al-Kubra

items.title: Abu Uthman al-Sabuni
items.fullName: Abu Uthman Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Naysaburi al-Sabuni
items.description: Abu Uthman al-Sabuni was a leading Shafi'i jurist, hadith scholar, Qur'anic exegete, preacher, and theologian of Nishapur. Widely honored as Shaykh al-Islam in Khurasan, he defended Sunni doctrine and taught hadith for many years.
items.works: Aqidat al-Salaf wa-Ashab al-Hadith, Tafsir al-Sabuni, Al-Wasiyya

items.title: Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani
items.fullName: Abu Nu'aym Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Mihran al-Isfahani
items.description: Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani was a leading Shafi'i hadith scholar, historian, and author on asceticism and Sufism. He travelled extensively to collect hadith and became renowned for his large body of transmissions and high-level chains of narration.
items.works: Hilyat al-Awliya wa-Tabaqat al-Asfiya, Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, Dhikr Akhbar Isbahan

items.title: Al-Khatib al-Shirbini
items.fullName: Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Khatib al-Shirbini
items.description: Al-Khatib al-Shirbini was an Egyptian Shafi'i jurist, Qur'anic exegete, theologian, and Arabic-language scholar. After studying with leading scholars in Cairo, he received authorization to teach and issue legal opinions while his teachers were still alive. He became known for his major commentaries on al-Nawawi's Minhaj al-Talibin, Abu Shuja's al-Ghaya wa-l-Taqrib, and the Qur'an.
items.works: Mughni al-Muhtaj, Al-Iqna', Al-Siraj al-Munir, Sharh al-Tanbih

items.title: Shihab al-Din al-Ramli
items.fullName: Shihab al-Din Ahmad ibn Hamza al-Ansari al-Ramli
items.description: Shihab al-Din al-Ramli was a leading Egyptian Shafi'i jurist, mufti, and teacher of the 10th/16th century. A prominent student of Zakariyya al-Ansari, he became a major authority in Shafi'i jurisprudence and was permitted to edit his teacher's writings. His legal opinions and commentaries influenced later Shafi'i scholarship, and his son Shams al-Din al-Ramli succeeded him as a leading jurist.
items.works: Fath al-Rahman, Fath al-Jawad, Ghayat al-Ma'mul, Hashiya ala Asna al-Matalib

items.title: Nur al-Din al-Haythami
items.fullName: Nur al-Din Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abi Bakr ibn Sulayman al-Haythami
items.description: Nur al-Din al-Haythami was an Egyptian Shafi'i hadith scholar and hadith master who devoted his life to collecting, organizing, and evaluating Prophetic traditions.
items.works: Majma al-Zawa'id wa-Manba al-Fawa'id, Mawarid al-Zam'an ila Zawa'id Ibn Hibban

items.title: Wali al-Din al-'Iraqi
items.fullName: Abu Zur'a Wali al-Din Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Iraqi
items.description: Wali al-Din al-'Iraqi was an Egyptian Shafi'i jurist, hadith master, legal theorist, and Qur'anic scholar. Trained first by his father, Zayn al-Din al-'Iraqi, he became a leading authority in hadith and Shafi'i jurisprudence, taught at prominent institutions in Cairo, and served as chief judge of Egypt in 824 AH. His scholarship continued his father's hadith tradition and influenced major scholars of the following generation.
items.works: Al-Ghayth al-Hami' Sharh Jam' al-Jawami, Mukhtasar al-Muhimmat

items.title: Jamal al-Din al-Isnawi
items.fullName: Jamal al-Din Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahim ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Umawi al-Qurashi al-Isnawi
items.description: Jamal al-Din al-Isnawi was a leading Egyptian Shafi'i jurist, legal theorist, Qur'anic scholar, and grammarian. He taught at prominent madrasas in Cairo and became a major authority in Shafi'i jurisprudence. His works addressed substantive law, legal theory, Arabic grammar, and the biographies of Shafi'i scholars.
items.works: Nihayat al-Sul, Al-Muhimmat fi Sharh al-Rawda, Tabaqat al-Shafi'iyya

items.title: Ibn al-Mulaqqin
items.fullName: Sirāj al-Dīn Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad al-Anṣārī
items.description: Ibn al-Mulaqqin was a major Egyptian Shafi‘i jurist and hadith specialist of the eighth Islamic century. Of Andalusian family origin, he studied jurisprudence, hadith, Qur’anic studies, and Arabic grammar, eventually becoming a teacher, deputy judge, and extraordinarily prolific author. He reportedly produced hundreds of works, particularly commentaries on hadith collections and Shafi‘i legal texts.
items.works: Al-Tawḍīḥ li-Sharḥ al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Al-Badr al-Munīr fī Takhrīj Aḥādīth al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr, Tuḥfat al-Muḥtāj ilā Adillat al-Minhāj

items.title: Salah al-Din al-Ala'i
items.fullName: Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn Abū Saʿīd Khalīl ibn Kaykaldī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAlāʾī
items.description: Al-Ala'i was a leading Shafi‘i scholar of the Mamluk period, particularly renowned for his mastery of hadith transmission, narrator criticism, hidden defects in hadith, and legal theory. He studied in Damascus and travelled widely in pursuit of knowledge, learning from a very large number of scholars. He taught in Damascus and later served at the Ṣalāḥiyya madrasa in Jerusalem.
items.works: Jāmiʿ al-Taḥṣīl fī Aḥkām al-Marāsīl, Ithārat al-Fawāʾid al-Majmūʿa,

items.title: Qutb al-Din al-Razi
items.fullName: Quṭb al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Rāzī al-Rāzī
items.description: Qutb al-Din al-Razi was an influential scholar of post-classical Islamic philosophy and logic. He also studied Islamic jurisprudence and Qur’anic exegesis. His writings helped shape later madrasa curricula in logic, philosophical theology, and legal theory. He is especially known for his commentaries on the logical works of Siraj al-Din al-Urmawi and Najm al-Din al-Katibi, and for his critical comparison of the interpretations of Ibn Sina offered by Fakhr al-Din al-Razi and Nasir al-Din al-Tusi.
items.works: Taḥrīr al-Qawāʿid al-Manṭiqiyya, Lawāmiʿ al-Asrār, Al-Muḥākamāt

items.title: Ibn Jama'ah
items.fullName: Badr al-Dīn Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Jamāʿah
items.description: Ibn Jamaʿah was a leading Shafi‘i scholar of the Mamluk period, known for his work in jurisprudence, hadith, Qur’anic studies, education, and political thought. He served as a judge in Jerusalem, Cairo, and Damascus, and held major teaching and preaching positions, including in the al-Aqsa Mosque and the Umayyad Mosque. His treatise on the ethics of teachers and students became particularly influential in Islamic educational literature.
items.works: Tadhkirat al-Sāmiʿ wa-l-Mutakallim, Taḥrīr al-Aḥkām fī Tadbīr Ahl al-Islām, Al-Manhal al-Rawī

items.title: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id
items.fullName: Taqī al-Dīn Abū al-Fatḥ Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ṭāʿa
items.description: Ibn Daqiq al-ʿId was one of the foremost jurists and hadith scholars of the late Ayyubid and early Mamluk periods. He achieved deep expertise in both the Shafi‘i and Maliki schools, studied hadith transmission and criticism under leading authorities, and served as chief judge in Egypt. His scholarship was particularly distinguished by his careful analysis of legal evidence, the meanings of prophetic reports, and the principles of jurisprudence. His major works remain influential in hadith-based jurisprudence.
items.works: Iḥkām al-Aḥkām, Al-Imām, Al-Ilmām, Al-Iqtirāḥ, Tuḥfat al-Labīb

items.title: Ibn al-Rif'ah
items.fullName: Najm al-Dīn Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Anṣārī al-Miṣrī
items.description: Ibn al-Rifʿah was a leading Egyptian Shafi‘i jurist during the late Ayyubid and early Mamluk periods. He served as Cairo’s muḥtasib—an official responsible for market supervision and public conduct—and also held judicial responsibilities. He became particularly renowned for his extensive commentaries on foundational Shafi‘i legal manuals. His scholarship was highly regarded by later jurists, who drew on his detailed treatment of disputed questions within the school.
items.works: Al-Maṭlab fī Sharḥ al-Wasīṭ, Kifāyat al-Nabīh, Badhl al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Sharʿiyya

items.title: Ibn al-Wardi
items.fullName: Zayn al-Dīn Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn al-Muẓaffar ibn ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Fawāris
items.description: Ibn al-Wardi was a Syrian Shafi‘i jurist, historian, literary author, grammarian, and poet of the Mamluk period. He held judicial positions in northern Syria, including in Manbij, and became known for his writing across several disciplines. His historical work continued the chronicle of Abu al-Fida, while his poetry and grammatical compositions circulated widely. He also wrote on Sufism and composed verse summarizing Shafi‘i jurisprudence.
items.works: Tārīkh Ibn al-Wardi, Bahjat al-Ḥāwī, Dīwān Ibn al-Wardi, Taḥrīr al-Khaṣāṣa fī Taysīr al-Khulāṣa

items.title: Safi al-Din al-Hindi
items.fullName: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Muḥammad, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ṣafī al-Dīn al-Hindī
items.description: Al-Hindī left India and travelled through Yemen and the Ḥijāz, visited Egypt and Anatolia, and settled in Damascus in 685 AH. There he taught, wrote legal and theological works, and became known for his command of Ashʿarī theology and legal theory. He was also summoned to participate in a theological disputation involving Ibn Taymiyya in Damascus
items.works: Nihāyat al-Wuṣūl fī Dirāyat al-Uṣūl, Al-Fāʾiq, Al-Zubda

items.title: al-Dimyati
items.fullName: Sharaf al-Dīn ʿAbd al-Muʾmin ibn Khalaf ibn Abī al-Ḥasan al-Tūnī al-Dimyāṭī
items.description: Abu Muhammad Sharaf al-Din al-Dimyati was a leading Egyptian Shafiʿi hadith master, jurist, Quran reciter, linguist, and genealogist. Born near Damietta, he travelled extensively through Egypt, the Hijaz, Syria, Iraq, and other regions in pursuit of hadith, compiling a biographical dictionary of approximately 1,250 teachers in four volumes. Praised by al-Dhahabi and al-Mizzi for his exceptional memory and scholarship, he became a major authority in hadith transmission and the study of genealogies.
items.works: Al-Mutajir al-Rabih fi Thawab al-ʿAmal al-Salih, Kashf al-Mughatta, Mukhtasar fi Sirat Sayyid al-Bashar, Fadl al-Khayl

items.title: Kamal al-Din Ibn Yunus
items.fullName: Kamāl al-Dīn Mūsā ibn Yūnus ibn Muḥammad ibn Manʿa ibn Mālik
items.description: Kamāl al-Dīn Mūsā ibn Yūnus al-Mawṣilī was a leading Shāfiʿī jurist and polymath of Mosul, renowned for his mastery of mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, medicine, and the religious sciences. He studied in Baghdad and taught for decades in Mosul, attracting students from across the Islamic world and beyond. He wrote on geometry, logic, astronomy, Quranic exegesis, and jurisprudence.
items.works: Sharḥ Risāla fīmā Yaḥtāju Ilayhi al-Ṣāniʿ, Risāla fī Bayān Muqaddimatayn, Risāla fī al-Burhān

items.title: Ibn al-Qasim
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim ibn Khālid al-ʿAtqī al-Miṣrī
items.description: Ibn al-Qasim was a leading Egyptian jurist and one of the most important early authorities of the Maliki school. He studied with Malik ibn Anas for approximately twenty years and became renowned for his mastery of Malik's legal opinions and his own juristic reasoning. His extensive answers to legal questions, transmitted through Asad ibn al-Furat and Sahnun, formed a principal foundation of the Mudawwana, one of the most influential works of Maliki jurisprudence. He helped establish and transmit the school throughout North Africa.
items.works: The extensive corpus of legal questions and answers transmitting Malik ibn Anas's positions

items.title: Ibn Wahb
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb ibn Muslim
items.description: Ibn Wahb was a leading Egyptian Maliki jurist and hadith scholar, renowned for his memory, legal reasoning, and extensive transmission of hadith. He studied with Malik ibn Anas for approximately twenty years and became one of the principal transmitters of Malik's legal teachings. His compilations preserved a vast body of hadith and jurisprudence and helped establish the Maliki school in Egypt and North Africa. Offered a judicial appointment, he reportedly withdrew from public view rather than accept the office.
items.works: Al-Jamiʿ li-Ibn Wahb, Kitab al-Qadar, Al-Muwattaʾ

items.title: Asad ibn al-Furat
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Asad ibn al-Furāt ibn Sinān
items.description: Asad ibn al-Furat was a prominent jurist, hadith scholar, judge of Kairouan, and military commander who played a major role in the development of Islamic jurisprudence in Ifriqiya. Born in Harran and raised in North Africa, he studied Hanafi jurisprudence in Iraq under Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani, and Maliki jurisprudence with Malik ibn Anas and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim. His legal compilation, al-Asadiyya, became an important early source for Maliki jurisprudence. In 827, he led the Aghlabid campaign against Sicily and died during the siege of Syracuse.
items.works: Al-Asadiyya

items.title: Abu Imran al-Fasi
items.fullName: Abū ʿImrān Mūsā ibn ʿĪsā ibn Abī Ḥājj al-Ghafjūmī al-Zanātī al-Fāsī
items.description: Abu Imran al-Fasi was a leading Maliki jurist, hadith scholar, theologian, and Quran reciter originally from Fez who settled in Kairouan. He studied with major scholars in the Maghrib, al-Andalus, Egypt, Mecca, and Baghdad, including Abu al-Hasan al-Qabisi, Abu Muhammad al-Asili, and the theologian Abu Bakr al-Baqillani. His teaching helped consolidate Maliki jurisprudence and Ashʿari theology in the western Islamic lands. Through his student Wajjaj ibn Zalwi, he also played an indirect role in the scholarly network that produced the Almoravid movement.
items.works: Taʿaliq ʿala al-Mudawwana, Al-Fahrasah, Taʿaliq fi Tarajim

items.title: Abu Amr al-Dani
items.fullName: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd ibn ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd Ibn al-Ṣayrafī al-Dānī
items.description: Abu Amr al-Dani was a leading Andalusi Maliki scholar of Quranic readings, recitation, Quranic script, vocalization, and hadith. His al-Taysir became one of the defining manuals of the Seven Readings, while Jamiʿ al-Bayan offered a comprehensive treatment of their transmissions. His writings on Quranic orthography, verse numbering, pronunciation, and stopping points became foundational references in the study and teaching of the Quran. He reportedly authored more than 120 works.
items.works: Al-Taysir fi al-Qiraʾat al-Sabʿ, Jamiʿ al-Bayan fi al-Qiraʾat al-Sabʿ, Al-Muqniʿ

items.title: Abu al-Hasan al-Qabisi
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-Qābisī
items.description: Abu al-Hasan al-Qabisi was a leading Maliki jurist, hadith master, legal theorist, theologian, and educator from Kairouan. After studying in Ifriqiya and travelling east to Mecca, Egypt, and other scholarly centres, he became the foremost Maliki authority in Kairouan following the death of Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani. He helped establish the transmission of Sahih al-Bukhari and Sunan al-Nasa'i in the Maghrib and contributed to the spread of Ash'ari theology in Ifriqiya. His influential treatise on teachers and students is an important source for the history of Islamic education.
items.works: Al-Risala al-Mufassala, Kitab Mulakhkhas al-Muwattaʾ, Al-Mumahhad

items.title: Makki ibn Abi Talib
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib Ḥammūsh ibn Muḥammad
items.description: Makki ibn Abi Talib al-Qaysi was a leading Maliki jurist, Quran exegete, grammarian, and authority on Quranic readings and recitation. Born in Kairouan, he travelled extensively to study in Egypt and the Hijaz before settling in Córdoba in 393 AH/1003 CE, where he taught Quranic readings at the city's congregational mosque. His works, particularly al-Tabsira, al-Kashf, and al-Hidaya ila Bulugh al-Nihaya, became important references in Quranic recitation, orthography, and interpretation. He helped transmit the developing scholarly tradition of the Seven Readings to al-Andalus.
items.works: Al-Hidaya ila Bulugh al-Nihaya, Al-Tabsira fi al-Qiraʾat al-Sabʿ, Al-Kashf ʿan Wujuh al-Qiraʾat al-Sabʿ, Al-Ibana ʿan Maʿani al-Qiraʾat

items.title: Abu al-Walid al-Baji
items.fullName: Abū al-Walīd Sulaymān ibn Khalaf ibn Saʿdūn ibn Ayyūb al-Bājī
