items.description: Abu al-Walid al-Baji was a leading Andalusi Maliki jurist, hadith scholar, theologian, legal theorist, and poet. After extensive travels through the Hijaz, Iraq, Syria, Egypt, and the Jazira, he returned to al-Andalus and became one of the foremost authorities of the Maliki school. His works on jurisprudence, legal theory, hadith criticism, and theological argument helped consolidate Maliki scholarship in the western Islamic world. He was also renowned for his debates with Ibn Hazm and his influential commentary on Malik ibn Anas's al-Muwatta.
items.works: Ihkam al-Fusul, Al-Minhaj, Al-Tasdid ila Maʿrifat al-Tawhid,

items.title: Qadi Abd al-Wahhab
items.fullName: Qāḍī Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAlī ibn Naṣr
items.description: Qadi Abd al-Wahhab al-Baghdadi was a leading Iraqi Maliki jurist, legal theorist, judge, theologian, and poet. He played a pivotal role in developing the Iraqi branch of the Maliki school, systematizing its jurisprudence and legal theory, and defending its positions through comparative legal argument. After serving as a judge in Iraq, he moved to Egypt, where he continued teaching and died in Cairo.
items.works: Al-Talqin fi al-Fiqh al-Maliki, Al-Ma'una, Al-Ishraf ʿala Nukat Masaʾil al-Khilaf, ʿUyun al-Majalis

items.title: Ibn al-Faradi
items.fullName: Abū al-Walīd ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf ibn Naṣr
items.description: Ibn al-Faradi was an Andalusi historian, hadith master, jurist, and man of letters from Córdoba. He travelled east for pilgrimage and scholarly study, collecting transmissions from scholars in the Hijaz, Egypt, and Ifriqiya. He served as a judge in Valencia and Écija and authored Tarikh Ulama al-Andalus, a foundational biographical source on Andalusi scholars, judges, hadith transmitters, and poets.
items.works: Tarikh Ulama al-Andalus, Al-Muʾtalif wa-al-Mukhtalif, Al-Mutashabih

items.title: Abu Bakr al-Turtushi
items.fullName: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭurṭūshī
items.description: Abu Bakr al-Turtushi was a leading Andalusi Maliki jurist, hadith scholar, theologian, and political ethicist. After studying in Zaragoza and travelling throughout the eastern Islamic lands, he settled in Alexandria, where he taught a large circle of students. His Siraj al-Muluk became an influential work of political advice, discussing governance, justice, and the moral responsibilities of rulers. He also wrote important works on Maliki jurisprudence and religious innovation, helping transmit Andalusi scholarship to Egypt and the wider Islamic world.
items.works: Siraj al-Muluk, Kitab al-Hawadith, Birr al-Walidayn,

items.title: Abu al-Qasim al-Shatibi
items.fullName: Abū Muḥammad al-Qāsim ibn Fīrruh ibn Khalaf al-Shāṭibī
items.description: Abu al-Qasim al-Shatibi was a leading Andalusi Quranic reciter, hadith scholar, grammarian, and poet who settled in Cairo. Blind from birth, he became renowned for his exceptional memory and mastery of Quranic readings. His poem Hirz al-Amani wa-Wajh al-Tahani, known as the Shatibiyya, systematized the Seven Readings and became a foundational text memorized and taught by generations of reciters. His other poems treat Quranic orthography and verse-counting. He taught at Cairo's Faziliyya school and attracted students from across the Islamic world.
items.works: Hirz al-Amani wa-Wajh al-Tahani(al-Shatibiyya), ʿAqilat Atrab al-Qasaʾid

items.title: Khalil ibn Ishaq
items.fullName: Khalīl ibn Isḥāq ibn Mūsā ibn Shuʿayb al-Jundī
items.description: Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Jundi was a leading Egyptian Maliki jurist, hadith scholar, grammarian, and legal theorist. He taught and issued legal opinions in Cairo and Alexandria, eventually becoming a prominent teacher at the Shaykhuniyya school. His Mukhtasar distilled the authoritative positions of Maliki jurisprudence into an exceptionally concise manual that became a standard reference across North and West Africa. His other major work, al-Tawdih, is an extensive commentary on Ibn al-Hajib's legal compendium.
items.works: Mukhtasar Khalil, Al-Tawdih fi Sharh al-Mukhtasar, Sharh al-Mudawwana al-Kubra

items.title: Ibn Farhun
items.fullName: Abū al-Wafāʾ Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Qāsim
items.description: Ibn Farhun was a leading Medinan Maliki jurist, judge, legal theorist, and biographer. Appointed qadi of Medina in 793 AH, he helped strengthen the Maliki school in the city through teaching, legal scholarship, and judicial service. His al-Dibaj al-Mudhahhab, a biographical dictionary of Maliki scholars, and Tabsirat al-Hukkam, a major treatise on judicial procedure, became enduring reference works in Maliki scholarship and Islamic judicial practice.
items.works: Al-Dibaj al-Mudhahhab fi Maʿrifat Aʿyan ʿUlamaʾ al-Madhhab, Tabsirat al-Hukkam, Durrat al-Ghawwas, Irshad al-Salik

items.title: Al-Hattab
items.fullName: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥaṭṭāb
items.description: Al-Hattab al-Ruʿayni was a leading Maliki jurist, legal theorist, grammarian, and scholar of hadith and Quranic interpretation. Born in Mecca to a family of Maghribi origin, he studied with prominent scholars of the Hijaz and travelled through Egypt and North Africa before settling in Tripoli. His Mawahib al-Jalil became one of the most authoritative commentaries on Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Jundi's Mukhtasar, while his other writings addressed legal commitments, Islamic legal theory, pilgrimage, and Arabic grammar. He helped shape the later Maliki scholarly tradition.
items.works: Mawahib al-Jalil li-Sharh Mukhtasar Khalil, Tahrir al-Kalam, Qurrat al-ʿAyn, Mutammimat al-Ajurrumiyya

items.title: Mahmud Shakir
items.fullName: Abū Fihr Maḥmūd ibn Muḥammad Shākir ibn Aḥmad
items.description: Mahmud Muhammad Shakir known as Abu Fahr, was an influential Egyptian literary scholar, poet, critic, and editor of classical Arabic texts. Renowned for his mastery of Arabic language and pre-Islamic poetry, he developed a distinctive method of literary criticism grounded in close reading and historical understanding. He made major contributions to the preservation and study of Arabic heritage through his editions of classical works and writings on literary history, Quranic eloquence, and Arab intellectual culture. His home became an important gathering place for generations of scholars and researchers.
items.works: Al-Mutanabbi, Abatil wa-Asmar, Namat Saʿb wa-Namat Mukhif, Qadiyyat al-Shiʿr al-Jahili,

items.title: Zirr ibn Hubaysh
items.fullName: Zirr ibn Hubaysh ibn Hubasha ibn Aws
items.description: Zirr ibn Hubaysh was a prominent Kufan Quran reciter, hadith transmitter, and linguist from the generation of the senior Tabi'un. A mukhadram who encountered several Companions, he studied Quranic recitation with Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. He became one of Kufa's leading authorities in Quranic readings, and his reading was transmitted through Asim ibn Abi al-Najud and Shu'ba ibn Ayyash. He was also renowned for his mastery of Arabic language and grammar.
items.works: No independently authored books or compilations.

items.title: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami
items.fullName: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb ibn Rabīʿa al-Sulamī al-Kūfī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān
items.description: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami was a prominent Kufan Quranic reciter, hadith transmitter, and leading authority of the generation of the Tabi'un. Born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, he studied Quranic recitation with several Companions and taught in the Great Mosque of Kufa for approximately forty years, beginning during the caliphate of Uthman.He was also renowned for his devotion to teaching and practicing the Quran.
items.works: No independently authored books or written compilations.

items.title: Asim ibn Abi al-Najud
items.fullName: ʿĀṣim Ibn Abī al-Najūd Abū Bakr al-Asadī al-Kūfī
items.description: Asim ibn Abi al-Najud was a leading Kufan Quranic reciter, grammarian, and one of the Seven Imams of the canonical Quranic readings.He inherited the principal Kufan traditions of Quranic recitation. His reading became one of the most influential in Islamic history, transmitted principally through Hafs ibn Sulayman and Shuʿba ibn Ayyash. He was renowned for his precision in recitation, eloquence, beautiful voice, and devotion to the Quran.
items.works: No independently authored books or written compilations.

items.title: Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani
items.fullName: Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ al-Makhzūmī al-Madanī
items.description: Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani was a leading Medinan Quranic reciter, hadith transmitter, and one of the Ten Imams of the canonical Quranic readings. A prominent authority of the Tabiʿun. He taught Quranic recitation in the Prophet's Mosque and became the foremost reading authority of Medina in his generation.
items.works: No independently authored books or written compilations.

items.title: Mujahid ibn Jabr
items.fullName: Abū al-Ḥajjāj Mujāhid ibn Jabr al-Makhzūmī al-Makkī
items.description: Mujahid ibn Jabr was a leading Makkan Quranic exegete, reciter, jurist, and hadith scholar of the Tabiʿun. He was among the most distinguished students of Abd Allah ibn Abbas, to whom he reportedly presented the entire Quran thirty times, questioning him about the circumstances and meanings of individual verses. His interpretations became one of the principal foundations of early transmitted Quranic exegesis and were extensively preserved by later commentators. He was particularly renowned for his mastery of tafsir, with Sufyan al-Thawri and Qatadah praising his exceptional authority in the field.
items.works: Tafsir Mujahid

items.title: Sa'id ibn Jubayr
items.fullName: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr ibn Hishām al-Asadī al-Wālibī al-Kūfī
items.description: Sa'id ibn Jubayr was a leading Kufan Quranic exegete, jurist, hadith scholar, and reciter of the generation of the Tabi'un. One of the foremost students of Abd Allah ibn Abbas, he became renowned for his mastery of Quranic interpretation, jurisprudence, and inheritance law. Ibn Abbas held his knowledge in such high regard that he referred visiting Kufans to him for religious questions. He participated in the revolt of Ibn al-Ash'ath against the Umayyads and was subsequently executed by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf.
items.works: No independently authored books or complete written compilations.
